title: kotile: GL test suite is flaky -- HeadlessGl boots one Lwjgl3Application per render (~60/JVM)
description:
PROVEN FLAKY, PRE-EXISTING. Evidence (2026-07-15):
- Commit 05b05fd7 (krogue-0y8): build run 29457944532 FAILED with 38 GL failures; re-run of the SAME commit -> SUCCESS.
- Commit 697b3bd7 (krogue-xcx, contains none of 0y8's code): originally SUCCESS; re-run 29456562020 -> FAILED with 40 GL failures.

So the failure is independent of the change under test. It is also load-dependent, not a fixed cap: the failure boundary MOVES between runs (05b05fd7 broke at RenderingIntegrationTest test 22; 697b3bd7 broke at test 14).

Shape of the failure: tests pass in file order up to some test N, then EVERY GL test from N onward fails -- including all GL tests in every later spec (RenderingLifecycleIntegrationTest, ViewportIntegrationTest, NpotTileSheetTest, TileSheetFilterTest, AsciiTileWindowSharedCanvasTest). All throw GdxRuntimeException at the HeadlessGl.render call site. Once GL breaks in that JVM it stays broken.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis, strong): HeadlessGl.render boots a brand-new Lwjgl3Application (and thus a new GLFW window + GL context) for EVERY render, then exits it. There are ~60 such boots per test JVM (39 in RenderingIntegrationTest alone). Under xvfb + llvmpipe on a shared CI runner, context creation eventually fails; after the first failure nothing recovers. Local macOS cannot reproduce (real GPU): 60 realistic boots -- sheet texture + canvas + renderer + composite-cache FBOs, with and without dispose -- all pass.

FIX: boot ONE Lwjgl3Application per JVM and reuse it across renders (post render work to it via Gdx.app.postRunnable + a latch, resizing the window per case since KotileCanvas reads Gdx.graphics.width/height). This removes ~60 GLFW/GL context creations, should kill the flake, and should speed the suite up.

Aggravating factor worth noting: several tests never dispose their renderer (e.g. maxEdgeBlend, the AnimatedSpriteTile tint tests), leaking GridCompositeCache FBOs per boot. Worth fixing alongside, though the reruns show leaks are not the trigger on their own.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: these tests only execute on Linux CI (xvfb); on macOS they are skipped because GLFW needs the first thread and Gradle test workers do not own it. To exercise GL locally on macOS use the JavaExec + -XstartOnFirstThread harness pattern in kotile/demo/build.gradle.kts (renderHarness/spriteHarness).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED + a second, subtler bug the fix exposed.

Run 1 of the one-app-per-JVM fix: 38 GdxRuntimeException failures -> 1 real assertion failure. The mass GL failure is gone, so the diagnosis (per-render Lwjgl3Application churn) was right.

The remaining failure was 'sprite tiles smooth at a fractional scale but stay crisp at an integer scale': integer-scale edge blend measured 0.50, expected 0.0. NOT a filter bug and NOT a bad assertion -- a STALE READ, and the test was right to catch it:

libGDX framebuffers DO NOT NEST. GLFrameBuffer.end() rebinds framebuffer 0 (the window's back buffer), not whatever FBO was bound before it. GridCompositeCache does fbo.begin()/fbo.end() per recomposite, so any render that goes through the composite cache finishes drawing on the WINDOW, not on HeadlessGl's capture FBO -- and Pixmap.createFromFrameBuffer captures whatever is currently bound, i.e. the window. When each render had its own application this was invisible (that back buffer was necessarily blank). With one shared, double-buffered application, it still holds an earlier frame, so the integer-scale pass captured leftover blended pixels from the fractional-scale pass that ran immediately before it.

Fix: clear framebuffer 0 as well as the capture FBO at the start of every render.

Worth knowing for anyone touching kotile rendering, independent of tests: a caller who wraps kotile rendering in their OWN FrameBuffer will have it silently unbound the first time the composite cache recomposites. That is a real (if niche) consumer-visible constraint and is currently undocumented -- consider filing it separately.
close_reason: Fixed and merged (PR #3). HeadlessGl now boots one Lwjgl3Application per JVM and reuses it, instead of one per render (~60/JVM). Validated 5/5 consecutive green against a ~50% flake (~3% by luck). The harness fix alone took 38 GdxRuntimeException failures -> 1 real assertion failure; that last one was a genuine bug it exposed (libGDX FBOs don't nest, so composite-cache rendering lands on the window's back buffer and the capture read stale frames) -- fixed by clearing framebuffer 0 too. Also disposed the 10 leaked SpriteTileRenderers and set testLogging.exceptionFormat=FULL. Consumer-facing FBO-unbind split out as krogue-s5h.

title: Built-in System constructors use inconsistent dependency-injection shapes
description: The public System constructors (systems/*.kt) each take their dependencies a different way, so a consumer instantiating the built-in pipeline faces an arbitrary grab-bag: (a) zone terrain arrives as either a bare Map<String,Zone> (MovementSystem, LightingSystem, RangedAttackSystem) OR the whole GameWorld (PortalSystem, PerceptionSystem) — no rule for which, even though GameWorld.zones is right there; (b) registry access is sometimes a decomposed (String)->T resolver lambda passed as gameModule.strategies::resolve / gameModule.calculators::resolve (BehaviorSystem, LightingSystem), sometimes nothing; (c) zone-scoped systems take a SEPARATE optional activeZones: (()->Set<String>)? provider that every caller fills with world::simulatedZones by hand (demo MyGame.kt:210-226) — yet the systems that already receive GameWorld could read simulatedZones() themselves. Result: no consistent convention for 'a system needs terrain / a registry / the active-zone policy', and the split (why does Movement get just the map but Portal gets the whole world?) is arbitrary. Normalizing on one shape (e.g. every zone-scoped system takes GameWorld and reads .zones/.simulatedZones itself; registries passed as Registry<T> not a bare lambda) is a source-breaking change to these public constructors — P1, do it before 1.0 locks them. Prerequisite for a clean default-pipeline helper (see the companion 'no engine-provided system pipeline' bead).
acceptance_criteria: The built-in systems share one documented injection convention for terrain, registry, and active-zone scope; a consumer can read one system's constructor and predict the others'. Signature normalization lands before 1.0.
close_reason: Landed together in one engine change (ADR-0032). cjv: built-in systems normalized onto GameWorld + Registry<T>, per-system activeZones removed (scope now the world's SimulatedZonePolicy); added public Registry.of factory. 32d: installStandardSystems + Staged/PipelineStage/StandardStage with World.tick() auto-validating order (PipelineOrderException). elm: PerceptionSystem moved to perception/. Demo uses installStandardSystems; Rogue port rewired by hand and its RogueCombatSystem/RoguePickupSystem declare COMBAT/PICKUP. 586 engine + 590 rogue tests green, both ktlint-clean.

title: Determinism contract is opt-in and silently violable: RNG-consuming API defaults to Random.Default
description: The engine's flagship guarantee (ADR-0009: seeded reproducible RNG via GameRandom's named xoshiro256** streams; 'same master seed => same world+loot'; exact save/resume) rests entirely on the caller threading a seeded stream through every randomness sink. But FOUR public entry points default the 'random' parameter to kotlin.random.Random.Default — a non-deterministic, non-serializable source: ecs/World.kt:180 (tick), world/GameWorld.kt:139 (Builder.zone), world/Zone.kt:76 and :132 (Zone.Builder / create). A consumer who omits the argument — or a new strategy/system that reaches for Random.Default directly — gets non-reproducible gameplay and a save that will NOT resume identically, with zero error or warning. The footgun is known: BehaviorStrategy.kt:24's own KDoc literally warns 'draw from ctx.random ... never Random.Default', yet the default value stays. Only ONE call site in the whole codebase threads it correctly (demo MyGame.kt:285: world.ecs.tick(random = gameRandom.stream("gameplay"))); a consumer copying anything less gets silent nondeterminism. This is P1 because it sits directly on top of the central design guarantee and the fix is source-breaking (remove/repoint the default, or funnel all randomness through GameRandom so the seeded stream is non-optional) — cheap now, a breaking change post-1.0.
acceptance_criteria: No public API path can produce gameplay/worldgen randomness from an unseeded/non-serializable source by default; either the seeded stream is required (no dangerous default) or the default routes through GameRandom. A test proves two runs from the same master seed (including across a save/load) tick identically without the caller having to remember to pass an RNG.
close_reason:
Fixed via ADR-0025: the world now owns its GameRandom. World(random: GameRandom = GameRandom.random()); World.tick() lost its random parameter entirely and draws TickContext.random from the world's GameRandom.GAMEPLAY stream; GameWorld.Builder/create thread the master seed and default zone() to the WORLDGEN stream; Zone.Builder/create keep an explicit random but now REQUIRED (no Random.Default default); SaveCodec.save() reads world.random instead of taking it as a separate arg (a mismatched world/RNG pair is now unrepresentable). New World.tickContext() replaces the TickContext(random=Random.Default) priming hack both consumers had independently hand-rolled. All four Random.Default entry points named in the bead are gone.

Acceptance criteria met: engine/src/test/.../random/DeterminismTest.kt proves same-seed replay of worldgen + 20 ticks, divergence on a different seed (non-vacuity guard), and exact save/load resume (10 ticks + save + load + 10 ticks == 20 straight) — none of it passing an RNG anywhere.

Also fixed a latent bug in korogue-rogue this surfaced: LevelFactory built its world with GameWorld.create { } while RogueGame held the real GameRandom beside it — two RNG roots for one game. Migrated korogue-rogue in the same pass (Dungeon lost its worldgen ctor param; Dungeon.begin takes one GameRandom instead of two streams). korogue 788 tests + rogue 585 tests green; ktlint clean (korogue); rogue lint debt is pre-existing, filed as rogue-fom.

title: Test: composite cache reveals lower z-layer when the top layer at a cell is removed (per-cell z-compositing across frames)
description: Within GridCompositeCache the per-cell draw callback re-composites every populated layer bottom-up (layersBottomUp) into that cell. LayeredTilemapTest verifies 'removing the top cell exposes the cell beneath' at the data level, and RenderingIntegrationTest verifies free-layer painter's order via LayerStack — but nothing verifies the two together THROUGH the cache: on a persistent renderer, draw a cell with two stacked layers (opaque top over a differently-colored bottom), render, then removeCell the TOP layer and re-render. The cell must recomposite to show the BOTTOM layer's color, not stay showing the removed top layer's stale pixels. This is a distinct code path from the single-layer clearTile guard (krogue-drk): it depends on the removeCell version bump reaching the tracker AND the cell being fully cleared before the surviving lower layer is redrawn. Plausible silent-in-1.0 bug: if the cell were redrawn without a clear, the removed top layer's pixels would persist under a transparent lower layer, or z-order could invert. GL-gated pixel assertion.
close_reason: Added a GL-gated test to RenderingIntegrationTest.kt: two stacked z-layers at one cell (opaque red top over blue bottom) on a persistent window; removing the top layer and re-rendering must recomposite to reveal the bottom layer's color, not retain the removed layer's stale cached pixels. Same macOS local-skip caveat as krogue-flj applies.

title: Test: ViewportDirtyTracker cross-frame scroll-invalidation and shared-source animated cells on a persistent renderer
description: ViewportDirtyTracker (the render(source,viewport) poll-based path, krogue-c0q) has no test that reuses ONE renderer across frames while the viewport moves or an animated tile is present. Existing ViewportIntegrationTest 'krogue-c0q' cases for shared-source do reuse a renderer for a plain write, but the scroll case ('tile visible only after scrolling') uses two SEPARATE HeadlessGl windows, so the tracker's own viewportChanged->markAllDirty branch and its lastVersions/-1 resize sentinel are never exercised across the persistent cache. Two untested cross-frame scenarios, both matching the 'wrong on the Nth paint' shape: (1) render a shared LayeredTilemap through one persistent window at origin (0,0), then re-render at a scrolled origin — the newly-revealed column must paint and the scrolled-off content must not linger from the cache; (2) place an AnimatedAsciiTile/AnimatedSpriteTile in the shared source and render the SAME window on two frames with NO write between them but advancing the animation clock — isAnimatedAt must force that cell dirty each frame so the animation doesn't freeze on the first-painted frame (the exact krogue-asz symptom, but on the shared-source path instead of the internal-tilemap path that krogue-drk already guards). GL-gated pixel assertions.
close_reason: Added two GL-gated tests to ViewportIntegrationTest.kt: (1) scroll invalidation on a persistent (reused) window across two render(source, viewport) calls, verifying the newly-revealed column paints and scrolled-off content doesn't linger; (2) an AnimatedAsciiTile on a shared source rendered by the same window across two frames with no writes between, verifying isAnimatedAt keeps it animating. Note: GL tests self-skip on macOS (no DISPLAY) per docs/STATUS.md -- compiled and confirmed skipping cleanly locally; correctness verified by hand-tracing ViewportDirtyTracker/GridCompositeCache and will be exercised by CI's Linux Mesa llvmpipe run.

title: Test: GridCompositeCache partial-dirty path preserves untouched cells across frames on a persistent renderer
description: The whole reason GridCompositeCache exists is the partial-dirty steady state: on frame N only the cells that changed are scissored/cleared/redrawn while every un-marked cell keeps its existing pixels. The krogue-drk RenderingIntegrationTest cases cover clearTile (one cell) and 'identical output when NOTHING changed', but nothing exercises the mixed case: on a multi-cell grid, change exactly ONE non-background cell on frame N and assert BOTH (a) that cell now shows the new content AND (b) an adjacent, unchanged, non-background cell still shows its own prior content — verifying the per-cell glScissor+glClear in recompositeIfDirty's partial branch doesn't bleed into or wipe neighbors, and the required per-cell batch.flush() lands under the right scissor rect. Must reuse ONE persistent TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow instance across the two renders (not a fresh HeadlessGl window per frame, which only ever hits the fully-dirty first-paint path). GL-gated pixel-assertion test alongside the existing krogue-drk suite. Depends on the same failure shape as krogue-asz.
close_reason: Added a GL-gated test to RenderingIntegrationTest.kt: on a persistent window, changing one cell on a multi-cell grid and re-rendering must update only that cell's pixels while an adjacent, unchanged, non-background cell keeps its own prior content -- verifies the per-cell glScissor+glClear in recompositeIfDirty's partial-dirty branch doesn't bleed into neighbors. Same macOS local-skip caveat as krogue-flj applies; reasoned through the scissor/flush code path by hand.

title: TileRenderer vs AsciiTileWindow: parallel render paths have drifted (naming + missing methods)
description:
kotile's two documented parallel rendering paths — rendering/TileRenderer.kt (sprite) and display/ascii/AsciiTileWindow.kt (ascii) — have diverged in both naming and capability. They should stay in sync (ARCHITECTURE/kotile docs treat them as siblings).

Naming divergence (breaking to fix post-1.0):
- Grid dimensions in tiles: TileRenderer exposes windowWidth/windowHeight; AsciiTileWindow exposes widthInTiles/heightInTiles. Same concept, different names.
- Resize entry point: TileRenderer.onResize(w,h) vs AsciiTileWindow.resize(w,h).
- Construction: TileRenderer is an abstract class subclassed with regionFor(); AsciiTileWindow uses a private ctor + create{}/createWithCanvas{} DSL factory. (Arguably principled, but the two entry points feel unrelated.)

Capability gaps on TileRenderer that AsciiTileWindow has:
- No clear() (clear all cells/layers), no clearLayer(z), no fill(...). TileRenderer only offers drawTile/clearTile per cell.
- No query method; AsciiTileWindow has topDescriptorAt(x,y)/(pos). 
- AsciiTileWindow has a z-defaulted drawTile(x,y,tile); TileRenderer requires drawTile(x,y,z,tile) always.

Why it matters for 1.0: windowWidth/heightInTiles/onResize/resize are baked into the public API of com.sletmoe:kotile; renaming for parity is a breaking change after release. The missing clear/fill/query methods are additive (safe to add later) but should be decided now so the sibling APIs read as one system. Prioritize aligning the names pre-1.0.
close_reason: Aligned TileRenderer to AsciiTileWindow's vocabulary (ADR-0028). Renamed windowWidth/windowHeight->widthInTiles/heightInTiles and onResize->resize; collapsed the split drawTile overloads to one sealed SpriteTile param; added clear/clearLayer/fill/topTileAt/z-defaulted drawTile+clearTile and tileWidthPx/tileHeightPx/layout. Parity now enforced by RenderPathParityTest (reflective, no GL needed) rather than by convention. Compositing-policy asymmetry split out as krogue-8mr.

title: Test: LayeredTilemap.versionAt bump semantics (composite-cache dirty backbone)
description: LayeredTilemap.versionAt is the sole signal the whole dirty-region composite cache (GridCompositeCache + ViewportDirtyTracker, ADR-0024) relies on to know a cell changed, yet LayeredTilemapTest has ZERO direct tests of it (grep: versionAt appears in main, never in tests). Every mutation path must monotonically bump the cell's version: setCell, removeCell, moveCell (both from AND to cells), clearLayer, clearAllLayers. If any path forgets to bump (e.g. moveCell not versioning both endpoints, or clearLayer only versioning occupied cells), a stale cache cell survives silently — exactly the krogue-asz 'looks fine, wrong on the Nth paint' shape. A good test asserts: (a) unwritten cell reads version 0; (b) each mutating call strictly increases the version at every affected coordinate; (c) a no-op (removeCell/clearLayer on an absent layer) does NOT change any version; (d) versions are unique-enough that a consumer's last-seen comparison detects the change. Pure unit test, no GL needed.
close_reason: Added versionAt tests to LayeredTilemapTest.kt covering: unwritten=0, monotonic bump on setCell/removeCell/moveCell(both endpoints)/clearLayer/clearAllLayers, no-op absent-layer cases not bumping, and global uniqueness. Found and fixed a real bug while writing these: removeCell(x,y,z) was bumping the version unconditionally even when layer z didn't exist (unlike clearLayer, which already correctly guarded this a few lines below) -- a spurious dirty signal that would cause unnecessary cache redraws. Fixed in LayeredTilemap.kt.

title: Two divergent Grid<T> types (kotile.utilities.Grid vs korogue.utilities.Grid)
description:
Both :kotile:library and :engine publish a public class named Grid<T>:
- kotile/library/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/kotile/utilities/Grid.kt — single row-major Array backing; API: get/set[x,y], fill, clear, forEachIndexed((Int,Int,T)); throws IndexOutOfBoundsException.
- engine/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/korogue/utilities/Grid.kt — MutableList<MutableList<T>> backing; API: get/set[x,y] AND [Vector2Int], fill (no clear), forEach, forEachIndexed((Vector2Int,T)), forEachCoordinate, forEachCoordinateInRadius, lastColumnIndex/lastRowIndex, companion of(); throws raw RuntimeException.

Same name, two packages, incompatible method sets, incompatible forEachIndexed signatures, different exception types, different perf characteristics. The engine's Grid leaks into the published save API: SaveCodec.save(fog=) and LoadedGame.fog expose Map<String, korogue.utilities.Grid<Boolean>>. A consumer importing both libraries has two 'Grid' symbols to disambiguate.

Why it matters for 1.0: Grid is a public type in both semver surfaces. Consolidating (engine reuses kotile's Grid, since kotile is the lower/general layer per the boundary principle in ARCHITECTURE.md) or renaming is a breaking change after 1.0. The engine Grid's list-of-lists backing and RuntimeException are also weaker than kotile's. Decide the single canonical Grid now.
notes:
Resolved by ADR-0026 (docs/adr/0026-single-canonical-grid.md). kotile's Grid is canonical; engine Grid deleted. Vector2Int accessors, forEach, forEachCoordinate, lastColumnIndex/lastRowIndex, and copy() (replacing the Grid.of companion) moved onto kotile's Grid. forEachIndexed((Vector2Int,T)) dropped — zero call sites in either repo. forEachCoordinateInRadius + Grid<Boolean>.or stayed in the engine as extensions on kotile's Grid (they need IntRect/distanceSq, which are above kotile's boundary).

Exemplary-consumer check: the Rogue port needed import-only changes across 20 files (20 insertions, 20 deletions, all the same line) and its 585 tests pass unchanged — evidence the merged API is a true superset in practice.

Side effects: partially resolves krogue-fuz for Grid (raw RuntimeException -> IndexOutOfBoundsException, a narrowing, so existing catches hold). Zero-sized grids are now legal and copyable; Grid.of used to reject them. The x/y-vs-Vector2Int duality is deliberately preserved — that is krogue-dat's call, not this one.

Tests: 569 engine + 227 kotile + 585 rogue = 1381, zero failures. Grid<Boolean>.or previously had no coverage at all; it now has four cases (GridExtensionsTest).
close_reason: kotile's Grid is now the single canonical grid type; engine Grid deleted. See ADR-0026.

title: krogue-drk composite cache: stale content survives clearTile / animation freezes across no-write renders
description:
Commit 1f959f9a ('krogue-drk: per-cell grid composite cache to skip full-grid repaint') was shipped to mainline without the pixel-assertion GL suite actually passing — its own commit message says it was verified via live-demo pixel diffing 'rather than this repo's pixel-assertion GL suite, which can't run reliably on this machine.' Now that krogue-0k1 wires Xvfb into CI, the suite runs and 3 of its own regression-guard tests fail:

- RenderingIntegrationTest.kt:695 'krogue-drk: AsciiTileWindow's composite cache reflects a clearTile, not stale content' — expected red channel 0.0, got 1.0 (fully red) after clearTile.
- RenderingIntegrationTest.kt:768 'krogue-drk: SpriteTileRenderer's composite cache reflects a clearTile, not stale content' — same pattern (expected 0.0, got 1.0).
- RenderingIntegrationTest.kt:801 'krogue-drk: TileRenderer keeps an AnimatedSpriteTile animating across renders with no writes between them' — expected green 1.0 (frame 1 color), got 0.298 (still showing frame 0's sheet color); the animation froze on the first-painted frame.

Note the AsciiTileWindow-side sibling tests for the 'no writes between renders' cases (line 699, 718) DO pass — the bug appears isolated to the SpriteTileRenderer/TileRenderer side of the cache (GridCompositeCache as used by the sprite path), not the AsciiTileWindow path, except clearTile is broken on both paths.

See PR https://github.com/ksletmoe/korogue/pull/1 for the CI run that surfaced this. docs/adr/0024-dirty-region-redraw-grid-composite-cache.md has the design.
acceptance_criteria: All RenderingIntegrationTest 'krogue-drk' tests pass under CI (Xvfb + llvmpipe), including the clearTile-recomposite and animation-without-writes cases for both AsciiTileWindow and SpriteTileRenderer/TileRenderer paths.
close_reason: Fixed: added BlendMode.REPLACE for the GridCompositeCache->canvas blit (was alpha-blending, so cleared/transparent cache cells never erased stale canvas pixels). Also fixed two mis-asserting tests unrelated to the cache bug. Verified green on PR #1, runs 29395109053/29395109017 (kotile:library:test actually executed and passed, not skipped).

title: kotile: establish provenance/license for the bundled cp437_10x10.png
description: The bundled library font kotile/library/src/main/resources/cp437_10x10.png has no provenance or license note in-repo (unlike vaarn-8x8.license.txt and the new cp437_12x12.license.txt). Kyle likes this sheet and wants to keep it, but its source font is unknown ('I really wish I knew where I got it'). Before the Sonatype 1.0.0 publish (krogue-5-sonatype), we must either (a) identify its source and confirm a redistributable license + add a cp437_10x10.license.txt note, or (b) if provenance can't be established, replace it with a known-licensed sheet (e.g. the CC0 Modern DOS downscale generated for krogue-kotile-font12, accepting slightly softer glyphs). Do NOT ship an unprovenanced font asset in the published JAR.
design: RESOLVED (provenance found 2026-07-19): cp437_10x10.png is pixel-identical (ImageMagick AE=0; normalized content sha 19f9090404...) to AsciiPanel's cp437_10x10.png (github.com/trystan/AsciiPanel), one of AsciiPanel's own 'system fonts'. Kyle re-exported it on macOS (Apple 'Generic RGB Profile' ICC chunk + 2026-06-10 date = the re-export, not the source). AsciiPanel is MIT (Copyright 2015 Trystan Spangler) — redistributable in the published JAR provided the MIT copyright+permission notice is included. So: KEEP the font, add cp437_10x10.license.txt crediting AsciiPanel/Trystan under MIT (mirroring vaarn-8x8/cp437_12x12 notes). Minor residual: AsciiPanel presents these CP437 bitmaps as its own under MIT; no evidence of an earlier upstream, treat as MIT.

title: Tiled import: loader/registry wiring, docs, and worked example
description: Capstone: wire the import entry points into the public API/loader story (keep IO at the edge; consider a GameModule hook so tile/object mappings resolve save-load-aware like other registries), document the authoring workflow (what standard properties the engine reads, how to declare the consumer mapping, how to mark 9-slice regions and variant families), and add a worked example: a hand-authored .tmj imported as a Zone AND a .tmj/template imported as a variably-sized Prefab, used by the demo or the Rogue example (ADR-0012 'engine capability surfaced by the example' pattern). Update docs/STATUS.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as needed.

title: Tiled import: variably-sizeable prefabs (9-slice + variant families)
description:
Make imported prefabs variably sizeable, BOTH ways the user asked for:
(a) 9-slice / edge+fill — author a border + a repeatable interior region (via Tiled layers/properties marking corners/edges/fill); the importer tiles the interior to reach a requested WxH. Clean for rectangular rooms; define minimum size and how doors/anchors reposition as it grows.
(b) Variant families — group several authored fixed-size Prefabs under one logical id; a generator/placer requests a size (or size range) and the importer picks a fitting variant (RNG-seeded, faithful/deterministic).
Builds on the fixed-size Prefab import. Acceptance: stamp the same logical prefab at multiple sizes into a zone with no overlap (exercises importer + resize/variant selection + PrefabPlacer). Headless-testable.

title: Tiled import: map/template -> Prefab, fixed-size (use case 2 core)
description: Import a Tiled map (or object template) as a Prefab — the existing ADR-0019 primitive. Tiles -> Prefab.tiles (unpainted/blank cells left transparent so non-rectangular rooms work, matching the ASCII builder); object-layer objects -> EntityPlacements (offset + mapped components) via the semantics seam; named/typed objects or properties -> doors (with Direction) and anchors. Fixed-size path first (a single authored footprint). Produces a normal Prefab that stamps through the existing Prefab.stamp + PrefabPlacer, so generators can place Tiled-authored rooms with no other changes. Headless-testable.

title: Tiled import: non-procedural tilemap -> Zone (use case 1)
description: Load a whole Tiled map as a Zone. Terrain layer(s) -> the Zone's Grid<Tile> via the semantics seam; object layer(s) -> buffered entity spawns (Position + ZoneMember + mapped components), materialized after build exactly like ADR-0019 generation (GameWorld materializes buffered spawns; generation/import stays World-free and pure). Define multi-layer compositing (top-layer-wins vs explicit terrain-vs-object layers) and out-of-bounds/size handling (the map's width/height sets the Zone dimensions). Wire an entry point into GameWorld.Builder / Zone.Builder (e.g. a fromTiled(...) source) alongside the existing procedural zone(...) path. Headless-testable end to end (no GL).

title: Tiled import: tile & object semantics seam (consumer mapping + standard props)
description: The game-agnostic mapping layer between the neutral Tiled model and engine types. Read a small set of STANDARD Tiled custom properties into Tile semantics (e.g. walkable, glyph, blocksLineOfSight, blocks/movement modes, description) and expose a CONSUMER HOOK: tileset tile-id -> Tile, and object 'class' + properties -> List<Component>. Mirrors the ADR-0014 registry/module seam so the engine stays game-agnostic and the Rogue example supplies its own tiles/components. Define precedence when both a standard property and a consumer mapping apply, and behavior for unmapped ids/classes (fail loudly vs skip, per the engine's existing 'reject, don't silently hole' stance in Prefab).

title: Tiled import: headless parse -> neutral map model (.tmj first)
description:
Foundation for the epic. Parse a Tiled map into an engine-neutral, texture-free intermediate model (layers; tile cells with gids/flip flags; object-layer objects with class + properties; tilesets with per-tile properties; map/layer custom properties). MUST stay headless and pure (no GL, no image/texture loading) so downstream Zone/Prefab extraction is unit-testable without a GL context, per ADR-0019.

Decide (see the ADR child): reuse gdx-core's com.badlogic.gdx.maps.tiled Base* structural loaders subclassed to skip texture resolution, vs a lightweight kotlinx.serialization parse of .tmj (JSON). Target .tmj first; keep .tmx reachable through the same neutral model. IO stays at the edge (parse takes a string/stream), not baked into the pure parse.

title: ADR: Tiled import — structure-only, semantics seam, parse approach, variable-size
description:
Record the keystone decisions for Tiled import (copy docs/adr/template.md; link it back to this bead and the epic krogue-62h). Points to capture:
- Import STRUCTURE + SEMANTICS only; the engine renders its own CP437 glyphs, not Tiled's images.
- Semantics seam = consumer mapping + standard Tiled custom properties (tileset id -> Tile, object class/props -> components).
- Parse approach: reuse gdx-core's gdx-maps Base* structural loaders (texture-free) vs a lightweight kotlinx .tmj parse into a neutral model — chosen to keep the parse + extraction fully headless/pure per ADR-0019. Records why the stock gdx TmxMapLoader/TmjMapLoader (GL/texture-coupled) are NOT used as-is.
- Variable-size prefabs: support both 9-slice/edge+fill resizing and authored fixed-size variant families; why true arbitrary stretching of hand-authored art is out.
- Relationship to ADR-0019 (feeds the existing Prefab + buffered-spawn model) and ADR-0014 (registry/consumer-hook seam pattern).

title: Engine: Tiled (mapeditor.org) map + prefab import
description:
Add support for authoring content in Tiled (https://doc.mapeditor.org/) and importing it into the engine, for two consumer use cases:

1. NON-PROCEDURAL TILEMAPS — load a whole hand-authored map as a Zone: terrain layer(s) become the Zone's Grid<Tile>; object layer(s) become buffered entity spawns (monsters/items/traps/etc.), materialized after build the same way ADR-0019 generation does. A game can hand-place a fixed level instead of generating one.

2. PREFABS FOR PROCEDURAL WORLDS — import a Tiled map (or object template) as a Prefab (the existing ADR-0019 primitive: tiles + EntityPlacements + doors + anchors), so hand-authored rooms/structures can be stamped by generators/placers. Prefabs must be VARIABLY SIZEABLE: support BOTH (a) 9-slice / edge+fill resizing (author a border + a repeatable interior; the importer tiles the interior to reach a requested size — clean for rectangular rooms) AND (b) selecting among a family of authored fixed-size variants at gen time.

SCOPE / STANCE (decided with the user):
- Import STRUCTURE + SEMANTICS only, not Tiled's pixel/image tiles: the engine keeps rendering its own CP437 glyphs. A Tiled tile contributes which cell is wall/floor/etc. and its semantics, not an image.
- SEMANTICS SEAM = consumer mapping + standard properties: the engine reads a small set of standard Tiled custom properties (e.g. walkable, glyph, blocksLineOfSight, blocks, object 'class'), AND exposes a consumer hook mapping tileset tile-id -> Tile and object class/properties -> List<Component>. Keeps the importer game-agnostic (like the ADR-0014 registry seams).
- PARSING: libGDX ships a Tiled model + loaders in gdx-core (com.badlogic.gdx.maps.tiled: TmxMapLoader/TmjMapLoader + the Base* structural parsers), already on the classpath (gdx 1.14.1) — no new dependency. BUT the stock loaders resolve tileset images into GL textures (asset/GL-coupled), which conflicts with ADR-0019's rule that generation stays headless and pure, and with importing structure-only. So the foundation bead must decide: reuse gdx's Base* structural parse (texture-free) vs a lightweight kotlinx .tmj (JSON) parse into our own neutral model. Lean: whatever keeps the parse + Zone/Prefab extraction fully headless-testable (no GL); target .tmj (JSON) first, .tmx reachable through the same path.

Mirrors the ADR-0019/krogue-b1p decomposition (layered, generation stays pure, all pieces headless-testable). Warrants an ADR (see the decision child). Faithful Rogue behavior is unaffected — this is a general engine capability the Rogue example (and demo) can adopt.

title: kotile: GridCompositeCache REPLACE blit erases neighbor panes on a shared canvas
description:
Bisected regression (first bad commit 3bff9b4f1, krogue-asz). That commit switched the GridCompositeCache->canvas blit from NORMAL (alpha) to BlendMode.REPLACE (GL_ONE/GL_ZERO) so a cleared cell (transparent in the cache) erases its own stale pixel instead of alpha-compositing over it. Correct for a window that owns its whole canvas region — but on a SHARED canvas with multiple panes (AsciiTileWindow + SpriteTileRenderers via createWithCanvas), the window blits its full contentWidth x contentHeight rect with REPLACE, and cells it never populated are transparent in the cache. REPLACE writes those transparent pixels over whatever a neighboring pane drew earlier that frame, erasing it.

Concrete repro: the animation showcase (demo/AnimationShowcaseHarness) is a full-width (TOTAL_COLS=50) AsciiTileWindow sharing one canvas with sprite renderers that draw the left half (cols 0-24). Since krogue-asz, asciiWindow.render()'s REPLACE blit erases the entire sprite (left) half every frame -> it renders blank. Proven via the PNG snapshot task + a left-half pixel check: SPRITES (66.7% content) at the harness birth commit b47560553, BLANK (0%) from 3bff9b4f1 onward through mainline HEAD.

Not caused by krogue-2co; discovered while validating the krogue-2co demo change (which is byte-identical output and unrelated).

Likely fix directions (needs design): (a) blit only the populated bounding box region rather than the full window rect; (b) let a shared-canvas pane declare its owned sub-region so REPLACE is confined to it; (c) document that a full-width fixed-grid window can't share a canvas with other panes and reshape the demo. Fix is verifiable on macOS via the snapshot + spritecheck even though the GL assertion suite is Linux-only.
close_reason: Fixed via sharesCanvas flag (SpriteTileRenderer/TileRenderer + AsciiTileWindowConfig) blitting the composite with NORMAL instead of REPLACE for shared-canvas panes; demo wired to use it. Verified: showcase snapshot sprite half restored to 66.1% content (was 0%), visually correct on both halves. GL regression test added to AsciiTileWindowSharedCanvasTest (Linux/Xvfb-gated). Default REPLACE unchanged for single-owner windows.

title: kotile: rendering silently unbinds a caller's FrameBuffer (composite cache's fbo.end() rebinds framebuffer 0)
description:
libGDX framebuffers do not nest: GLFrameBuffer.end() rebinds framebuffer 0 (the window's back buffer), not whatever FBO happened to be bound before begin(). GridCompositeCache does fbo.begin()/fbo.end() on every recomposite (see recompositeIfDirty), so the FIRST time a TileRenderer or AsciiTileWindow recomposites, any FrameBuffer the CONSUMER had bound is silently dropped and all subsequent drawing lands on the window instead.

A consumer doing the reasonable thing -- wrapping kotile rendering in their own FBO to post-process the frame, render the map to a texture, do a screen transition, capture a screenshot -- will find their FBO empty and their content on screen instead, with no error. That is a real consumer-visible constraint on the 1.0 API and it is currently undocumented.

Found via krogue-8lo: kotile's OWN test harness hit exactly this. HeadlessGl renders into a capture FBO, and every composite-cache test was silently being captured from the window's back buffer rather than that FBO. It only went unnoticed because each render used to get a fresh application whose back buffer was blank, so the stale read was always blank-then-correct. Sharing one application exposed it as a real failure.

Options: (a) save/restore the previously bound framebuffer around the cache's begin/end (query GL_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING before begin, rebind after end) so kotile composes transparently inside a caller's FBO; or (b) accept it and document loudly on TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow/GridCompositeCache that rendering must not be wrapped in a consumer FBO. (a) is the better 1.0 behaviour and is not much code.

Note libGDX's own FrameBuffer has this flaw by design, so (a) means kotile doing the save/restore itself rather than relying on the framework.
notes: Surfaced by krogue-8lo. Pre-1.0 relevance: if the answer is (a), that is a behaviour change worth landing before release; if (b), it is a doc change on the public API. Either way decide before 1.0 rather than after.
close_reason: Fixed (PR #6). GridCompositeCache now wraps both the FrameBuffer allocation and the draw pass in preservingFrameBuffer{}, snapshotting GL_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING + GL_VIEWPORT and restoring them, so kotile composes transparently inside a consumer's own FBO. Chose option (a) from the issue -- the better 1.0 behaviour -- and documented it as a supported guarantee on TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow. Key finding: libGDX steals the binding in TWO places, not one -- FrameBuffer.end() binds 0, AND the FrameBuffer CONSTRUCTOR leaves 0 bound, so the theft happened on the first render inside ensureSize, before the draw pass ran. Fixing only recompositeIfDirty did nothing; found by measuring rather than assuming. Pinned by a pixel test proven to fail without the fix (caller's FBO reads back empty, binding returns 0).

title: No engine-provided system pipeline: every consumer hand-wires the built-in systems in a correctness-critical order
description: GameModule is documented as 'the single seam describing a game's pluggable pieces' but it bundles only the REGISTRIES (strategies/calculators/senses/effects/generators/components) — it knows nothing about SYSTEMS. So the built-in simulation pipeline is entirely hand-assembled by every consumer: construct each system with the right registry slice + zones + activeZones provider, then addSystem them in a specific order where mistakes are SILENT correctness bugs. The demo's registerSystems() (MyGame.kt:208-226) is the only reference, and the order is load-bearing: PerceptionSystem must run AFTER LightingSystem (comment at :211-213 explains why — it reads the freshly-written lightMap), MovementSystem after BehaviorSystem (consumes its MoveIntents), CombatSystem after MovementSystem (consumes AttackIntents), etc. Nothing enforces or documents this ordering as API; a consumer who registers perception before lighting gets stale visibility with no error. GameModule.engineDefaults() pre-loads built-in *registries* but there is no engineDefaults()-equivalent that installs the standard *systems* on a World in the correct order wired to a given module. For a 'reusable, extensible game engine', the very first thing every consumer must do is re-derive this load-bearing wiring from the demo. Fix is purely additive (a helper like GameModule/World.installStandardSystems(gameWorld, module) that registers the built-ins in the correct order, letting consumers add/replace/reorder from a known-good baseline) so it's non-breaking = P2, but it's the highest-value ergonomic gap for 1.0. Best built on normalized system constructors (see companion 'inconsistent System DI shapes' P1 bead).
acceptance_criteria: A consumer can stand up the standard simulation pipeline in the correct order from a GameModule with one documented call (then customize), instead of hand-copying the demo's registerSystems(). The required inter-system ordering constraints are documented as part of that API.
close_reason: Landed together in one engine change (ADR-0032). cjv: built-in systems normalized onto GameWorld + Registry<T>, per-system activeZones removed (scope now the world's SimulatedZonePolicy); added public Registry.of factory. 32d: installStandardSystems + Staged/PipelineStage/StandardStage with World.tick() auto-validating order (PipelineOrderException). elm: PerceptionSystem moved to perception/. Demo uses installStandardSystems; Rogue port rewired by hand and its RogueCombatSystem/RoguePickupSystem declare COMBAT/PICKUP. 586 engine + 590 rogue tests green, both ktlint-clean.

title: Package com.sletmoe.korogue.kotile.* is a confusing home for engine classes
description:
engine/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/korogue/kotile/ holds korogue's own engine classes (Game.kt, ZoneFog.kt) under a package literally named 'kotile' — the name of the separate lower-level rendering library (com.sletmoe:kotile). A newcomer scanning imports will read com.sletmoe.korogue.kotile.Game as belonging to the tile-renderer, not the game engine. STATUS.md already notes this ('odd home for korogue's own classes (consider .rendering)') but there is no tracked bead.

Why it matters for 1.0: the package name is the import path and is part of the published API surface of com.sletmoe.korogue.korogue. Moving these classes to a clearer package (e.g. com.sletmoe.korogue.rendering) after 1.0 is a breaking change for every consumer's import. Rename before release. Also review overall package discoverability while here (entry points a newcomer reaches for: world/GameWorld, registry/GameModule, the Game loop).
close_reason: Moved Game -> com.sletmoe.korogue.app and ZoneFog -> com.sletmoe.korogue.perception; korogue.kotile package deleted. Chose a role-based split over the bead's proposed .rendering (Game is the app shell; ZoneFog is player knowledge that game logic mutates and SaveCodec persists, not a rendering class) -- rationale in ADR-0031. Demo + Rogue port updated in lockstep. Remaining discoverability debt from the review half filed as krogue-elm.

title: Inconsistent x/y Int pairs vs Vector2Int across the coordinate API (swap-prone)
description:
The public API has no consistent rule for expressing a 2D coordinate, mixing bare same-type Int pairs (easy to transpose, since Kotlin doesn't enforce named args at call sites) with the available Vector2Int value type:
- Components: Position(x,y) (but exposes a .point: Vector2Int getter), MoveIntent(dx,dy) (has a Direction ctor but no Vector2Int ctor), Portal(targetX,targetY).
- GameWorld: relocate(entityId, zoneId, x, y), entityAt(zoneId, x, y), isWalkable(zoneId, x, y) — all trailing (x:Int, y:Int).
- Grids: kotile Grid indexes by [x,y] only; engine Grid accepts both [x,y] and [Vector2Int].

So identical adjacent Int params (x,y / dx,dy / targetX,targetY) are transposition footguns, and a caller can't tell without checking each type whether a Vector2Int overload exists. Position offers .point one way but no Vector2Int constructor the other way.

Why it matters for 1.0: these are public constructors/method signatures in both semver surfaces. Adding Vector2Int overloads is additive, but making the convention consistent (e.g. every public coordinate accepts Vector2Int, with Int pairs as secondary overloads) is worth locking before callers proliferate. Reduces a whole class of silent x/y-swap bugs in downstream games.
notes: Resolved via ADR-0034 (docs/adr/0034-vector2int-canonical-coordinate.md): every public coordinate API now offers a Vector2Int form as the canonical one, Int pairs kept as secondary. Additive/non-breaking. Vector2Int gained plus/minus operators. Rogue port (../korogue-rogue) migrated to the canonical forms. Covered by ComponentsTest, GameWorldTest, and kotile Vector2IntTest.
close_reason: Coordinate API convention locked per ADR-0034; engine + kotile + Rogue port updated and tested.

title: Test: line-of-sight calculators (LineOfSightCalculator, OmnicientLineOfSightCalculator) have zero coverage
description: engine/algorithms/los has three implementations; only SymmetricShadowCaster is tested (SymmetricShadowCasterTest). The LineOfSightCalculator interface's other bundled implementations — the concrete Bresenham-style LineOfSightCalculator and OmnicientLineOfSightCalculator — have no direct tests, despite being public perception primitives a consumer selects between via the registry and the visibility model (ADR-0015). Good tests assert: OmnicientLineOfSightCalculator reports every in-bounds cell visible regardless of walls (its contract) and is symmetric; LineOfSightCalculator blocks correctly behind an opaque wall, sees an unobstructed target, is symmetric where the algorithm promises to be, and handles the degenerate cases (source==target, adjacent cells, target just past a wall corner, out-of-bounds/edge origin). Pure unit tests, no GL. Prevents a silently-broken visibility mode shipping in 1.0.
close_reason: Added OmnicientLineOfSightCalculatorTest (engine/src/test/.../los/) covering all-visible contract, wall-ignoring, maxViewDistance-ignoring, symmetry, and output dimensions. Note: the bead description referred to 'the concrete Bresenham-style LineOfSightCalculator' but no such class exists in algorithms/los -- only the LineOfSightCalculator interface, SymmetricShadowCaster (already tested), and OmnicientLineOfSightCalculator (now tested) exist. bresenhamLine in algorithms/geometry is a separate, unrelated utility (line-of-cells for projectiles, not a LOS calculator).

title: World mutation seam: inconsistent 'unknown id' contract; World.set silently drops writes
description:
The ECS mutation seam on ecs/World.kt handles a missing/despawned entity id three different ways:
- set(id, component): silently returns Unit (no-op) if id is unknown.
- update<T>(id){}: returns null if the entity or component is absent.
- remove<T>(id): returns null if absent.
- get(id): returns null. Meanwhile Entity.require and Registry.resolve throw.

The set() case is the sharp one: writing a component to a typo'd or already-despawned id vanishes with zero signal — a real footgun for consumers driving the world from input/AI code. GameWorld.relocate() delegates to two set() calls and inherits the same silent-drop. 

Why it matters for 1.0: the return type of set() (currently Unit) is part of the public signature; giving it a Boolean 'existed' result (or making update/set/remove uniform) is easier to do before callers exist. At minimum, document the divergent contract; ideally make the 'entity not found' outcome consistent across set/update/remove. Additive-leaning but signature-touching, so decide pre-release.
notes: Decision recorded as an amendment to docs/adr/0005-world-mutation-chokepoint.md (2026-07-18): the mutation seam signals absence and never silently drops; set returns Boolean; reified set<T> rejected (would key by caller's static type, storing an upcast value under Component). Keying stays concrete-runtime-class per ADR-0002.
close_reason: Made the ECS mutation seam signal absence uniformly: World.set now returns Boolean (true if the entity existed and the write applied, false — writing nothing — for an unknown/despawned id), so a typo'd or stale write is reported rather than silently dropped. GameWorld.relocate propagates the same Boolean. Unit->Boolean is source-compatible; the Rogue port (exemplary consumer) compiled and passed unchanged, and every one of its ~30 set() call sites targets a known-live entity — which validated returning a Boolean over throwing (throwing would force all of them to guard a liveness invariant they already hold). Kept set()'s concrete-runtime-class keying (ADR-0002) rather than making it reified set<T>: documented that a reified T would be the real footgun (an upcast 'val c: Component = Health(...)' would store under Component, unfindable by get<Health>()), so update/remove key by T while set keys by runtime class by design. Tests added in WorldTest (set returns true on apply, false for unknown id, false after despawn) and GameWorldTest (relocate true/false).

title: Test: rendering lifecycle edge cases (double-dispose, dispose-then-render, render-before-write, resize-during-use)
description: AsciiTileWindow, TileRenderer, SpriteTileRenderer and GridCompositeCache are the classes a 1.0 consumer drives directly, but their lifecycle/ordering edges are untested. Cases worth a test each: (a) double dispose() must not throw or double-free GPU resources (GridCompositeCache.disposeGpuResources nulls its FBO/batch — assert a second dispose is a clean no-op); (b) render/recomposite BEFORE any cell is written must produce a valid empty (clear-color) frame, not an NPE from a null frameBuffer/batch (recompositeIfDirty returns early on null — confirm the whole first-paint-with-no-content path is safe); (c) resize-during-use: change the window/grid tile dimensions between two renders on a persistent renderer and assert GridCompositeCache.ensureSize reallocates the FBO and forces a full redraw at the new size (including grow AND shrink, and a 1x1 grid), with no stale pixels from the old size; (d) the RenderingIntegrationTest:493 note says a window's shared canvas+font are intentionally NOT disposed by the window — add a guard test that disposing the window leaves a shared canvas still usable by a second window. Mix of GL-gated and plain unit tests.
close_reason: Added RenderingLifecycleIntegrationTest.kt covering all four cases: (a) double dispose() on AsciiTileWindow and SpriteTileRenderer is a clean no-op; (b) render() before any cell is written produces a valid clear-color frame, no NPE; (c) resize mid-use (grow x2, shrink, then a degenerate 1x1 grid) on a persistent window reallocates the cache and redraws correctly at each new size; (d) disposing one window sharing a canvas/font leaves it usable by a second window. Same macOS local-skip caveat as krogue-flj applies.

title: Public API throws raw RuntimeException for argument/state errors
description:
Several public entry points throw bare RuntimeException where a specific standard exception is expected, and the choice is inconsistent across the codebase:
- engine/utilities/Grid.kt checkBounds -> RuntimeException (but kotile/utilities/Grid.kt throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for the same out-of-bounds case).
- world/GameWorld.kt: invalid currentZoneId setter, removeZone of current zone, Builder.build() with no zones / no currentZoneId -> all RuntimeException (should be IllegalArgumentException / IllegalStateException).
- GameWorld.currentZone uses zones[currentZoneId]!! (raw NPE path) rather than a checked error.

Contrast with the parts that already do it well: Registry.resolve and Entity.require use error()/IllegalStateException; World.update/remove return null.

Why it matters for 1.0: throwing RuntimeException forces callers to catch the broad base type (or Throwable) to handle a bad zone id vs a genuine bug, and narrowing the thrown type later (to IllegalArgumentException etc.) is a behavioral/source-compatibility break for any code that catches. Standardize on IllegalArgumentException (bad caller input) / IllegalStateException (bad object state) / IndexOutOfBoundsException (indexing) before release. Low-effort, mostly mechanical.
close_reason: Standardized GameWorld public-API exception types: IllegalArgumentException for bad zone-id args (currentZoneId setter, removeZone of current), IllegalStateException for bad builder/object state (build with no zones/no currentZoneId, currentZone invariant). Grid.kt/checkBounds part of the issue was stale (that path is now bin/ cruft; kotile Grid already throws IndexOutOfBoundsException).

title: Parallel tile type hierarchies named inconsistently (sprite vs ascii)
description:
kotile has two parallel sealed tile hierarchies whose corresponding members are named on different schemes:

Sprite path (tiles/): SpriteTileEntry (sealed base) -> StaticTile (coordinate/static branch) + Tile (region-owning/animated branch); concrete AnimatedSpriteTile.
Ascii path (display/ascii/): AnimatableAsciiTile (sealed base) -> AsciiTileDescriptor (static branch) + AnimatedAsciiTile (animated branch).

Mismatches for the same roles:
- Sealed base: 'SpriteTileEntry' vs 'AnimatableAsciiTile' — one names the container, the other the animatability.
- Static branch: 'StaticTile' vs 'AsciiTileDescriptor' (Tile vs Descriptor).
- Animated branch: the sprite interface is just 'Tile' — the most generic possible name for the *animated* specialization, sitting under a base called SpriteTileEntry and beside a sibling StaticTile. It reads like a base type, and collides conceptually with the engine's own world.Tile (terrain). 

Why it matters for 1.0: these are all public types in com.sletmoe:kotile. A newcomer wiring both paths can't transfer intuition from one to the other, and bare 'Tile' meaning 'animated sprite tile' is a discoverability trap. Renaming (e.g. StaticSpriteTile/AnimatedSpriteTile interface + a consistent base naming) is a breaking change once published. Reconcile the two hierarchies' naming before release.
close_reason:
Both hierarchies reconciled onto one scheme (ADR-0027): sealed SpriteTile/AsciiTile bases -> Static{Sprite,Ascii}Tile + Dynamic{Sprite,Ascii}Tile branches -> Animated{Sprite,Ascii}Tile built-in impls. Bare 'Tile' (the discoverability trap, and the conceptual collision with engine world.Tile) is gone; AsciiTileDescriptor -> StaticAsciiTile, descriptorAt -> resolveAt, topDescriptorAt -> topTileAt.

Also closed the structural asymmetry: added the open DynamicAsciiTile branch so consumers can write custom time-driven ASCII cells, as they always could for sprites. That exposed a latent bug, now fixed: AsciiTileWindow keyed per-frame repaint on 'is AnimatedAsciiTile' (concrete class) rather than the branch, so a consumer's own dynamic tile would have painted once and frozen.

Verified: full ./gradlew build green (tests + ktlint) in korogue; korogue-rogue force-recompiled and its tests pass with zero changes — it imports only kotile's Vector2Int/Grid, so the engine's TileSurface hides the hierarchy entirely. Follow-up krogue-2co filed for TileSurface not exposing the dynamic branch.

title: Run GL-gated tests in GitHub Actions via Xvfb + Mesa llvmpipe
description:
Unit tests already run in CI (build.yml: ./gradlew build; pr.yml: ./gradlew check), but the
GL-gated integration tests in kotile:library (RenderingIntegrationTest, TileSheetFilterTest,
NpotTileSheetTest, ViewportIntegrationTest, etc.) self-skip because HeadlessGl.available checks
System.getenv("DISPLAY") and CI never sets it.

kotile/library/build.gradle.kts already anticipates this: the test task sets
LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe and has a comment saying to run under
`xvfb-run -a ./gradlew :library:test`. So the fix is CI-only, no test code changes:

- Install Xvfb on the ubuntu-latest runner (apt-get install -y xvfb, or an action like
  GabrielBB/xvfb-action / coactions/setup-xvfb).
- Wrap the Gradle invocation in build.yml and pr.yml with xvfb-run -a (or export DISPLAY from
  a long-running Xvfb service step) so LWJGL3's hidden window + Mesa llvmpipe software GL
  context can initialize headlessly.
- Verify the previously-skipped GL tests actually execute and pass (check the test report /
  test count, not just green CI) — a silent continued skip would defeat the point.
acceptance_criteria:
- build.yml and pr.yml run kotile:library tests under Xvfb with DISPLAY set.
- CI test output/report shows the GL-gated tests (HeadlessGl.available == true) executing and
  passing, not skipped.
- macOS-only concerns (NPOT glyph bug etc.) are irrelevant here since CI runs Linux; no change
  needed for the demo module's manual harnesses.
close_reason: PR #1 merged into mainline (f60c09ee0, now 855148ea after the unrelated author-history rewrite). Both build.yml and pr.yml run kotile:library:test under Xvfb+llvmpipe and it actually executes (194 tests, not silently skipped). Composite-cache regression it surfaced (krogue-asz) and the mis-asserting test (krogue-85j) both fixed and verified green.

Also filed krogue-85j for one unrelated pre-existing broken test assertion. This issue (krogue-0k1) can't fully close (tests green) until krogue-asz is fixed — the whole point was to have CI catch exactly this class of bug.

title: MapPanel flicker lookup: eliminate per-cell/per-frame List allocation
description:
MapPanel.flickerFactorAt does:

    flickerSources.filter { (origin, emitter) -> origin.distance(coord) <= emitter.radius }
        .minByOrNull { (origin, _) -> origin.distance(coord) }

This runs once per visible cell AND once per visible occupant, every single frame, as soon as any
LightEmitter in the zone has flicker set (krogue-ncl). filter{} allocates a fresh List on every
call. For a normal viewport (e.g. 80x25 = 2000 cells) with even a couple of flickering torches,
that's thousands of short-lived List allocations per frame purely to find "nearest in-range
flickering source" -- a linear scan that doesn't need an intermediate collection at all.

Separately (lower severity): flickerSourcesIn(zone) re-runs the ECS query + filter + map + toList
every draw() call (once per frame, not per cell -- so O(emitters), not O(cells x emitters)). Much
cheaper than the above but still redone every frame even when nothing changed.

Found during a design/efficiency review of the animation + animated-lighting work (krogue-ncl,
krogue-wuq, krogue-tnf, krogue-2ua) at the user's request.
acceptance_criteria: flickerFactorAt allocates no List/collection per call. Existing MapPanelTest flicker cases and LightFlickerTest stay green; behavior (which source wins, the returned factor) is unchanged for every existing test case.
close_reason: Rewrote flickerFactorAt's filter{}.minByOrNull{} as a manual loop, no per-cell List allocation. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: engine/demo: on-demand rendering to cut idle CPU (turn-based games)
description: libGDX renders every frame at vsync even when nothing changed, so a static roguelike view pegs a CPU core for no reason (this is frame COUNT, distinct from per-frame draw cost in krogue-drk). Add opt-in on-demand rendering: Gdx.graphics.setContinuousRendering(false) at startup, then Gdx.graphics.requestRendering() on input and while any animation/effect is active. For a turn-based game the view then costs ~0% CPU until the next keypress. Engine should expose a clean hook so games/host loops can request a redraw (tie into the TurnBasedLoop / animation-queue seams); the demo (MyGame) should adopt it. Note: NOT a GPU/software-rendering issue — GL is already hardware (AMD radeonsi confirmed); this is purely about not redrawing an unchanged frame. Complements krogue-drk (dirty-region redraw).
close_reason: Game (engine/kotile) gained a continuousRendering constructor flag: false calls Gdx.graphics.setContinuousRendering(false), wires requestRedraw() into every key press automatically, and exposes protected requestRedraw()/needsContinuousRedraw() hooks for a subclass to request extra frames (e.g. while a presentation animation plays). MyGame opts in when turnBased (continuousRendering = !turnBased) and overrides needsContinuousRedraw() with animationQueue.isPlaying. Default (true) preserves prior behavior exactly, so RealTimeLoop games are unaffected. Verified empirically: idle CPU sampled at 0.4-0.8% with the demo sitting idle, vs. a vsync-pegged core before.

title: MovementSystem occupancy is a hardcoded Portal/Item denylist — no generic per-entity walkability signal
description:
MovementSystem.occupantAt decides what blocks movement (and what a step bumps into -> AttackIntent) with a hardcoded denylist: every positioned entity (Position + ZoneMember) is treated as an attackable occupant EXCEPT those carrying Portal or Item. This does not scale: any game that models a non-creature as a positioned entity — traps, secret doors, altars, pressure plates, decorations, remembered corpses — silently turns it into an invisible attackable wall until it is added to the skip-list. It is untested for that case (the engine demo only has creatures + portals + items).

Found via korogue-rogue (rogue-291): Rogue keeps traps and secret doors/passages as ECS entities (the type/flags ride on an entity because korogue terrain holds only a glyph). Those entities read as attackable occupants, so the hero's step onto a trap/secret cell became a no-op attack and the hero never reached the cell — traps never sprang, secret doors were impassable after discovery. Worked around downstream with a game-specific RogueMovementSystem whose occupant = a creature (an entity with Health). That is a Rogue policy, not something the engine can assume, so the engine needs a general mechanism.
design:
Replace the hardcoded !Portal && !Item skip-list with a data-driven, per-entity walkability signal (ADR-0003: components are data, behaviour resolves).

RECOMMENDED — Option A: a NonBlocking (a.k.a. Passable) opt-out MARKER component in engine.components. A positioned entity blocks movement and is a bump target UNLESS it carries NonBlocking; occupantAt becomes firstOrNull { ... && !it.has<NonBlocking>() }. The engine attaches NonBlocking to the entities it already exempts (portals, floor items) so behaviour is unchanged; games tag their own non-blocking entities (traps, secret doors) with it. Preserves today's default (positioned = blocks), which is fail-CLOSED for creatures — forgetting the marker on a new monster still blocks, the safe direction — and is a minimal, backward-compatible generalization of the existing skip-list.

Option B — a Blocking opt-IN marker (occupantAt blocks only entities with Blocking). Conceptually cleaner (blockers are explicit) but fail-OPEN: forget it on a monster and the hero walks through it, and it forces touching every creature spawn (engine demo + all games). Rejected as the default for safety/migration cost.

Option C — a richer Passability/Collider DATA component (flags/enum: blocks-walkers vs flyers vs swimmers; and separate 'blocks movement' from 'is a bump/attack target' — occupantAt currently conflates the two, so a non-attackable solid like a boulder or closed portcullis can't be expressed). More future-proof but heavier; defer to a second consumer (rule of three); Option A can evolve into it.

Also note the escape hatch is already sound: a game with a wholly different occupancy policy can swap MovementSystem entirely (ADR-0014). korogue-rogue's RogueMovementSystem (occupant = has Health) is the reference/rule-of-three input if the engine later generalizes.
acceptance_criteria: occupantAt no longer names Portal/Item directly; a game can mark an arbitrary positioned entity non-blocking via an engine component and have the player/monsters step onto it; existing demo behaviour (portals, floor items non-blocking; creatures block/bump) unchanged; covered by an engine MovementSystem test that adds a non-blocking positioned entity and asserts a step lands on its cell.
notes: Implemented Option C (tag-based), ADR-0022. New: MovementTags (open string tags, no registry, mirrors PerceptionTags), Locomotion(modes), Collision(blocks,bump)+BumpResponse+Collision.PASSABLE. MovementSystem.occupantAt -> blockerAt: mover blocked iff moverModes subset-of blocks; blocked mover's response = Collision.bump (ATTACK|BLOCK). Fail-closed: absent Collision => solid+attackable. Registered Collision/Locomotion in GameModule. Portals/items tagged Collision.PASSABLE (demo + BehaviorSystemTest cross-zone chase). 4 new MovementSystem tests (passable, solid-BLOCK, flyer-vs-walker). Terrain per-mode passability deferred to krogue-xeb. Full suite + ktlint green.
close_reason: Data-driven occupancy via Collision+Locomotion tag model (ADR-0022); occupantAt no longer names Portal/Item; solid-vs-attackable split + locomotion modes; engine tests green. Terrain per-mode passability follow-up: krogue-xeb.

title: World-gen: GameModule.generators registry (resolve-by-id, save-aware)
description: Add a GameModule.generators: Registry<ZoneGenerator> with a Builder .generator(id, gen), and register engine built-ins in engineDefaults() (starting with randomWalkCave). Zones/levels reference a generator by id (like strategyId/calculatorId) so it persists and re-resolves on load. Mirror the existing registry pattern (strategies/senses/perceptionModels/calculators) exactly.
design: ADR-0019. Mostly mechanical — mirrors the existing GameModule registries. Depends on the ZoneGenerator type from the context/seam bead, but otherwise self-contained -> clean Sonnet task.
acceptance_criteria: generators registry resolves a built-in by id; a game can register its own; a generatorId round-trips through save/load; mirrors the other GameModule registries.
notes: FAN-OUT READY (b1p.1 landed). The ZoneGenerator fun interface now exists (com.sletmoe.korogue.algorithms.zonegen.ZoneGenerator). Mirror the existing GameModule registries EXACTLY (see engine .../registry/GameModule.kt + Registry.kt): add val generators: Registry<ZoneGenerator> to GameModule + constructor + Builder param; add Builder.generator(id, gen); register built-ins in engineDefaults(). randomWalkCave returns the terrain-only ZoneFeatureGenerator, so register it wrapped as a ZoneGenerator { ctx -> randomWalkCave(...)(ctx.tiles, ctx.random) } (give it an ID const). CORE scope = registry + registration + resolve-by-id, following the pattern. Mechanical -> ideal Sonnet task.
