title: World-gen: placement framework (overlap/spacing/density/try-N/bounds-fit)
description: A placer takes a prefab (or feature) + constraints (overlap avoidance, spacing, density, try-N attempts, bounds-fit) + RNG and finds valid positions, tracking occupied regions so repeated stamps don't collide. Crisp, headless-testable placement logic.
design: ADR-0019. Depends on the context/seam bead; pairs with the Prefab bead. Well-scoped, testable -> good Sonnet task once the seam exists.
acceptance_criteria: Scattering N prefabs with a no-overlap + min-spacing constraint places only non-colliding instances and respects bounds; try-N gives up gracefully when it can't fit.
notes:
FAN-OUT READY (b1p.1 landed; b1p.2 Prefab done, pending merge). Build against ZoneGenContext (bounds via ctx.tiles.width/height, random, pendingSpawns) and Prefab.stamp(ctx, originX, originY) (com.sletmoe.korogue.algorithms.zonegen.Prefab). A placer scatters prefabs with constraints (max count, min spacing, density, try-N attempts, bounds-fit), tracking occupied rects so stamps do not overlap, then calls Prefab.stamp at chosen origins.

DESIGN CALLS from b1p.2 to build on:
- Prefab is FIXED-SIZE + immutable; VARIABLE-size (e.g. shack-stamper 2-5x2-5) is expressed by a Prefab FACTORY (a lambda that builds a differently-sized Prefab per attempt, e.g. taking the Random) — NOT a size range on Prefab. The placer/generator holds such a factory and calls it per placement attempt to get a concrete-sized prefab, then bounds-fits + stamps it.
- Prefab.stamp REJECTS (throws) if it does not fit at the given origin — the placer must pick a fully-fitting origin BEFORE stamping (its bounds-fit job); never rely on stamp to clip.
- Prefab exposes width/height (bounding box) and doors/anchors (local-offset metadata) for alignment.
Pure/headless-testable: scatter into a ZoneGenContext, assert placed rects do not overlap + respect spacing/bounds, and that try-N gives up gracefully. Crisp logic, good Sonnet task.
close_reason: PrefabPlacer scatter framework implemented (Sonnet), reviewed, committed. PrefabPlacerTest 12/12 + GeometryTest 29/29 (IntRect.overlaps), full suite green.

title: World-gen: Prefab / room-stamp primitive
description: A Prefab describes a parameterized structure (size range, tiles, entity placements, anchor/door metadata) relative to a local origin. Stamping it into a ZoneGenContext at a position writes tiles and buffers entity spawns translated to that origin. Builds on the entity-aware context seam.
design: ADR-0019. Depends on the context/seam bead. Moderate.
acceptance_criteria: A Prefab can be defined with a size range + tiles + entity placements and stamped at a position, writing terrain and buffering its entities at the correct offsets.
notes:
FAN-OUT READY (b1p.1 landed + review-hardened). Build against ZoneGenContext (val tiles: Grid<Tile>, val random: Random, fun spawn(x,y,components: List<Component>)/vararg, val pendingSpawns view). Prefab = a value describing tiles + entity placements relative to a local (0,0) origin; fun stamp(ctx, originX, originY) writes tiles at the offset and calls ctx.spawn(originX+dx, originY+dy, components). Test by stamping into a ZoneGenContext and asserting ctx.tiles + ctx.pendingSpawns.

DESIGN DECISIONS from the b1p.1 API-fit review (2026-07-02):
- ANCHORS/DOORS live in the Prefab VALUE and are read by the placer (b1p.3) — NOT surfaced through the ZoneGenerator seam (generate() stays Unit). If inter-room connection (corridor-joining) is later needed, add a channel then (additive: a return value or a ZoneGenContext accumulator like pendingSpawns). Not needed for the shack-stamper acceptance.
- NO ENTITY IDS AT STAMP TIME: spawns are buffered (ids don't exist until GameWorld materializes them), so a Prefab's entity placements CANNOT reference each other (container->contents, wielder->weapon). Fine for Rogue (independent gold/monsters/traps/floor items); design the placement model accordingly.

The one open choice for the .2 author: how to express the tile layout (explicit Grid<Tile> vs char-map + legend).
close_reason: Implemented by Sonnet agents in isolated worktrees, reviewed, cherry-picked to mainline (b3cf12a3 Prefab, c4c421bc generators registry). Full suite green (PrefabTest 11/11, GameModuleTest 10/10).

title: World-gen: entity-aware generation context + seam (ZoneGenerator/ZoneGenContext)
description: Replace the terrain-only ZoneFeatureGenerator=(Grid<Tile>,Random)->Vector2Int with a context-carrying seam: fun interface ZoneGenerator { generate(ctx: ZoneGenContext) }. ZoneGenContext exposes the tile grid, the RNG, and a BUFFERED entity sink (declare position + component list to spawn) — Zone.Builder has no World, so generators emit spawn requests that GameWorld materializes via World.spawn (with Position/ZoneMember) AFTER build(). Generation stays a pure fn of (grid, RNG) -> (tiles, spawn requests): deterministic, ordering-independent, headless-testable. Migrate randomWalkCave to the new seam; keep a thin terrain-only adapter for the old shape. FOUNDATION for the other 3 sub-beads.
design: ADR-0019. Design-heavy (the context/sink shape + GameWorld materialization + migration). Do first.
acceptance_criteria: A generator can write tiles AND buffer entity spawns; GameWorld materializes them post-build; randomWalkCave works via the new seam; generation is unit-testable with no World.
close_reason: Entity-aware ZoneGenerator seam + buffered spawn sink implemented (d9d3e1c), API-fit reviewed (Opus, no blockers), and hardened (15006bd: fail-fast Zone.create). Full suite green. Fan-out (.2/.3/.4) ready.

title: Engine: feature/prefab-based world-gen (entity-aware seam + Prefab stamping + generators registry)
description: Today's world-gen extensibility is a single primitive seam: ZoneFeatureGenerator = (Grid<Tile>, Random) -> Vector2Int, applied via Zone.Builder.addFeature, with one built-in (randomWalkCave). Limitations surfaced building the Rogue generator (krogue-c20): (1) terrain-only — the seam can only mutate Grid<Tile>, with no way to place ENTITIES (monsters, gold, items, traps), so real generators bypass it; (2) no prefab/room primitive — nothing to define a parameterized structure (e.g. a 2-5 x 2-5 'shack') and stamp it; (3) no placement framework — no overlap/spacing/density/try-N/bounds-fit; (4) no generator registry — unlike strategies/senses/perception/calculators (first-class GameModule registries, ADR-0014), world-gen has no resolve-by-id, save/load-aware registry. Goal: an entity-aware generator seam (operate on Zone.Builder + an entity sink, or a richer build context), a Prefab/room-stamp primitive with placement constraints, and a GameModule.generators registry. Acceptance test: a 'shack stamper' that scatters variable-size single-room structures across a zone with no overlap. Informed by the bespoke c20 Rogue generator (faithful 3x3-grid port stays example-side; this is the complementary general capability — see ADR-0012 'engine pieces surfaced by the Rogue example' pattern). Likely warrants an ADR.
design: Decomposed into 4 sub-beads per docs/adr/0019-prefab-entity-aware-worldgen.md. Layered so generation stays pure (no live World; a buffered entity sink is materialized by GameWorld after build) and fully headless-testable. Acceptance for the epic: a 'shack stamper' generator scatters variable-size single-room structures with no overlap (exercises all four pieces). Faithful Rogue 3x3 generator stays example-side (ADR-0012); this is the general engine capability.
close_reason: All 4 pieces implemented, reviewed, integrated + green. End-to-end shack-stamper acceptance test (composes Prefab factory + PrefabPlacer + GameModule.generators + GameWorld materialization) passes. ADR-0019.

title: MapPanel renders Perceived; relocate view distance (supersedes f50)
description: Per ADR-0015. MapPanel is handed a chosen observer's Perceived and draws it; it no longer computes LOS-and-lit or owns maximumVisibilityDistance (that moves onto the Sight component, superseding the interim krogue-f50). The rendered observer becomes a presentation choice (player by default; companion/faction views fall out). Wire the Rogue example onto the perception model (player gets a Sight).
close_reason: MapPanel renders a chosen observer's Perceived (default: player); dropped LOS-and-lit and maximumVisibilityDistance (now Sight.radius), finishing krogue-f50->ADR-0015. PerceptionSystem wired after LightingSystem in both demo and Rogue example; player gets Sight()+Perceived(). LineOfSightCalculator made a fun interface. Engine 356 tests + rogue example build green. Force-closed past the soft dep on krogue-1my.3 (concealment): the two are independent — invisible-monster hiding already works via Perceived.entities once 1my.3 lands its Invisible/Blind components; no rendering change needed there.

title: Concealment + tags + piercing + suppressors (two-phase)
description: Per ADR-0015. Concealment components on targets (Invisible) carrying tags they conceal from; senses may declare pierces-tags (see-invisible). Observer suppressor components (Blind) negate tags; suppressors are components (not removal) so a transient blind effect is scheduler-expirable (krogue-6uq). Implement the suppress phase: remove sense contributions whose tags are negated, unless a contributing sense pierces. Tags are string ids with engine constants; no tag registry.
notes: Two-phase reveal/suppress ALGORITHM already landed in 1my.1 (StandardPerception), along with the Suppressor/Concealment MARKER interfaces and Contribution carrying tags/pierces; the algorithm fully handles suppressors, concealments, and piercing generically. This task ADDS: concrete components (Invisible: Concealment{visual}; Blind/Dazzled: Suppressor{visual}; future Silenced{vibration}), engine tag-id constants, piercing senses/modifiers (see-invisible, true-sight) [coordinate with 1my.2 senses], scheduler-expirable transient suppressors (krogue-6uq wiring), GameModule registration, and scenario tests (invisible monster, blindness restore-on-expire).
close_reason: Concrete suppress-phase payload: Invisible (Concealment{visual}), Blind/Dazzled (Suppressor{visual}) as dataless data-objects + TrueSight built-in sense piercing {visual} (sees invisible, unblinded by design — uniform piercing). Registered for save/load + senses in engineDefaults. Transient blindness scheduler-expirable via fuse removing Blind (krogue-6uq). 10 new tests (TrueSightSense unit + PerceptionScenarioTest E2E); full suite + ktlint green. Completes epic krogue-1my.

title: Senses: opt-in components + Sense contributor registry + engine senses
description: Per ADR-0015 + ADR-0014. Senses are opt-in data components (Sight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, Telepathy) interpreted by Sense contributors registered by id in GameModule (module.sense(id, impl)); no sense contributes unless the observer has its component. Each sense declares tags ({visual, light-dependent}, etc.). Engine ships the common senses; games register their own. Move the view-distance (sight radius) onto the Sight component (it is per-observer and mutable).
notes: Senses registry SEAM already exists (added in 1my.1): GameModule.senses (Registry<Sense>) + .sense(id, impl) builder, currently empty. This task ADDS the concrete engine sense COMPONENTS (Sight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, Telepathy as SenseComponent types), their Sense CONTRIBUTORS (with tags + LOS/lightMap reads — note: no LOS registry yet; MapPanel holds losCalculator directly, decide where the sight sense gets its LOS calc), engine tag-id constants, and registers them in GameModule.engineDefaults(). Each sense = its own component type (ECS keys by concrete type).
close_reason: Added engine sense components (Sight/Darkvision/Tremorsense/Telepathy) as opt-in SenseComponent types, their Sense contributors (tags + LOS/lighting/radius reveal), PerceptionTags constants, registered in engineDefaults() with LOS injected via SymmetricShadowCaster. View distance moved onto Sight.radius. Components registered for save/load. 16 new tests, 353 total green.

title: Perception core: PerceptionModel, Perceived, StandardPerception
description: Per ADR-0015. Add the perception layer skeleton: a Perceived result (perceived cells + entities), a PerceptionModel interface (perceive(observer, world) -> Perceived) resolved via GameModule (new registry), and a default StandardPerception implementing the two-phase reveal/suppress model. A PerceptionSystem writes a derived Perceived component per-tick for observers that need it each frame (per-observer caching, like lightMap). Query is the primitive; cache is the optimization.
close_reason: Perception core landed: perception package (Perceived, Contribution, Sense/SenseComponent, Suppressor/Concealment, PerceptionModel, StandardPerception two-phase model), PerceptionSystem per-observer cache, GameModule senses+perceptionModels registries. 16 tests added (337 total, green). Ships inert pending 1my.2 (senses) / 1my.3 (concealments).

title: Perception & visibility model (ADR-0015)
description: Implement the three-layer visibility model from ADR-0015: illumination (exists) + line-of-sight (exists) + a new observer-relative perception layer. Perception = composable senses (opt-in data components interpreted by registered Sense contributors), concealment components carrying tags, sense-pierces-tags, a two-phase reveal-then-suppress execution, suppressor components (blindness, scheduler-expirable), per-observer query with per-observer caching, and MapPanel rendering a chosen observer's Perceived result. Engine ships StandardPerception + common senses so simple games just add a Sight component. Governed by ADR-0014 (pluggable policy, fixed mechanism).
close_reason: All 4 children complete: perception core + two-phase reveal/suppress (1my.1), built-in senses (1my.2), MapPanel renders Perceived (1my.4), concealment/piercing/suppressors (1my.3). Three-layer visibility model per ADR-0015 shipped: illumination + LOS + observer-relative perception via composable senses, tag-based concealment/suppression with piercing, per-observer cache. Engine ships StandardPerception + Sight/Darkvision/TrueSight/Tremorsense/Telepathy + Invisible/Blind/Dazzled.

title: MapPanel: optional (uncapped) view distance
description: MapPanel.maximumVisibilityDistance is a non-nullable Double (default 30), so every game gets a hard circular visibility cap even though the LineOfSightCalculator interface already accepts a nullable maxViewDistance (null = no cap, honored by SymmetricShadowCaster). A game with global/room lighting wants visibility limited only by walls, not distance. Make the field Double? (default 30.0, null = unlimited) and pass it through. Surfaced by the Rogue example: a lit room was clipped to a 30-tile disc, which read as non-global. Discovered via krogue-hhe.
close_reason: MapPanel.maximumVisibilityDistance is now Double?, default null (uncapped/walls-only). Test added. Note: view distance ultimately moves onto a per-observer Vision component in the visibility rework.

title: Direction enum: 8 compass directions as a grid primitive
description: Movement, AI, FOV, and throwing all hand-roll dx/dy steps (WanderStrategy's STEPS list, HuntPlayerStrategy's coerceIn, the Rogue example's MOVES map). Add a Direction enum to com.sletmoe.korogue.utilities: 8 compass dirs with (dx,dy) unit steps, opposite, from(Vector2Int), and companion CARDINAL/DIAGONAL plus ofStep/between for turning a delta into a single grid step. Add a MoveIntent(Direction) constructor. Dogfood it in WanderStrategy. Discovered building the Rogue example (krogue-hhe) per the 'find missing engine pieces' directive.

title: Ambient light / global illumination mode (lightMap baseline)
description: Lighting is purely emitter-driven: LightingSystem fills each zone's lightMap to null and only LightEmitter entities light cells, and MapPanel hides any cell whose lightMap is null. So a roguelike that doesn't model light (Rogue, and many others) has no clean way to render — it must fake a giant LightEmitter on the player. Add an ambient-light baseline to LightingSystem (ambientLight: LightValue? = null): fill the lightMap with the ambient value instead of null, so emitters blend on top and, with a full-white ambient, the whole zone is uniformly lit ('global illumination' / fullbright). Add LightValue.FULLBRIGHT preset. Backward compatible (default null = current point-light behavior). Discovered while scaffolding the Rogue example (krogue-hhe).
close_reason: LightingSystem gains ambientLight baseline + LightValue.FULLBRIGHT; global illumination without faking emitters. Tests added.

title: Fixed-timestep RealTimeLoop (decouple continuous ticks from render FPS)
description: RealTimeLoop (krogue-lhw) currently ticks the world once per render frame, so the continuous game speed is tied to frame rate (faster machine / higher FPS = faster monsters; frame hitches stutter the sim). Decouple it: accumulate per-frame wall-clock delta and advance the world at a fixed timestep (e.g. every N ms) independent of render FPS, with a max-catch-up cap to avoid the spiral of death after a long frame. Requires threading a deltaMs into GameLoop.advance (currently advance(tick) has no time arg) — e.g. advance(deltaMs, tick); TurnBasedLoop ignores it. Then real-time AI can act every fixed tick and the per-tick act-chance throttle could be dropped. Engine change in com.sletmoe.korogue.loop.
close_reason: RealTimeLoop is now a fixed-timestep accumulator (stepMs/maxCatchUpSteps); deltaMs threaded through Game.onTick -> GameLoop.advance. World speed is FPS-independent. Tests + build green.

title: Timed-effects scheduler (daemons & fuses) for the turn loop
description: Rogue drives most timed behaviour through a daemon/fuse scheduler (rogue.h/daemons.c): one-shot 'fuses' that fire after N turns and recurring 'daemons' that run every turn (regen, hunger, status-effect expiry, ring effects, wandering-monster spawns). Add a general turn-keyed scheduler to the krogue engine: schedule one-shot and recurring callbacks/effects by turn count, cancel/lengthen them, advance on each world turn, and make it part of save state (so timers resume). Pairs with krogue-lhw (turn-on-input loop). The Rogue example ([deleted:krogue-sdh]) is its first consumer.
close_reason: Added turn-keyed Scheduler (fuses/daemons, cancel/lengthen) + TimedEffect extension point + SchedulerSystem; GameModule effects registry; serializable SchedulerState round-tripped via SaveCodec (timers resume across save/load). Demo wired (no effects yet). 17 new tests, ktlint clean.

title: Turn-on-input loop (replace per-frame ticking)
description: The ECS world currently ticks once per render frame (MyGame.onTick), so creatures act ~60x/sec and combat is near-instant (the player can die immediately). AI strategies carry a 2%-per-tick act gate as a band-aid. Replace with a turn-based loop: advance the world only when the player takes an action (move/wait/etc.), so one player action = one world turn and AI acts once per turn (drop the act-gate throttle). This is also a prerequisite for the Rogue example ([deleted:krogue-sdh]), which is turn-based by nature. Touches MyGame's loop (onTick vs input) and BehaviorStrategies' throttle.
close_reason: Closed

title: kotile: bundle 12x12 CP437 font
description: Needs license/provenance decision.
design: DECISION: bundle a 12x12 CP437 sheet derived from the CC0 'Modern DOS' 8x16 bitmaps (Jayvee Enaguas) via susam/pcface, used under CC0 1.0 (pcface offers them MIT-or-CC0). Rendered per-glyph 8x16 -> 12x12 (Lanczos + smoothstep contrast) into a 16x16 CP437 grid; alpha-carrying sheet (RGB white, coverage in alpha) loaded with keyColor=null so it composites cleanly when tinted by the cell fg. Rationale: a native square-12x12, permissively-licensed, CP437-complete bitmap font does not exist; the clean-licensed options are all non-square/non-12 (Spleen BSD 8x16/16x32, GNU Unifont OFL 16x16) or copyleft (VileR oldschool CC-BY-SA/GPL). Deriving from CC0 keeps the requested 12x12 metric with zero attribution obligation, matching the vaarn-8x8 precedent. Verified in-engine via :kotile:demo:fontHarness (full CP437 chart + text + box frame, no halos on light bg).

description: The primary Brogue-look route (ADR-0036 tier 3). A GlyphSource impl that rasterizes a TTF at the EXACT cell pixel size via gdx-freetype (FreeType supplies the gamma-correct hinted AA Brogue hand-rolls), caching per size and regenerating on resize. Yields smooth, high-res-derived glyphs crisp at ANY window size — the actual Brogue aesthetic, which supersampling a bitmap (tier 2) cannot produce. Needs a bundled or BYO TTF (licensing TBD, like krogue-kotile-font12/krogue-pe1). Depends on the GlyphSource seam. Deferred refinement (optional): Brogue's per-region sub-pixel alignment + brightness curves.
notes: Correction (per CodeRabbit): FreeType outputs hinted AA *coverage* (an alpha mask), not gamma-correct pixels — gamma-correct compositing is the pipeline's job (blend the coverage in linear space, as tier-2 does). Don't claim FreeType makes output gamma-correct on its own.

title: Extract a size-parametric GlyphSource seam (Font becomes the bitmap impl)
description: Tier-3 prerequisite (ADR-0036). Introduce a GlyphSource interface: given a target cell pixel size, yield a glyph texture at that size (plus a resize/prepare hook to (re)generate on cell-size change). The existing Font becomes the size-agnostic BITMAP implementation, so tiers 1-2 and the current API (Fonts.cp437_10x10/12x12, AsciiTileWindow(font=...)) are unaffected — backward-compatible refactor. AsciiTileWindow generalizes its 'font: Font' dependency to accept a GlyphSource. This unblocks the freetype and SDF sources. Touch: Fonts.kt/Font, AsciiTileWindow constructor + glyph draw path.

title: Glyph/tile crispness beyond IntegerScale (resolution-independent + Brogue-fidelity)
description: Per ADR-0036 (docs/adr/0036-two-tier-glyph-tile-crispness.md): kotile offers three tiers of cell crispness, consumer's choice. Tier 1 = fixed bitmap Font + IntegerScale (default, done: krogue-kotile-font12). Tier 2 = resolution-independent PIXEL crispness via supersample-to-FBO + gamma-correct downsample (krogue-1zo) — crisp at any window size for glyphs AND sprites, reuses today's fonts, keeps the CP437 pixel look. Tier 3 = Brogue-fidelity SMOOTH glyphs via a size-parametric GlyphSource seam + a high-res/vector source rasterized at cell px (gdx-freetype TTF-at-size primary; SDF as an alt for UI text). Key insight: 'crisp at any size' (a scaling property, tier 2) is NOT the same as Brogue's smooth-glyph look (a glyph-SOURCE property needing high-res input, tier 3). Tiers 2 and 3 are independent and can land in either order; both are GL-visual work to verify on retina, ideally atop krogue-3eu (HiDPI/Viewport).
design: Supersedes ADR-0017's 'three coequal deferred ScalePolicy strategies' framing. krogue-yfs (multi-size swap) is dropped as dominated.

close_reason: Both double-dispose tests in RenderingLifecycleIntegrationTest now dispose the Pixmap that HeadlessGl.render returns (chained .dispose()); they ignore the pixels, so the capture was leaking on Linux CI.

title: Engine mixes layer-based and feature-based packaging inconsistently (systems/ vs schedule/, components/ vs perception/)
description:
Found while doing krogue-edn's 'review overall package discoverability' half.

The engine groups code two different ways at once, and the split is not predictable:

- Systems: 8 live in systems/ (Behavior, Combat, Lighting, Movement, Perception, Pickup, Portal, RangedAttack) but SchedulerSystem lives in schedule/ next to Scheduler/TimedEffect.
- Components: 17 live in components/ but 3 live in perception/ (SenseComponents.kt, PerceptionTags.kt).

So perception is featured-out EXCEPT its system (which is layered into systems/), and schedule is featured-in including its system. A newcomer asking 'where do I find the system for X' or 'where do I add a component' gets a different answer per feature, with no rule to infer.

Not urgent and not obviously a bug -- both groupings are defensible, but picking one per feature and applying it consistently is the point. Worth settling before 1.0 only insofar as these are published import paths (same argument as krogue-edn/ADR-0031); moving them after 1.0 is breaking for consumers.

Note the pull in each direction: co-locating a feature's system with its model (perception/PerceptionSystem) aids cohesion; keeping all systems in systems/ aids the 'what does the engine run' overview that ARCHITECTURE.md's systems section gives. Decide and record an ADR.
notes: Surveyed 2026-07-15 via grep for '*System' class defs and ': Component' impls under engine/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/korogue. Counts above are from that survey. Related: krogue-edn (ADR-0031) settled app.Game/perception.ZoneFog; this is the remaining discoverability debt from that same review.
close_reason: Landed together in one engine change (ADR-0032). cjv: built-in systems normalized onto GameWorld + Registry<T>, per-system activeZones removed (scope now the world's SimulatedZonePolicy); added public Registry.of factory. 32d: installStandardSystems + Staged/PipelineStage/StandardStage with World.tick() auto-validating order (PipelineOrderException). elm: PerceptionSystem moved to perception/. Demo uses installStandardSystems; Rogue port rewired by hand and its RogueCombatSystem/RoguePickupSystem declare COMBAT/PICKUP. 586 engine + 590 rogue tests green, both ktlint-clean.

title: kotile: per-channel ASCII compositing (glyph from top cell, background from top opaque cell)
description:
ADR-0029 settled that AsciiTileWindow's top-cell-wins compositing is correct rather than accidental (bottom-up would overlap glyphs), and fixed the KDoc that claimed otherwise. It explicitly left this on the table.

Today a cell is resolved whole: the highest-z non-null cell supplies glyph AND foreground AND background, and everything below is discarded. Measured consequence: Color.CLEAR and Color.BLACK backgrounds are byte-identical once layered, so StaticAsciiTile's alpha buys a layered consumer nothing.

Per-channel resolution would fix that: take the glyph+foreground from the top-most non-null cell, but the background from the top-most cell whose background is not fully transparent. Then:
- A creature cell can use a CLEAR background and sit on the terrain's background color, instead of restating it. Today every overlay must duplicate the colors of whatever it covers, which means overlays have to know about terrain.
- A background-ONLY overlay becomes expressible: targeting highlights, Brogue-style lighting/torch tint, damage flashes, 'this tile is in your path' shading -- all of which want to tint the cell while leaving the creature glyph alone. Right now that layer would erase the creature.

This is the roguelike-shaped model (Brogue resolves fg and bg separately) and it makes the layer stack in AsciiTileWindow's own class KDoc (terrain z=0 / creature z=1 / effect z=2) actually work as it reads.

Design notes:
- Keep glyph resolution top-cell-wins; only background resolution changes. Two glyphs still cannot share a cell.
- 'Not fully transparent' vs 'any alpha': decide whether a partially transparent background alpha-blends over the one below (more expressive, more expensive) or whether resolution is a simple first-opaque-wins scan (cheaper, predictable). Prefer the latter unless there is a real use for partial blending.
- Perf: today drawCell stops at topCellAt. This needs a scan down the layers for the background, bounded by layer count, and only on dirty cells (GridCompositeCache already limits that). Measure before assuming it matters.
- The engine's TileSurface seam (com.sletmoe.korogue.ui) documents top-cell-wins in its KDoc, and RegionSurface's dim-behind effect relies on it -- both need review if this lands.
- Behaviour change: a consumer relying on a CLEAR-bg overlay to blank the cell to the clear color would see terrain instead. That is a break, so it wants to land pre-1.0 or not at all.
notes: Filed from ADR-0029 / krogue-8mr. Pre-1.0 relevance: this changes the meaning of an existing public property (StaticAsciiTile.backgroundColor alpha) for layered use, so decide before release rather than after. Not a blocker -- the current behaviour is now honestly documented and pinned by tests.
close_reason: Implemented (PR #7, ADR-0030). Glyph+foreground stay top-cell-wins; background now resolves from the top-most cell that actually paints one, so a transparent background means 'I don't paint one' and defers to the cell below. First-painter-wins, not alpha blending -- the cheap predictable rule this issue recommended. ADR-0029's argument only ever proved something about glyphs (two can't share a cell); it generalised that to the background channel, which has no such conflict. Also fixed a latent bug it exposed: the viewport path only checked the TOP cell for DynamicAsciiTile, so a dynamic background under a static glyph would have frozen. Behaviour change landed pre-1.0 as the issue asked; surveyed engine + Rogue port + demos and found NO transparent-background usage, so nothing broke -- RegionSurface's dim-behind uses opaque bgs and its KDoc now records why it depends on that. Verified against real pixels, then CI green.

title: kotile: AsciiTileWindow.clear/clearLayer have no pixel-level test (sprite mirrors now do)
description:
krogue-0y8 added GL-gated behavior tests for the sprite path's new clear()/clearLayer()/fill()/topTileAt(). The ascii path's long-standing equivalents are only covered indirectly: RenderingIntegrationTest has a pixel test for AsciiTileWindow.fill and for clearTile cache staleness, but none for clear() or clearLayer().

clearLayer in particular carries the same 'collect affected cells before clearing, then mark them dirty' bookkeeping on both paths (it must dirty the cells it vacated or content goes stale, without disturbing lower layers). That logic is now pixel-tested on the sprite side and untested on the ascii side -- the asymmetry ADR-0028 is trying to eliminate, just in the tests rather than the API.

Mirror the sprite cases from RenderingIntegrationTest (search krogue-0y8) onto AsciiTileWindow: clear() drops every layer with no stale cache content; clearLayer(z) clears only z and reveals the layer beneath; clearLayer on a never-written layer is a no-op.

Note these are HeadlessGl-gated, so they only execute on Linux CI (xvfb), not on macOS -- GLFW needs the first thread and Gradle test workers don't own it. To check them locally on macOS, use the JavaExec + -XstartOnFirstThread harness pattern already in kotile/demo/build.gradle.kts (renderHarness/spriteHarness).
notes: Pre-existing gap, surfaced by krogue-0y8 rather than caused by it. Low risk (the code has shipped and works) but cheap, and keeps test coverage as symmetric as ADR-0028 makes the API.
close_reason: Done (PR #4). Added pixel coverage for AsciiTileWindow.clear/clearLayer mirroring the sprite cases from krogue-0y8: clear() drops every layer with no stale cache content, clearLayer(z) clears only z and reveals the layer beneath, clearLayer on a never-written layer is a no-op. Verified against real pixels via a throwaway JavaExec + -XstartOnFirstThread harness, then CI (green).

title: kotile: sprite and ascii paths use different z-compositing policies
description:
ADR-0028 aligned the two render paths' vocabulary but left a real behavioural asymmetry in place: AsciiTileWindow composites top-cell-wins (the highest-z non-null cell is drawn, lower layers ignored), while TileRenderer draws every populated layer bottom-up so upper-layer alpha reveals what is beneath.

This is not purely intrinsic. A StaticAsciiTile with a transparent background color would reveal lower layers under a bottom-up policy, but today it does not -- the top cell simply wins and paints its (transparent) background quad. So the ascii path's policy is a choice, not a consequence of glyphs, and it silently discards content a consumer may reasonably expect to show through.

Decide whether the ascii path should composite bottom-up like the sprite path (making transparent-bg ascii cells layer properly), or whether top-wins is the deliberate policy and should be documented as such on both sides. Either way the KDoc on both classes and ADR-0028's 'kept deliberately' section need updating to match.

Note the perf angle: top-wins lets the ascii path stop at the first non-null cell; bottom-up means every populated layer is drawn per cell. Measure before switching -- GridCompositeCache (ADR-0024) already limits this to dirty cells.

Surfaced while doing krogue-0y8.
notes: Deliberately out of scope for krogue-0y8, which was a naming/parity change. Not a blocker for 1.0 unless the answer is 'ascii should composite bottom-up', which would itself be a behavioural break worth landing pre-1.0 -- so triage this before release rather than after.
close_reason: Resolved by ADR-0029 (PR #4). Measured rather than assumed: with z=0 '#' on blue, a z=1 CLEAR-bg overlay leaves b=0.00 and is byte-identical to a BLACK-bg one, and a blank ' ' overlay erases the terrain entirely. So top-cell-wins genuinely discards lower layers -- but the behaviour is right and the DOCS were wrong. Matching the sprite path's bottom-up compositing would overlap two glyphs in one cell rather than draw a creature on a floor; the asymmetry is intrinsic to atomic glyph/fg/bg cells vs images. Kept top-cell-wins, fixed the StaticAsciiTile KDoc that promised transparent-bg overlays work, documented the policy + its two footguns on both paths, and pinned it with 4 pixel tests. Per-channel compositing split out as krogue-7va.

title: engine: TileSurface can't express a time-varying cell (kotile's DynamicAsciiTile branch is unreachable)
description:
kotile's ASCII hierarchy now has an open DynamicAsciiTile branch (krogue-xcx, ADR-0027): any cell whose appearance is a function of time, with AnimatedAsciiTile the built-in frame-cycling impl. AsciiTileWindow marks those cells for per-frame repaint.

The engine's UI toolkit cannot reach any of it. TileSurface.put() takes (x, y, z, glyph, fg, bg) and WindowSurface always constructs a StaticAsciiTile from those, so no widget can place an AnimatedAsciiTile or a custom DynamicAsciiTile — Brogue-style torch flicker is expressible in kotile but not through korogue. The kotile demo has to bypass the engine and drive AsciiTileWindow directly to show it off.

Worth deciding whether the toolkit seam should carry the dynamic branch (e.g. a put(x, y, z, tile: AsciiTile) overload) or whether animation belongs on a different seam entirely (presentation/VisualSequence). Note TileSurface is deliberately narrow so the toolkit stays headlessly testable against a fake (ADR-0011) — widening it has a cost, and a fake would need to model time.

Not a blocker for the Rogue example: original Rogue has no animated cells, so the faithful port doesn't need this.
notes: Surfaced while doing krogue-xcx. Rogue imports only kotile's Vector2Int/Grid — it never touches the tile hierarchies, so the rename needed zero changes there.
close_reason: Implemented and merged via PR #14 (ADR-0033): TileSurface/WindowSurface now carry kotile's DynamicAsciiTile branch. Merged into krogue-a24-shared-canvas-blend; reaches mainline when PR #13 merges.

title: NormalizedRgb has a thin API; model/presentation color split is an undocumented seam
description:
The engine exposes two color types to consumers with no stated convention for which to use where:
- algorithms/color/NormalizedRgb (Double r/g/b, immutable, @Serializable) — the MODEL color, used in components (Renderable.color, LightEmitter.color, LightValue).
- GDX Color (Float, mutable) — the PRESENTATION color, used across the UI toolkit (TileSurface.put/text/fill, Widget draws, AsciiTileWindow.drawText) and world.Tile.

A consumer authoring a colored component uses NormalizedRgb, but authoring UI uses Color, and must convert (toColor()/toNormalizedRgb()) at the seam. This is defensible (ADR: colors -> GDX at the draw boundary) but is nowhere stated as an API convention, and NormalizedRgb itself is bare: no BLACK/WHITE/common constants, no fromHex/from(Color) factory, no lerp; its file doc is a lowercase one-liner ('represent RGB data in a min-max normalized form').

Why it matters for 1.0: adding constants/factories to NormalizedRgb is additive (P3), but the two-color-type story should be documented (which type a consumer touches, and where the boundary is) so newcomers aren't surprised. Consider a short ADR/architecture note plus NormalizedRgb.BLACK/WHITE + fromColor().
close_reason: Added NormalizedRgb companion palette (BLACK/WHITE + common colours re-exported from GDX), fromColor/fromHex factories, and lerp; documented the model/presentation colour seam in ADR-0035 + ARCHITECTURE.md. Rogue port and demos now author model colours via NormalizedRgb constants instead of Color.X.toNormalizedRgb().

title: World system management: no removeSystem; chaining inconsistent with spawn
description:
ecs/World.kt: systems can be added (addSystem) and listed (systems()) but never removed — there is no removeSystem/clearSystems, unlike entities which have spawn+despawn. addSystem returns World for fluent chaining, but spawn (the entity equivalent) returns the Entity, so the 'add' verbs don't behave alike. Also note verb drift for 'add to a collection': entities use spawn/despawn, systems use addSystem (no remove), zones use addZone/removeZone.

Why it matters: additive and non-breaking to add removeSystem later, so P3 — but worth deciding whether hot-swapping systems (e.g. pausing AI, swapping loops) is in scope for 1.0, since the demo's save/load already re-registers systems on a fresh World as a workaround. Minor consistency polish.
close_reason: Added World.removeSystem(system): Boolean and World.clearSystems(), mirroring entity despawn / zone removeZone lifecycle; both invalidate order-validation so the surviving pipeline is re-checked before the next tick. Kept addSystem returning World (fluent builder) rather than matching spawn's return-Entity: documented the deliberate asymmetry in KDoc — the Rogue port's installRoguePipeline chains ~25 addSystem calls, so changing it would break real consumers; systems are wired in bulk and referenced by instance, unlike an entity whose id is needed immediately. Neither consumer needs removal today (save/load rebuilds a fresh World), so coverage is engine-side WorldTest cases: removal stops execution + returns presence bool, clearSystems leaves entities/events intact, and post-removal re-validation. Full :engine suite + korogue-rogue suite green.

title: kotile:library AND kotile:demo missing ktlint configuration (only root :demo and :engine have it)
description: build.gradle.kts applies id("org.jlleitschuh.gradle.ktlint") in engine/build.gradle.kts and demo/build.gradle.kts only. Both kotile/library/build.gradle.kts and kotile/demo/build.gradle.kts lack the plugin entirely -- confirmed via grep across all 4 build.gradle.kts files. CI logs (krogue-0k1's PR runs) show ktlint tasks (runKtlintCheckOverKotlinScripts, ktlintMainSourceSetCheck, etc.) only for :demo and :engine, none for either kotile module. kotile:library is the published library (com.sletmoe:kotile) and kotile:demo is its runnable sample -- both should have the same lint gate as the rest of the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: kotile:library runs the same ktlint check tasks as :demo/:engine as part of ./gradlew check, and existing kotile source passes (or is reformatted to pass).
close_reason: Added org.jlleitschuh.gradle.ktlint to kotile:library and kotile:demo (version already in settings.gradle.kts pluginManagement). Reformatted kotile:demo harness build script + 3 harness sources; fixed pre-existing kotile:library violations (suppressed function-naming on public Fonts.cp437_10x10, camelCased benchmark locals, unwrapped long test-comment lines). Both modules now run ktlint script/main/test checks under ./gradlew check and pass.

title: RenderingIntegrationTest: per-frame tint test asserts g=0 but SHEET_BLUE fixture has g=0.3
description: RenderingIntegrationTest.kt:145 ('TileRenderer applies an AnimatedSpriteTile's per-frame tint, not just its constant tint', added in commit 0ce83447) asserts frame0.g shouldBe (0.0 plusOrMinus 0.1), but the test's own SHEET_BLUE fixture is Color(0.3f, 0.3f, 0.9f, 1f) — g=0.3. The actual rendered value (0.298) correctly matches the fixture and the test's own comment ('no override -> the sheet's own blue shows through'); the assertion itself is wrong, unrelated to any renderer regression. Never caught because CI silently skipped GL tests until krogue-0k1 added Xvfb. Fix: change the assertion to 0.3 plusOrMinus 0.1, or assert on a channel that actually distinguishes tinted vs untinted (e.g. compare frame0 vs frame1's g directly).
acceptance_criteria: The assertion matches the documented/actual untinted-frame color; test passes under CI.
close_reason: Fixed as part of krogue-asz's commit 2a35a920 -- same root cause investigation turned up this second unrelated test bug.

title: kotile: per-observer dirty tracking for shared/multi-pane tilemaps (TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow render(source, viewport))
description: TileRenderer.render(source, viewport) and AsciiTileWindow.render(source, viewport) take a caller-owned LayeredTilemap that may be sampled by multiple renderers/panes at different viewport origins (the windowed-viewport pattern those overloads exist for, e.g. one big world map shown through several panes). krogue-drk's whole-frame composite cache (GridCompositeCache, ADR-0024) deliberately did NOT cover this overload: a naive 'dirty since last render' flag on the shared tilemap would be consumed/cleared by whichever renderer calls render() first, leaving other panes wrongly believing nothing changed. Fixing this needs per-observer generation tracking (e.g. a monotonic version counter per LayeredTilemap cell, with each consumer remembering the last version it rendered per logical cell) rather than a single consumable dirty flag. Currently this overload always fully repaints every call, same as before krogue-drk -- no regression, just no perf win here.
close_reason: Implemented: LayeredTilemap gained a per-position version counter (versionAt), bumped by every write touching that position -- a query, not a consumable event, so any number of observers can read it independently without stepping on each other. A new ViewportDirtyTracker (paired with its own GridCompositeCache, separate from the internal-tilemap one) does per-observer bookkeeping for render(source, viewport) on both TileRenderer and AsciiTileWindow: compares each visible cell's versionAt against what THIS tracker last recorded, invalidating everything on a changed TileViewport origin or a different source instance. Animated entries still force a cell dirty via an isAnimatedAt callback, same pattern as krogue-oxi. Verified with the exact scenario the ticket describes: two windows sharing one world tilemap at different viewport origins, each written to differently, window A rendered first then window B -- B came back pixel-identical to a fresh reference (built from the same final state directly), confirming the 'flag stolen by whichever renders first' bug does not occur. Added two permanent GL-gated regression tests to ViewportIntegrationTest. Full writeup appended to docs/adr/0024-dirty-region-redraw-grid-composite-cache.md's second Update section.

title: GlyphProjectile has no direction-based glyph selection (ASCII directional missiles)
description: VisualEvent.SpriteProjectile got continuous geometric rotation (krogue-m05, nativeBearingDeg + rotationTowards/atan2) so a sprite arrow visibly points along its actual travel angle. VisualEvent.GlyphProjectile has no equivalent -- a glyph can't rotate geometrically, so today a caller passes one fixed glyph regardless of travel direction. Original Rogue (and the roguelike genre generally) instead picks from a small set of missile characters (|, -, \, /) based on travel direction -- see rogue5.4.4's missile rendering for the canonical reference (~/Downloads/rogue5.4.4) if korogue-rogue wants to port that exactly. This bead is the generic engine-side piece: a reusable way to bucket a travel angle (or dx/dy) into one of a small glyph set, so any ASCII game (not just Rogue) can drive directional missile glyphs off GlyphProjectile the same way SpriteProjectile already drives rotation off nativeBearingDeg. Likely a small standalone utility function (e.g. in algorithms/geometry, mirroring rotationTowards's home in kotile) rather than a GlyphProjectile field, since the actual glyph choice (which characters, how many buckets) is a caller/game concern -- the engine should supply the angle-to-bucket math, not hardcode Rogue's specific four characters.
close_reason: Added directionalMissileGlyph(dx, dy) in engine/algorithms/geometry -- the ASCII counterpart to rotationTowards's continuous sprite rotation, bucketing a travel direction into the classic -|\/ missile glyph set (customizable characters, since the choice is a caller/game concern). MyGame's archer (krogue-4tn) now uses it instead of a fixed '*', so the shot's glyph actually points the way it's travelling. Unit tested; full gate + smoke-boot passed.

title: Projectiles (glyph and sprite) aren't tinted by cell lighting
description: GlyphProjectileSequence.render() (VisualSequence.kt:145-146) draws with event.color straight into putAt(), and SpriteProjectileSequence.renderSprite() (VisualSequence.kt:201) draws with event.tint straight into canvas.drawSprite() -- neither looks up zone.lightMap or calls the litColor/tintedByLight helper MapPanel now uses for terrain and occupants (krogue-0w3). A projectile keeps a constant color for its whole flight even when passing through dim or unlit cells, while everything else in the lit-rendering path (terrain fg/bg, occupant fg) now dims/flickers correctly. Fix: thread a per-cell light lookup into the projectile sequences (they'd need read access to the Zone/lightMap the way MapPanel's litColor does) and apply Color.tintedByLight() per rendered position along the path.
close_reason: Added tintAt callback to VisualEvent.GlyphProjectile and SpriteProjectile (mirrors the existing backgroundAt precedent), applied in GlyphProjectileSequence.render/SpriteProjectileSequence.renderSprite. Demo's maybeFireProjectiles wired both projectile events to its own litColor helper so they dim/tint with the room's torchlight instead of staying a flat constant color. Verified visually via a temporary mid-flight snapshot.

title: Facing-direction sprite mirroring (flip left/right on move/aim)
description:
The animation showcase demo just hit this manually: DawnLike's ranger sprite faces a fixed
direction in its source art, and had to be hand-flipped (TextureRegion.flip(true, false), a one-off
fix in AnimationShowcaseHarness.kt's creatureTile) to actually face the target it's shooting at.
There's no general mechanism for a sprite to face left/right based on which way an entity is moving
(or last moved, when stationary) or aiming/attacking -- every graphical-tile game needs this (it's
about as universal a need as ambient torch flicker), and right now each consumer would have to
reinvent the hand-flip the demo just did.

krogue-2ua's SpriteProjectile already threads a computed bearing through drawSprite's real
rotationDeg for the *projectile* case (full rotation, any angle); a walking/standing creature wants
the cheaper, far more common horizontal-only version (mirror, not rotate) that most 2D sprite games
use for their characters.
design:
Two layers, buildable independently -- same "build the primitive, let a real consumer land later"
pattern already used for SpriteProjectile before any real sprite MapPanel existed:

1. kotile: flipX/flipY at the primitive level. KotileCanvas.drawSprite already has everything
   needed -- libGDX's own TextureRegion.flip(x, y) does the actual mirroring -- just add
   flipX: Boolean = false, flipY: Boolean = false parameters so a caller doesn't need to mutate a
   region itself the way the demo just did by hand. AnimatedSpriteTile/StaticTile (kotile/tiles)
   should carry the same flag so the grid-locked drawTile path gets it too, not just free-layer
   drawSprite -- otherwise only free/pixel-space sprites could ever mirror.

2. engine: a Facing component (data-only, ADR-0003) holding the last horizontal direction moved or
   aimed -- LEFT/RIGHT only, deliberately not a full 4/8-way facing model, matching exactly what was
   asked for. MovementSystem sets it from a resolved move's horizontal delta; whatever resolves a
   ranged/thrown attack (krogue-4tn, once that lands) sets it from the attack's aim direction.
   Facing persists across ticks (doesn't reset when an entity stops moving) -- that's the "or last
   moved" requirement.

No sprite-rendering consumer exists at the engine level yet -- only the demo hand-rolls sprite
drawing (see krogue-2ua's own notes: there's no general graphical MapPanel, only
AnimationShowcaseHarness's bespoke room-building). Wiring Facing into an actual render call is out
of scope here until a real sprite MapPanel exists (rogue-jk6/krogue-tvm territory, tracked in the
korogue-rogue repo). This issue is scoped to making the mirroring *available*: the kotile flip
primitive + the Facing component/system, not a full render-path integration.
acceptance_criteria: KotileCanvas.drawSprite and AnimatedSpriteTile/StaticTile support flipping a sprite horizontally (and vertically, for symmetry with flipX) without the caller needing to mutate a TextureRegion itself, verified via existing GL-gated test conventions. A Facing component (LEFT/RIGHT) exists; MovementSystem sets it from a resolved move's horizontal delta and it persists (doesn't reset) when an entity stops moving; unit tests cover both. No behavior change for existing games/tests that don't use it.
close_reason: Implemented: kotile flipX/flipY primitive (KotileCanvas.drawSprite/drawTile, StaticTile, AnimatedSpriteTile, TileRenderer dispatch) + engine Facing component set by MovementSystem from a resolved intent's horizontal delta; demo's hand-rolled ranger flip replaced with the real primitive. Filed krogue-ea7 for the discovered follow-on gap (projectiles not light-tinted).

title: Add a VisualEffectPool for simultaneous non-gating cosmetic effects
description:
EventAnimationQueue plays exactly one sequence at a time by design -- correct for its actual job
(gate turn-advancing input on a bolt-in-flight, per ADR-0023/krogue-wuq's own doc comment). But it
gets used for cosmetic effects too (hit-flashes, floating damage numbers) that obviously need to
play *simultaneously* with each other and with the projectile, and shouldn't gate input at all.
The animation showcase demo (krogue-aqo) works around this by hand-rolling five separate
EventAnimationQueue instances (sprite/glyph projectile, sprite/glyph flash, sprite damage text) --
a real game with multiple monsters flashing at once will hit the same wall immediately and have to
reinvent the same multi-queue juggling, with no engine-provided pattern for it.

Notably, kotile's own lower-level EffectsLayer primitive (krogue-tk9) already models N-simultaneous
transient items via a plain list (spawn/update/render each independently) -- EventAnimationQueue,
built one layer up, collapsed that down to exactly one at a time. That collapse is right for
input-gating; there's just nothing engine-side for the "many independent, non-blocking, play out
on their own" case that's equally common.

Found during a design/efficiency review of the animation work (krogue-wuq, krogue-ncl, krogue-tnf,
krogue-2ua) at the user's request.
design:
A new, separate class (not a mode flag on EventAnimationQueue -- keep that one simple and focused
on its actual job): a pool of independently-timed VisualSequences with no isPlaying/gating concept
at all, mirroring EffectsLayer's own list-of-independent-items shape:

  class VisualEffectPool {
      private data class Entry(val sequence: VisualSequence, val startMs: Long)
      private val active = mutableListOf<Entry>()

      fun spawn(event: VisualEvent, nowMs: Long)
      fun update(nowMs: Long)   // drops entries whose durationMs has elapsed
      fun render(surface: TileSurface, camera: MapCamera, nowMs: Long)       // renders all active, in spawn order
      fun renderSprite(canvas: KotileCanvas, camera: MapCamera, nowMs: Long) // begin/end once, draws all active
      fun clear()
  }

Once this lands, the demo should be refactored to use one EventAnimationQueue per half (still
gating on the projectile-in-flight, unchanged) plus one shared VisualEffectPool per half for
flashes + floating text, replacing today's five hand-managed EventAnimationQueue instances --
proving the new primitive actually removes the workaround it's meant to replace, not just adding
an unused class alongside it.
acceptance_criteria: VisualEffectPool exists, is unit-testable the same way EventAnimationQueueTest is (fake TileSurface/MapCamera, no GL), and correctly plays N simultaneously-spawned sequences of different durations without any gating semantics. The animation showcase demo is refactored to use it in place of its current 3-4 workaround queues for non-gating effects, and still passes its own visual verification.
close_reason: Added VisualEffectPool (spawn/update/render/renderSprite/clear, no gating). Demo refactored to use one pool per half in place of its 3 workaround queues, verified visually. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: VisualEvent: open it up to match ecs.Event's precedent, not a closed sealed hierarchy
description:
VisualEvent is a sealed interface with five fixed variants (HitFlash, DeathFade, Projectile,
SpriteProjectile, FloatingText), dispatched via an exhaustive `when` in VisualSequence.kt's
`fun VisualEvent.toSequence(): VisualSequence`. A game wanting a new visual effect (a beam, an
area burst, a screen shake) has no seam -- it would have to fork the engine to add a case to that
when.

This is inconsistent with the engine's own precedent for "events": com.sletmoe.korogue.ecs.Event
(ADR-0010) is an OPEN marker interface -- EntityDamaged/EntityDied/ZoneChanged/ItemPickedUp each
implement it directly, and EventBus.subscribe<T> dispatches by concrete class, not a closed `when`.
A game can define and publish its own Event today with zero engine changes. VisualEvent should
work the same way; right now it's the "closed struct" ADR-0014/ADR-0015 explicitly call out as the
anti-pattern to avoid ("would a game designer plausibly want this to work differently?" -> yes,
obviously, for visual effects).

Found during a design/efficiency review of the animation work (krogue-wuq, krogue-tnf, krogue-2ua,
krogue-ncl) at the user's request.
design:
Mirror ecs.Event's shape exactly rather than inventing a new pattern (id-registry would be the
wrong fit here -- unlike LightValueCalculator/BehaviorStrategy, a VisualEvent instance carries
per-occurrence data, not "which policy to use in general"; self-contained dispatch is the right
shape, same as Event already does):

  interface VisualEvent {
      fun toSequence(): VisualSequence
  }

Change `sealed interface VisualEvent` -> `interface VisualEvent`. Each built-in variant
(HitFlash/DeathFade/Projectile/SpriteProjectile/FloatingText) implements `toSequence()` itself
(e.g. `override fun toSequence() = HitFlashSequence(this)`) instead of being matched in a central
`when`. Delete the free `fun VisualEvent.toSequence()` extension function entirely -- there's
nothing left to dispatch centrally once each event supplies its own conversion.

A game then defines its own VisualEvent + VisualSequence pair with zero engine changes:

  data class ScreenShake(val amplitudePx: Float, val durationMs: Long) : VisualEvent {
      override fun toSequence(): VisualSequence = ScreenShakeSequence(this)
  }

EventAnimationQueue/EventAnimationQueueTest should need no changes (they already deal in the
VisualEvent/VisualSequence interfaces, never the sealed hierarchy itself) -- confirm this holds
once the change lands. The five *Sequence private classes can stay private in VisualSequence.kt
(each VisualEvent's toSequence() override still lives there, adjacent to its owning data class, or
move alongside it in VisualEvent.kt -- whichever reads cleaner once written).
acceptance_criteria: VisualEvent is a plain (non-sealed) interface with an abstract toSequence(): VisualSequence method; every built-in variant implements it directly; the central when-based dispatch function is gone. A game-defined VisualEvent implementation (not in the sealed hierarchy) can be enqueued into EventAnimationQueue and played without any engine source changes -- demonstrate this with a test. All existing VisualEvent/EventAnimationQueue/VisualSequence tests still pass unchanged in behavior.
close_reason: VisualEvent is now a plain (non-sealed) interface with self-dispatching toSequence(), mirroring ecs.Event's precedent. Test proves a game-defined event/sequence pair works with zero engine changes. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: Polish AnimationShowcaseHarness as an exemplar animation-authoring example
description:
AnimationShowcaseHarness.kt (and its DawnLike*Tiles.kt helpers under
demo/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/korogue/demo/animation/) grew iteratively across the whole

Once the epic itself is done, do a dedicated pass to make this file genuinely good *reference*

would want to read and copy from, not just working demo scratch code. Concretely: re-check
section ordering and grouping (lighting vs. torches vs. projectiles vs. lifecycle), tighten/trim
comments that reference session-specific back-and-forth rather than durable rationale, verify

No functional/behavioral changes expected, just clarity and organization. Tests + ktlint stay green.
close_reason: Reorganized AnimationShowcaseHarness.kt into clearer sections (shared lighting, both-halves combat script, sprite half, glyph half, lifecycle) and trimmed narrative-history comments to state current design rules. DawnLike*Tiles.kt helper files reviewed -- already clean, no changes needed. No behavior change, verified via snapshot. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: Free-form pixel-space projectile animation (sprite EffectsLayer, directional)
description:
VisualEvent.Projectile / ProjectileSequence (engine/presentation) only ever render through
TileSurface.put — writing a glyph/color at an interpolated, round-to-nearest-cell position. There
is no sprite/pixel-space consumer anywhere in the engine or demo: EffectsLayer (kotile's
free-moving-overlay primitive, krogue-tk9) is never referenced outside kotile itself, and
krogue-m05 (drawSprite rotation support) — built explicitly "for directional projectiles" per its
own issue — has never been consumed by anything. VisualSequence.kt's own doc comment already
frames krogue-tnf as "distinct from the free (pixel-space drawSprite) projectile mode," implying
that free/sprite mode already exists — it doesn't; this issue is that missing mode.

This is the SPRITE-side counterpart to krogue-tnf's grid-snapped ASCII cell-walk: true sub-pixel
free-form motion (not rounded to the nearest cell) with a heading-derived rotation via kotile's
existing rotationTowards helper, drawn through EffectsLayer/drawSprite instead of TileSurface.
design:
VisualEvent.Projectile currently carries only `glyph: Char` — no sprite/tile reference, tint, or
rotation, because the whole event model was built glyph-first. Needs either: (a) a new sealed
VisualEvent variant (e.g. SpriteProjectile) carrying a Tile/TextureRegion + tint, parallel to the
existing glyph-only Projectile, or (b) extending Projectile with an optional sprite payload. Lean
towards (a) — keeps the ASCII path's simplicity, matches how tnf is framed as a separate mode
rather than a Projectile field toggle.

EventAnimationQueue/VisualSequence.render() takes a TileSurface + MapCamera — both ASCII/glyph
abstractions. A sprite-space sequence needs a different render seam (an EffectsLayer/KotileCanvas
target, not TileSurface), since no pixel-space equivalent of TileSurface exists at the engine
level yet. There is also no general engine-level graphical map renderer to consume this from real
gameplay (the only sprite rendering that exists anywhere is krogue-aqo's AnimationShowcaseHarness,
which hand-rolls its own room/lighting) — that's a separate, larger gap (see rogue-jk6 in the
korogue-rogue repo for the graphical-tileset work motivating it). Scope this issue to the
presentation-side machinery (event + sequence + EffectsLayer-driving render call) and let
krogue-aqo's showcase be the first real consumer, the same way tnf's ASCII stepper will plug into
TileSurface/MapPanel — don't block this on a general graphical MapPanel existing.

Rotation: use kotile's existing rotationTowards(velX, velY) helper (EffectsLayer.kt, krogue-m05)
computed from (to - from), so the sprite visibly points along its direction of travel.
acceptance_criteria:
A sprite/tile travels smoothly (true sub-pixel interpolation, not cell-rounded) from a source to a
target pixel position over its event's duration, rotated to face its direction of travel via
kotile's rotationTowards, rendered through EffectsLayer/drawSprite — not TileSurface. Exercised at
minimum by krogue-aqo's showcase demo (its sprite-side projectile, alongside tnf's ASCII one).
Presentation-only: never touches game state or saves.
notes: Implemented: VisualEvent.SpriteProjectile (new sealed variant: from/to/region/tint/durationMs/nativeBearingDeg) + SpriteProjectileSequence (VisualSequence.kt) -- true sub-pixel linear interpolation via KotileCanvas.drawSprite, rotated via kotile's rotationTowards(toPx-fromPx) minus nativeBearingDeg (so source art not drawn facing +X still ends up pointing the right way). VisualSequence gained a second entry point, renderSprite(canvas, camera, elapsedMs), defaulting to a no-op -- a sequence overrides render() (glyph/TileSurface), renderSprite() (pixel-space/KotileCanvas), or both; existing HitFlash/DeathFade/glyph-Projectile sequences are unaffected (still only override render()). EventAnimationQueue gained a matching renderSprite(canvas, camera, nowMs), self-contained (canvas.begin()/end()) like TileRenderer.render(). Deliberately bypasses EffectsLayer's own spawn/update(dtMs) state machine -- it's stateful (accumulates via velocity each frame) where wuq's whole sequence model is stateless (recomputes purely from elapsedMs), so directly calling canvas.drawSprite (the same primitive EffectsLayer itself calls) fits better than adapting to a mismatched state model. Exercised end-to-end by krogue-aqo's showcase demo's sprite-side arrow, verified via a temporary snapshot that the rotation faces the correct travel direction.
close_reason: Sprite/pixel-space mode implemented: VisualEvent.SpriteProjectile + SpriteProjectileSequence + VisualSequence.renderSprite()/EventAnimationQueue.renderSprite(), wired into krogue-aqo's showcase. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: Light-tint occupant foreground (glyph color), not just background
description:
MapPanel.backgroundAt already tints an occupant's BACKGROUND by the lit cell's light value (color*intensity), and now (krogue-ncl) that background flickers correctly too. But the occupant's FOREGROUND -- the glyph's own color, from occupantRenderer's default (draws Renderable.color unchanged) -- is never light-tinted at all, flicker or not. A creature standing in a dim/flickering torch's circle keeps its full, undimmed color while the floor around it darkens, which looks wrong (pre-existing asymmetry, not introduced by krogue-ncl -- that issue's DESIGN section flagged it as a 'secondary gap' explicitly out of its own acceptance criteria).

Fix: extend occupantRenderer's default (or add a new seam) to also multiply the occupant's Renderable.color by the same lit tint (and flicker factor) backgroundAt already computes for that cell, so a creature dims/flickers consistently with the terrain it's standing on. Sprite-path light tinting (once a graphical tileset exists, krogue-jk6/tvm) is separately out of scope here -- this is the ASCII glyph-color path only.
acceptance_criteria: An occupant standing on a dim or flickering lit cell shows a correspondingly dim/flickering glyph color, not its full undimmed Renderable color.
close_reason: MapPanel now light-tints occupant foreground the same way it already tinted background (flicker included), via a shared litColor helper. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: kotile: rotation support for drawSprite/EffectsLayer (directional projectiles)
description:
KotileCanvas.drawSprite(pxX, pxY, region, w, h, tint) has no rotation parameter -- it's a plain batch.draw(region, pxX, glY, w, h), libGDX SpriteBatch's non-rotated overload. EffectsLayer's Effect (krogue-tk9) inherits this: a sprite can move and fade but can't be drawn rotated.

This blocks a directional projectile that uses source art drawn at a single fixed angle -- e.g. DawnLike's Items/Ammo.png arrow tiles (see demo/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/korogue/demo/animation/DawnLikeAmmoTiles.kt, picked for the animation showcase krogue-aqo) are drawn at a fixed NE-pointing 45 degree diagonal; flying one south, west, or any angle other than its native diagonal needs the sprite rotated to match its actual velocity vector, which nothing in kotile can do today.

Fix: add a rotation parameter (radians or degrees) to KotileCanvas.drawSprite, threaded through to libGDX SpriteBatch's rotated draw overload (draw(region, x, y, originX, originY, width, height, scaleX, scaleY, rotation)), and let EffectsLayer's Effect carry an optional rotation (static, or derived from velocity direction each frame).
acceptance_criteria: A free-layer sprite (EffectsLayer Effect or a direct drawSprite call) can be drawn rotated to an arbitrary angle; an arrow-style projectile fired in any direction renders pointing along its actual velocity, not its source art's fixed angle.
notes:
Implemented: KotileCanvas.drawSprite gained rotationDeg: Float = 0f (screen/content-pixel convention: 0=unrotated, positive=clockwise on screen, matching atan2(dy,dx) on a Y-down velocity -- negated internally before reaching libGDX SpriteBatch's rotated draw overload, which is counter-clockwise in its Y-up GL world; rotation pivots on the sprite's center). Effect gained a matching rotationDeg field (plain/static like tint, NOT auto-derived from velocity -- EffectsLayer.update() doesn't touch it, caller sets it once at spawn since Effect motion is linear/constant-velocity). Added a small rotationTowards(velX,velY) utility for the common case. EffectsLayer.render() now threads effect.rotationDeg through.

Verified the Y-up/Y-down sign conversion empirically before trusting it: this machine has no DISPLAY env var so the headless-GL integration test suite (RenderingIntegrationTest) is skipped locally -- built a throwaway kotile:demo rotationHarness (kept, matches the repo's existing *Harness convention for macOS-safe visual verification) rendering a 4-quadrant sprite at 0/90/180/270 degrees and confirmed by eye that positive angles rotate clockwise (TL->TR->BR->BL cycle) exactly as documented, before writing the real pixel-assertion tests.

Added: RotationTowardsTest.kt (pure logic, runs everywhere), two new HeadlessGl-gated tests in RenderingIntegrationTest.kt (drawSprite rotation direction; EffectsLayer threads rotationDeg through) -- these are skipped on this machine but will run in CI/on a machine with DISPLAY set. Confirmed no breaking changes: grepped all Effect(...) construction call sites, both existing ones use named args so inserting rotationDeg before lifetimeMs in the constructor doesn't break them.

Scope note: rotation is NOT available on the StaticTile/SpriteTileRenderer grid-drawn path (drawTile), only drawSprite/EffectsLayer (free/pixel-space) -- matches the issue's stated scope. krogue-aqo's showcase arrow is currently drawn via the grid path (StaticTile), so it does NOT automatically start rotating from this change alone; converting it to an EffectsLayer Effect to actually use rotation is follow-through work for krogue-4tn (wiring a real projectile trigger) or krogue-aqo itself, not this issue.

Full test suite + ktlint clean (./gradlew test ktlintCheck, all modules).
close_reason: Rotation support added to KotileCanvas.drawSprite and EffectsLayer.Effect, verified both empirically (visual harness) and via headless-GL pixel-assertion tests. Wiring a live projectile to actually use it is follow-up scope (krogue-4tn).

title: Animation showcase demo: split sprite/glyph room
description:
A standalone demo scene purpose-built to develop and visually prove out the animation work (krogue-wuq and its still-open siblings) side by side, rather than relying on the roguelike demo's incidental combat.

Scene: a single room, split down the middle. The left half is drawn with graphical (sprite/tile-sheet) tiles; the right half with glyph (ASCII) tiles — same room, two rendering paths, visible at once for direct comparison. Torches on the walls on both sides demonstrate ambient light flicker (krogue-ncl for the glyph side's wall-clock light-field modulation; the sprite side needs krogue-2ur's per-frame tint so a sprite torch can flicker the same way an AnimatedAsciiTile does). One creature on each side periodically shoots a projectile at another creature, which flashes on impact (krogue-wuq's EventAnimationQueue: HitFlash already works today). The left (sprite) side's projectile travels via wuq's existing free-form linear interpolation; the right (glyph) side's projectile uses the grid-snapped, blocker-stopping cell walk from krogue-tnf once it lands, so the same event type visibly demonstrates both render modes at once.

Not gameplay: no player input driving it beyond maybe pausing/restarting the loop that fires projectiles on a timer — it's a proving ground, scripted or looping on its own.

Design notes (for whoever picks this up): kotile:demo already has a 'harness' pattern (RenderHarness.kt, EffectsHarness.kt, UiHarness.kt, etc. under kotile/demo/src/main/kotlin, each its own small ApplicationAdapter + main()) for exactly this kind of isolated feature showcase — likely the right home, though this demo needs engine-level types (EventAnimationQueue, VisualEvent, CombatSystem-adjacent snapshot events) that kotile itself doesn't depend on, so it may need to live under :demo instead (a new Game subclass alongside MyGame.kt, with its own entry point) or as a new small module. Whoever starts this should settle that placement question first (check whether kotile:demo's harnesses are picked via separate Gradle run tasks or an env/arg switch, and follow that precedent within :demo). Does not need real ECS combat/AI -- a scripted timer firing at two fixed 'creatures' is enough to exercise the animation machinery.

Can be scaffolded now with what already exists (wuq's HitFlash + free-form Projectile, MapPanel-style camera/decorate pattern or a bespoke minimal one); the glyph-side grid-snapped projectile and both torches' flicker slot in as krogue-tnf/2ur/ncl land, so this issue doesn't need to block on them -- linked as related, not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: A single runnable demo shows a room split into sprite-tile (left) and glyph-tile (right) halves; both sides show a projectile animating from one creature to another with a hit-flash on impact (left free-form, right grid-snapped once tnf lands); torches on both sides flicker ambiently once ncl/2ur land. Running it requires no player input to see the full loop.
notes: Closing out: hit-flash on impact is now implemented on both sides (sprite side re-tints the scorpion via EventAnimationQueue.currentEvent rather than an opaque overlay; glyph side uses HitFlashSequence's existing glyph render), plus a bonus floating '-4' damage number on the sprite side (new VisualEvent.FloatingText). All of this issue's acceptance criteria are now met: split room, both sides show a synchronized projectile (sprite: krogue-2ua's true sub-pixel SpriteProjectile; glyph: krogue-tnf's grid-snapped path-stepping Projectile) with hit-flash on impact, torches flicker ambiently (krogue-ncl/2ur), and the whole loop runs with no player input (a scripted timer). See krogue-tnf/krogue-2ua/krogue-ncl/krogue-2ur for implementation detail on each piece. krogue-4vu (polish pass) and krogue-0w3/krogue-4tn (related, separate scope) remain open as followups.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met: split sprite/glyph room, synchronized projectiles on both real render modes (krogue-tnf grid-snapped + krogue-2ua sprite-space) with hit-flash on impact and a floating damage number, ambient torch flicker (krogue-ncl/2ur), no player input required. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: Don't gate input on off-screen/unperceived event-animation sequences
description: EventAnimationQueue.isPlaying (krogue-wuq) gates MyGame.onTick regardless of whether the sequence actually draws anything. A HitFlash/DeathFade enqueued for a cell outside the map viewport or not perceived by the player still plays its full duration and still pauses the world -- the player gets an unexplained freeze from combat they can't see, and (separately) a flash can render on an unperceived cell, revealing hidden combat, since putAt() does no fog/perception check. Fix options: only enqueue a VisualEvent when its position is in the observer's current Perceived/viewport (checked in MyGame.wireAnimations, which already has access to the world), and/or have EventAnimationQueue not gate input for a sequence it knows will draw nothing this frame. Found during krogue-wuq's post-implementation review (2026-07-13).
acceptance_criteria: Combat damage/death happening off-screen or on an unperceived cell does not pause player input, and does not draw a flash/fade the player couldn't otherwise see.
notes: Fixed via the enqueue-time filter option (not modifying EventAnimationQueue itself, which stays presentation-primitive/perception-agnostic): MyGame.wireAnimations() now checks a new playerPerceives(at) helper (world.ecs.get(playerId)?.get<Perceived>()?.sees(x,y)) before enqueueing a HitFlash or DeathFade -- an event whose position isn't currently perceived by the player is simply never enqueued, so it neither gates input nor draws a flash the player couldn't otherwise see. Both acceptance criteria satisfied by the same single check. No zone check needed beyond cell perception: combat only resolves in the player's currently-simulated zone (ADR-0008), so a perceived position is inherently in the right zone already. No test added -- :demo has no test directory/precedent (MyGame is an application entry point tied to Gdx/GL, tested via manual/harness verification elsewhere in the repo, not unit tests); this is a small, direct fix consistent with that boundary. Full test suite + ktlint clean.
close_reason: Visual events are now only enqueued when the player currently perceives their cell, fixing both the input-gating-on-invisible-combat bug and the hidden-combat-reveal bug in one check.

title: Wire VisualEvent.Projectile to a real ranged/thrown attack trigger
description: krogue-wuq's EventAnimationQueue ships a Projectile VisualEvent + sequence (linear interpolation, free-form render mode) but nothing in CombatSystem or the demo triggers one — combat today is melee-only bump attacks (EntityDamaged/EntityDied), which drive HitFlash/DeathFade instead. Once a ranged or thrown attack exists (bow, thrown potion, etc.), publish a suitable game event carrying source/target cells and enqueue a VisualEvent.Projectile from a presentation-side subscriber, the same pattern MyGame.wireAnimations already uses for hit/death. See krogue-tnf for the grid-snapped (Bresenham, blocker-stopping) ASCII render mode this can graduate to.
acceptance_criteria: A ranged/thrown attack in the demo (or an example game) visibly animates a projectile from source to target via EventAnimationQueue before the next game step is shown.
close_reason: Wired a minimal ranged-attack trigger into the real ECS: RangedAttacker component + RangedAttackSystem (engine) checks LOS/range beyond melee and emits AttackIntent directly (CombatSystem already resolves damage distance-agnostically), publishing RangedAttackFired. BehaviorSystem gained a guard so it doesn't also move an entity that just fired. MyGame.kt (the real playable :demo game, not the scripted AnimationShowcaseHarness) registers the system, adds an 'archer' monster archetype, and extends wireAnimations() to enqueue VisualEvent.GlyphProjectile on RangedAttackFired -- gated on the player perceiving the shooter, same as existing HitFlash/DeathFade gating. Also registered RangedAttacker and the previously-missed Facing (krogue-csc) in GameModule's persistable component list. Full gate + smoke-booted the real demo.

title: Grid-snapped projectile animation (cell-stepped bolt, Brogue-style)
description: An ASCII/grid projectile that advances one CELL at a time along its trajectory (Brogue-style bolt/arrow), drawn snapped to the tile grid via drawTile on a transient overlay, as opposed to the free-form sub-tile pixel motion of the tk9 EffectsLayer. A game event (bolt/arrow/thrown item from A to B) becomes a wall-clock sequence that steps a glyph through each cell of the line in turn, clearing the prior cell, briefly gating input until it lands. This is the GRID-SNAPPED counterpart to tk9's pixel-space free projectiles.
design: Home: the wuq event-animation queue (a bolt's flight is in wuq's scope); this is wuq's ASCII/grid RENDER MODE, distinct from the free (pixel-space drawSprite) projectile mode and from ambient per-tile animation. wuq should support both projectile modes. Needs two pieces: (1) an ordered cell-line traversal (Bresenham / supercover line) yielding the trajectory cells origin->target and stopping at the first blocker -- NOTE nothing existing provides this: LineOfSightCalculator returns a boolean FOV Grid and SymmetricShadowCaster is quadrant FOV, neither an ordered path, so a small new line-walk utility is required (engine/algorithms). (2) a wall-clock stepper (N ms per cell) that draws the projectile glyph into the current cell each frame on a transient top z-layer / grid Layer, clearing the previous cell, input-gated by wuq until landing. Presentation-only, not saved. Reuses AsciiTileWindow z-layers / drawTile. Faithful-port note: match the target game's bolt speed and path rule.
acceptance_criteria: A bolt event animates a glyph stepping cell-by-cell along the grid line from source to target on the wall-clock, stopping at a blocker, gating input until it lands, leaving no residue afterward; game state and saves untouched; runs on the ASCII grid path via drawTile.
notes: Implemented: bresenhamLine/lineOfCellsStoppingAtBlocker (engine/algorithms/geometry/BresenhamLine.kt, 11 unit tests) is the ordered cell-line walk with blocker-stopping this issue's DESIGN section said didn't exist yet. VisualEvent.Projectile gained an optional path: List<Vector2Int>? field -- when set, ProjectileSequence (VisualSequence.kt) steps through it cell-by-cell (one per durationMs/path.size) instead of the free-form lerp-and-round, exactly the 'layered on top of this same event type' design already noted in Projectile's own doc comment. Input-gating comes for free from EventAnimationQueue.isPlaying (pre-existing, generic to any sequence).
