Exercised end-to-end by krogue-aqo's showcase demo (AnimationShowcaseHarness's glyph-side dash), including finding and fixing a real residue bug: RenderLayer.OVERLAY's z-band (3) is separate from the terrain z=0, so a moving glyph left old cells behind it until the whole window is cleared each frame (window.clear(), which MyGame.drawFrame already does but the demo harness didn't -- fixed there). The demo's own blocker predicate is always-false (no real Zone in a scripted room), so blocker-stopping itself is verified by BresenhamLineTest, not visually.
close_reason: Grid-snapped mode implemented: bresenhamLine/lineOfCellsStoppingAtBlocker utility + VisualEvent.Projectile.path + ProjectileSequence cell-stepping, wired into krogue-aqo's showcase. Tests + ktlint clean.

title: Presentation-side light flicker: wall-clock modulation of the cast light field
description: The engine already casts diminishing light: LightEmitter (color/radius/calculatorId) + DiminishingLightValueCalculator + LightingSystem recompute zone.lightMap each tick, and MapPanel.terrainCell renders it as a per-cell tint (normalizedColor * intensity) gated by shadowcast FOV. A character with a torch already produces a steady diminishing circle. MISSING: flicker. Because lightMap is derived state recomputed once per game TICK from static emitter params, the cast circle is constant between ticks. Add a presentation-side, wall-clock modulation of the RENDERED light (per-emitter intensity/radius/color jitter) layered over the tick-computed lightMap, so a torch's circle flickers smoothly at frame rate without consuming turns or touching game state/saves.
design: lightMap is derived game state, recomputed per tick and excluded from saves (SaveModel). Flicker must live on the wall-clock presentation axis (ADR-0023), NOT the tick axis: recomputing the whole field every frame is costly and blurs the game/presentation line. Approach: a presentation stage multiplies the lit tint (MapPanel.terrainCell already computes tint = normalizedColor * intensity) by a per-source wall-clock flicker factor before drawing, with a per-emitter phase so multiple torches flicker independently. Likely a small flicker descriptor on LightEmitter (amplitude/speed/seed) that only presentation reads, or a presentation-side registry keyed by emitter. SECONDARY GAP: occupants are not currently light-tinted (only terrain is); extend the occupantRenderer/backgroundAt path so creatures within the circle dim and flicker too. Sprite-path light tinting is future (graphical tileset rogue-jk6 / tvm). Shares the wall-clock axis with ambient animation and wuq.
acceptance_criteria: A torch-bearing entity's cast light visibly flickers on the wall-clock, independent per source, without advancing game time or altering saves; with zero flicker params the circle is steady (current behaviour); terrain tinting path unchanged when flicker is absent.
notes:
Implemented: LightFlicker (engine/algorithms/lighting/LightFlicker.kt, @Serializable) -- static amplitude/periodMs/seed config, factorAt(elapsedMs) a pure sine-based intensity multiplier around 1.0. LightEmitter gained flicker: LightFlicker? = null (opt-in, trailing defaulted field -- backward compatible, existing saves/callers unaffected).

Deliberately did NOT recompute the whole tick-computed zone.lightMap per frame (the DESIGN section explicitly flagged this as a cost to avoid) -- instead MapPanel (the renderer) gathers just the small list of flicker-configured LightEmitters in the current zone once per draw() call, and for each rendered cell finds the NEAREST one that reaches it (within its own radius), multiplying that source's wall-clock factor into the cell's existing lightMap intensity. This is an approximation of 'true independent per-source blending' for cells lit by multiple overlapping flickering sources (picks nearest rather than re-blending all contributions) -- documented inline as a deliberate tradeoff; a cell lit by only one source (the common case) is unaffected by the approximation. MapPanel gained elapsedMsProvider: () -> Long = { 0L } (mirrors the animationClockMs pattern from krogue-wuq); MyGame wires elapsedMsProvider = { animationClockMs }, reusing the field wuq already introduced. terrainCell AND backgroundAt (occupant background) both threaded through so an occupant's background flickers consistently with the floor beneath it.

Acceptance criteria verified via tests: LightFlickerTest.kt (9 pure-logic cases: range bounds, periodicity, peak/trough, seed phase-shift, amplitude=0, non-positive period, negative elapsedMs). MapPanelTest.kt (4 new cases): flicker modulates intensity over wall-clock time; NO flicker-configured emitter -> zero elapsedMs sensitivity (regression, matches 'terrain tinting path unchanged when flicker is absent'); flicker doesn't reach cells outside the emitter's radius; occupant background flickers too.

Filed krogue-0w3 (related, not blocking) for the 'secondary gap' the issue's DESIGN section flagged but excluded from its own acceptance criteria: occupant FOREGROUND (glyph color) still isn't light-tinted at all today, flicker or not -- only backgroundAt was already tinted pre-existing, this issue just made that tinting flicker too.

Full test suite + ktlint clean, all modules.
close_reason: Torch-borne light now flickers on the wall-clock, independent per nearby source (nearest-source approximation, documented), never touching game state/ticks/saves. Terrain and occupant backgrounds both covered; occupant foreground tinting filed separately (krogue-0w3, pre-existing gap this issue's own scope excluded).

title: Status-driven representation-override filter (confusion scramble)
description: A sustained, game-state-driven presentation filter: while a status such as confusion is active on the rendered observer, the on-screen representation of items and monsters cycles among a scrambled set (Brogue-style), reverting when the status ends. Distinct from ambient per-tile animation (authored frames on a tile instance) and from the wuq event-animation queue (one-shot sequences bound to a single event): this is a cross-cutting FILTER over many entities, bounded by a status duration, driven on the wall-clock (presentation) axis. Applies to both ASCII and (future) sprite representations.
design: MapPanel already exposes an occupantRenderer seam that remaps a perceived occupant's glyph/foreground at render time (or returns null to suppress). A confusion filter drives that seam: while the confusion status is active on the observer being rendered, remap each perceived occupant's glyph/fg to a wall-clock-cycled pick from a scramble set (e.g. a shuffle of other visible entities' representations), reverting on expiry. Presentation-only: no game-state mutation, not saved. Frame content is DYNAMIC (a runtime shuffle), unlike authored ambient frames. Shares the wall-clock presentation axis with ambient animation and wuq (ADR-0023); consumes the status-effect system. Faithful-Rogue note: Rogue's confusion cycles monster letters; keep the scramble rule matching the target game.
acceptance_criteria: While confusion is active on the observer, perceived occupants cycle representations on the wall-clock and revert when it expires; game state and saves are untouched; implemented via the MapPanel occupantRenderer seam; works for ASCII (sprite when that path exists).

title: Per-frame tint for sprite animation (ambient shimmer parity)
description: AnimatedSpriteTile cycles TextureRegion frames but applies a single constant tint; AnimationFrame<TextureRegion> carries no per-frame tint. This blocks tint-based ambient effects (crystal-wall shimmer, glow) on the SPRITE path that the ASCII path gets for free, since AnimatedAsciiTile frames are AsciiTileDescriptors carrying fg/bg color. Add an optional per-frame tint so sprite tiles can shimmer by cycling color, giving ambient animation full ASCII/sprite parity.
design: ASCII: AnimatedAsciiTile frames are AsciiTileDescriptor(glyph,fg,bg) so color cycling is native. Sprite: AnimationFrame holds only content(region)+durationMs, and AnimatedSpriteTile.tint is one constant multiplied at draw. Option: give AnimationFrame an optional tint override (default null = use the tile's constant tint), and have AnimatedSpriteTile expose the active frame's effective tint so the renderer multiplies it with entry.tint. Fully backward compatible: existing single-tint animations unchanged. kotile-level; no engine change.
acceptance_criteria: A sprite tile shimmers by cycling per-frame tints; existing constant-tint AnimatedSpriteTile animations render identically; per-frame tint defaults to the tile tint when unset.
notes:
Implemented per the issue's own design: AnimationFrame<T> gained tint: Color? = null (generic, but only meaningful for AnimatedSpriteTile frames -- AsciiTileDescriptor already carries its own per-frame fg/bg, so ASCII frames just leave it null/unused). Tile interface gained fun tintFor(elapsedMs: Long): Color = tint (default preserves old behavior for any non-overriding implementation). AnimatedSpriteTile overrides tintFor to fold a frame's override into the tile's constant tint: frame.tint == null -> returns tint unchanged (constant-tint animations behave identically); frame.tint != null -> returns tint.cpy().mul(frameTint) (composable: a status-effect constant recolor and a per-frame shimmer multiply together, matching 'defaults to the tile tint when unset' from acceptance criteria exactly). TileRenderer.renderGrid's Tile branch updated from entry.tint to entry.tintFor(elapsedMs) -- the one call site that needed to change; StaticTile's branch and Effect (unrelated, doesn't implement Tile) untouched.

Tests: extended AnimatedSpriteTileTest.kt with 5 new pure-logic cases (default-to-tile-tint, override-with-white-tile-tint, multiply-with-non-white-tile-tint, mixed frames, no-mutation-of-inputs) -- didn't need empirical harness verification this time since Color.mul is a standard non-directional operation, unlike krogue-m05's rotation sign which genuinely needed eyeballing. Added a headless-GL integration test in RenderingIntegrationTest.kt proving the RENDERER actually calls tintFor (not just that the class computes it correctly in isolation) -- skipped locally (no DISPLAY) but will run in CI.

Not wired into the existing showcase (krogue-aqo): its torch already animates via full region-swap (Decor0/Decor1), a valid and already-working approach: this capability is additive, for future ambient effects (e.g. a crystal wall glow) that don't have multiple pre-drawn art frames, not a required upgrade to what's already there.

Full test suite + ktlint clean, all modules.
close_reason: AnimationFrame/Tile/AnimatedSpriteTile/TileRenderer updated to support per-frame tint, giving sprite tiles the same shimmer capability AsciiTileDescriptor already had natively. Verified via unit tests plus a headless-GL renderer-wiring test.

title: MapPanel: remembered-occupant support (draw unperceived occupants at last-seen cell)
description:
Split from krogue-qrc (the heavy, risky half). drawOccupants() early-continues on any unperceived non-observer entity (MapPanel.kt:118), so a game cannot keep an out-of-view occupant drawn at its last-seen cell — the occupant analogue of terrain fog. Supporting this requires the occupant pass to also consider UNPERCEIVED in-zone entities (a change to the iteration set), plus a decision on who owns last-seen state.

Consumer: rogue-blv (item memory) — Rogue keeps a floor item/gold glyph drawn at its last-seen cell after you leave the room.

DEFERRED until krogue-a01 (render-time seam) and krogue-ho4 (camera helper) land, then REASSESS whether this is even needed: with a public camera helper the port can likely keep its own remembered-item overlay (game owns the last-seen store anyway per the policy-free stance), which may make engine-side unperceived iteration unnecessary. Only build this if the overlay approach proves to duplicate real engine logic beyond camera origin.
design: If built: engine stays policy-free — do NOT store last-seen glyph/pos in the engine (that over-fits Rogue's cell-holds-last-glyph model). Prefer: engine invokes the occupant seam for in-zone occupants including unperceived ones and lets the game gate on its own memory; remembered draws gate to !perceived cells so they naturally layer UNDER live perceived occupants. Watch per-frame cost of visiting all in-zone entities. Reuses the krogue-a01 seam shape and the krogue-ho4 camera helper.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) a documented decision that the overlay approach suffices and this is closed as not-needed, OR (b) MapPanel lets a game draw a remembered occupant at its last-seen cell while unperceived, layered under live occupants, with no Rogue memory model baked into the engine and existing tests unaffected.
close_reason: Not needed — do rogue-blv game-side (acceptance option (a)). Walked the sole consumer (rogue-blv, item memory) against the post-a01/ho4 code: a game-side overlay Widget in korogue-rogue expresses it fully with public API — MapCamera.centeredOn (ho4) for camera math, the port's own fogFor Grid<Boolean> for memory, ECS for perceived/entities. Layering needs no engine change: remembered items only draw in !perceived cells and MapPanel draws nothing live there, while a perceived item is drawn by MapPanel's normal occupant pass (items are Position+Renderable+ZoneMember) — the two paths are mutually exclusive by perception state, so no z-fight regardless of layer. Remembered background is a one-line Rogue-specific policy the overlay picks — exactly the cell-remembers-its-glyph model the bead said to keep OUT of the engine. Building 7tx would add a per-frame full-entity scan and bake that policy into MapPanel to serve one already-expressible consumer, failing the promote-on-second-consumer bar that justified a01/ho4. Reopen only if a second, genuinely-unperceived-iteration consumer appears.

title: MapPanel: extract shared camera-origin helper to de-dupe viewport math
description:
Split from krogue-qrc (Q3). MapPanel computes the viewport origin privately (MapPanel.kt:68-69: originX/originY = clamp of focus - surface/2 to zone bounds). Any game-side overlay that wants to draw into the same viewport must re-derive that exact math — the korogue-rogue port's revealItems already copy-pastes it, and it silently drifts if MapPanel's clamping changes. Extract a tiny shared helper (e.g. MapCamera) that maps zone<->screen coords given focus + surface + zone bounds, and have MapPanel use it internally. This is the concrete, existing duplication today and is orthogonal to any occupant seam.

Why first: it de-risks krogue-b02 — with a public camera helper, a game can maintain a remembered-occupant/item OVERLAY without engine-side unperceived iteration, so it may show that b02's heavier iteration change isn't needed at all.
design: Small value type / helper that owns the origin clamp and zone<->screen conversion; MapPanel delegates to it (no behavior change). Public so port overlays (revealItems) reuse it instead of re-deriving. No occupant/memory policy here.
acceptance_criteria: A shared camera-origin helper exists and MapPanel uses it internally with no rendering behavior change (existing MapPanelTest passes); the port's revealItems can consume it instead of re-deriving originX/originY.
close_reason: Added MapCamera (engine/ui): owns the origin clamp + zone<->screen conversion MapPanel inlined; MapPanel now delegates to MapCamera.centeredOn with no behavior change. Public so port overlays (revealItems) reuse it instead of re-deriving originX/originY. MapCameraTest pins the clamping.

title: MapPanel: render-time occupant transform seam (perceived occupants)
description:
Split from krogue-qrc (the cheap, safe half). drawOccupants() hardcodes renderable.glyph/color (MapPanel.kt:124-131). Add a narrow, game-supplied occupant seam invoked in the existing occupant pass that can remap or suppress how a *currently-perceived* occupant is drawn, given at least { entity/renderable, tile, perceived=true }. Return the glyph+fg to draw (bg stays engine-computed via backgroundAt so it can't desync from the terrain tint underneath), or null = don't draw. No change to the iteration set: this pass still only visits perceived (or observer) entities. This is a pure render-time transform — no memory, no unperceived iteration.

Consumer: rogue-1st (hallucination visuals) rerolls every VISIBLE monster/object glyph each turn — exactly a render-time transform of already-perceived occupants, so this half fully unblocks it.
design: Engine owns mechanism, game owns policy (same line rememberedRenderer draws). Seam defaults to today's behavior (pass renderable through unchanged) so existing games/tests are unaffected. Return type: glyph+fg only (NOT the full RenderedCell) — the engine keeps computing occupant bg via backgroundAt() so a game can't override it and desync from the terrain tint. Keep it Rogue-agnostic.
acceptance_criteria: MapPanel exposes an occupant render seam that can remap/suppress a perceived occupant's glyph+fg at render time; defaults to current behavior (existing tests unaffected); bg remains engine-computed; rogue-1st can be implemented through it in the port.
close_reason: Added occupantRenderer seam to MapPanel + RenderedGlyph/OccupantRender types. Perceived occupants route through a game-supplied callback that can remap glyph/fg or return null to suppress; default preserves current behavior. Background stays engine-computed (RenderedGlyph carries no bg) so a remapped glyph can't desync from terrain tint. Unblocks rogue-1st (hallucination).

title: MapPanel: occupant-render seam (symmetric to rememberedRenderer) + remembered-occupant support
description:
MapPanel has a render seam and a memory store for TERRAIN but neither for OCCUPANTS, an asymmetry the Rogue port keeps hitting. Terrain: last-seen persistence via fogFor -> Grid<Boolean> per zone, and game-owned look via the rememberedRenderer(Tile) seam (krogue-f84). Occupants: none — drawOccupants() hardcodes renderable.glyph and drops any entity the observer doesn't currently perceive (if entity.id != observer.id && !perceived.sees(entity.id) continue). So a game cannot (a) keep an out-of-view occupant drawn at its last-seen cell, nor (b) transform an occupant's glyph/color at render time.

Two Rogue parity beads sit squarely in that gap and are the second+third consumers that justify promoting this into the engine (the promote-on-second-consumer threshold, same as krogue-f84 did for terrain):
  - rogue-blv (item memory): Rogue keeps a floor item/gold glyph drawn at its last-seen cell after you leave the room (leave_room's switch clears FLOOR/monsters but lets an item glyph fall through) — the occupant analogue of terrain fog.
  - rogue-1st (hallucination visuals): visuals() rerolls every VISIBLE monster to a random A-Z and every visible object to a random glyph each turn — the occupant analogue of rememberedRenderer (a render-time glyph transform).

Without this seam both must be done as game-side overlay Widgets that re-derive MapPanel's private camera-origin math (revealItems already copy-pastes it) and re-read perceived/fog — throwaway duplication that silently drifts if MapPanel internals change.
design:
Engine owns the MECHANISM, game owns the POLICY — the exact line rememberedRenderer already draws for terrain. Add a narrow occupantRenderer seam to MapPanel, symmetric to rememberedRenderer: a game-supplied callback invoked in the occupant pass that returns how (or whether) to draw an occupant cell, given at least { entity/renderable, perceived?: Boolean, remembered?: Boolean, tile, computed bg }. Return null = don't draw. This lets the game: draw a remembered occupant (perceived=false but the game deems it remembered) — for rogue-blv; and remap a perceived occupant's glyph/color per turn — for rogue-1st.

Open design questions to resolve in this bead:
  1. Remembered-occupant iteration: drawOccupants currently only visits perceived (or self) entities. Remembered items need the loop to also visit unperceived floor entities in-zone (or the engine exposes an entity set + last-seen store the game maintains). Decide whether the engine stores last-seen occupant glyph/pos (like fog) or just calls the seam for every in-zone occupant and lets the game gate on its own memory. Prefer the latter (engine stays policy-free; do NOT bake Rogue's 'cell holds last glyph' memory model into the engine — that over-fits).
  2. Layering: remembered occupants must draw UNDER live perceived occupants; in practice they only differ in unperceived cells, so gating remembered draws to !perceived cells keeps it automatic.
  3. Camera reuse: consider also exposing the camera/viewport origin (MapPanel computes originX/originY privately; revealItems and any overlay re-derive it). A tiny shared MapCamera helper would de-duplicate that regardless of the seam. Could be folded in here or split to its own bead.

Keep the seam minimal and Rogue-agnostic; the memory policy and hallucination rules stay in the korogue-rogue port.
acceptance_criteria: MapPanel exposes an occupantRenderer seam (defaulting to today's behavior so existing games are unchanged) that lets a game: (1) draw an occupant at its last-seen cell while unperceived (remembered occupants), and (2) transform a perceived occupant's glyph/color at render time; the seam is game-agnostic (no Rogue memory model baked in); rogue-blv and rogue-1st can be implemented in the port through it with no camera-origin duplication; existing MapPanel tests/behavior unaffected by the default.
close_reason: Split into krogue-a01 (render-time occupant transform, cheap/now), krogue-ho4 (camera-origin dedup, now, de-risks the rest), and krogue-7tx (remembered-occupant iteration, deferred; may be unnecessary if a game-side overlay + camera helper suffices). Bundling a cheap safe transform with a risky iteration change and an orthogonal camera-dedup made the original too coarse to schedule.

title: MapPanel: make remembered (fog) tile rendering configurable per game
description:
MapPanel hardcodes how previously-seen-but-not-currently-perceived (fogged) terrain is rendered: it multiplies the tile's foreground color by a fixed PREVIOUSLY_VIEWED_DIM_FACTOR (0.35) and adds a fixed PREVIOUSLY_VIEWED_BLUE_BOOST (0.10), on a black background. These are private consts in MapPanel's companion object, so a game can't tune the look of remembered terrain without patching the engine.

Games should be able to control remembered-tile appearance. Motivating case: korogue-rogue wanted the remembered areas a touch brighter, which today requires editing an engine const that affects every game.

Expose this as configuration so a game can, at minimum, set the dim factor and blue boost, and ideally supply a full remembered-cell rendering strategy (e.g. a (Tile) -> Rendered function, or a small RememberedStyle holding dim factor / tint color / background) so a game could render remembered tiles in a different hue entirely rather than just a dimmed version of the lit color.
design:
Options, least→most flexible:
A) Constructor params on MapPanel: dimFactor: Double = 0.35, blueBoost: Float = 0.10f (+ maybe rememberedBackground: Color = BLACK). Smallest change, keeps current tint math. Backward compatible via defaults.
B) A RememberedStyle value type (dimFactor, tintColor, background) passed to MapPanel; the current dim+blue-boost becomes the default instance. Groups the knobs, room to grow.
C) A pluggable strategy: rememberedRenderer: (Tile) -> Rendered? passed to MapPanel, defaulting to today's dim-blue behavior. Maximum flexibility — a game can recolor remembered tiles arbitrarily (different glyph/hue), not just dim them.

Recommend shipping A now (unblocks the Rogue brightness tweak cleanly) with the field grouped so B/C can layer on later. Keep the existing default values so current visuals are unchanged unless a game opts in.
acceptance_criteria: MapPanel exposes the remembered-tile dim factor (and blue boost / background) as configuration with defaults matching current behavior; korogue-rogue can set its own brightness without patching engine consts; no visual change for games that don't opt in.
close_reason: Option C: pluggable rememberedRenderer (Tile)->RenderedCell? seam on MapPanel (matches fogFor/observer idiom), public RenderedCell result type, default reproduces the exact dim+blue look, plus dimmedRememberedRenderer(dimFactor,blueBoost,background) factory for the brightness-tweak case. Games can recolor remembered terrain arbitrarily or suppress it (null). Tests: default unchanged, full recolor, null-suppression. Suite + ktlint green.

title: Event-animation queue: presentation-side sequences for game events (projectile arc, hit-flash)
description:
Third time concept from ADR-0023, distinct from the two axes it makes invariant: transient VISUAL sequences bound to game events — a thrown potion's arc, a bolt's flight, a hit-flash, a death fade, floating damage numbers. Unlike ambient animation (flicker/shimmer), these are triggered BY game events and have a definite start/end; unlike the game-time actor scheduler (krogue-5z8), they are presentation-only and must never affect or be saved with game state.

Model: a presentation-side animation queue the render/UI layer owns. Game systems, when resolving an action, emit a lightweight visual-event (e.g. Projectile(from,to), Hit(entity), Death(entity)) that the presentation layer turns into a wall-clock-timed sequence; the loop drains the queue before showing the next game step and MAY briefly gate input while a sequence plays (so the player sees the bolt land before acting again). Ambient animation keeps running underneath on wall-clock.

Open questions: where visual-events live (transient ECS components consumed by a presentation system vs an event-bus channel); whether sequences block the game clock (they should not — game state already resolved; they only gate presentation/input); interruptibility/skippable (instant-play on keypress); interaction with the scheduler-driven loop (krogue-5z8) so several actors' events in one clock-step animate in a sensible order. Depends conceptually on nothing in 5z8 but shares the wall-clock presentation axis; can land independently.
acceptance_criteria: A game action can emit a visual-event that the presentation layer plays as a wall-clock sequence (e.g. a projectile animating from source to target) before the next step is shown; game state is unaffected and identical across a save/load taken mid-animation; ambient animation continues during and after; input can skip/fast-forward a sequence.
notes: Post-close review (fresh-context agent, 2026-07-13): no critical bugs, core logic/invariants verified correct. Fixed the cheap findings: added CombatSystemTest assertions for the new position/glyph/color snapshot fields (previously untested), added a MapPanelTest case for the decorate hook (previously untested), added EventAnimationQueue.clear() wired into MyGame.load() so a mid-animation save/load doesn't leave a stale sequence resolving against the new zone's camera. Filed krogue-c0j for the one substantive gap found: isPlaying gates input even for off-screen/unperceived sequences that draw nothing, causing an unexplained freeze (and, separately, a visibility leak since putAt does no fog check). Binary-compat note for korogue-rogue: the GameEvents changes are source-additive but not binary-compatible (constructor signature changed) -- recompile downstream against the new :engine rather than hot-swapping the jar. Full test suite (67 total incl. 10 new) + ktlint green.
close_reason: Core event-animation queue delivered: presentation-only, wall-clock sequencer with real hit-flash/death-fade triggers, input skip/fast-forward, camera-aware rendering, and save/load isolation. Follow-ups filed for the Projectile trigger (krogue-4tn) and grid-snapped render mode (krogue-tnf, pre-existing).

title: Time-cost turn scheduling (energy model): actor scheduler on the game-time axis
description:
Optional third turn policy (sibling to RealTimeLoop/TurnBasedLoop) implementing the classic energy/action-cost model: actions cost ticks, a game-time clock advances to the next due actor, that actor acts and is recharged by its action's cost. Design sketched in ADR-0023. Reuses the daemon Scheduler (same clock), the intent->system pattern, and the GameLoop seam; ships OFF by default so every-turn games are unaffected (ADR-0014 swap). Key new discipline: split action systems (Behavior/Movement/Combat/Pickup/Portal, game-time, per actor-step) from derived systems (Lighting/Perception, presentation-time, per frame).

Sketch scope: Actor(nextActTime, speed) component; per-action base-tick cost table + per-item swingTicks; a SchedulerDrivenLoop step loop that jumps the clock to min nextActTime, fires due daemons, yields to input when the player is due, else acts + reschedules; an Acting/Acted marker path so BehaviorSystem/action systems run for a single entity and report cost; deterministic tie-break by entity id; serialize nextActTime + clock.

Related: the game-time vs presentation-time (wall-clock animation) axis separation is documented as an invariant in ADR-0023 — ambient animation (flicker/shimmer) stays on wall-clock in the renderer, orthogonal to this scheduler; event-animations (projectile arcs, hit-flash) are a future presentation-side queue, not part of this.
design: See docs/adr/0023-time-cost-turn-scheduling-and-time-axes.md (Proposed). Open decisions: speed representation (cost/speed scaling vs energy accumulation — sketch picks scaling); cost source (table vs component-carried, likely both); interruptible multi-tick actions (v1 uninterruptible); derived-system cadence (per-frame recompute); whether Actor turn-state lives on the component (yes) with a heap as later optimization.
acceptance_criteria: A game can select the scheduler-driven loop; actors with different speeds act at different frequencies; a high-cost action (armor swap) keeps its actor out of play for its full cost while faster actors act repeatedly; player input commits an action that advances the clock by its cost; game state is deterministic and round-trips through save/load; existing every-turn demos unaffected (policy off by default).

title: Per-mode terrain passability (fly over lava, swim) via MovementTags
description: Generalize Zone.isWalkable (walk-only boolean) to per-locomotion-mode terrain passability using the MovementTags set-relation introduced in krogue-x9q. A cell declares which movement modes it blocks; a mover passes iff it has a mode the cell doesn't block (M-subset-of-blocks => blocked), the same rule x9q applies to entity occupants. Enables lava passable to flyers, water to swimmers, chasms, etc. Touches the Zone/terrain data model (korogue terrain is glyph-only today), so it is larger than the entity-occupancy fix and deferred to its own slice. Engine MovementSystem should call a Zone.isPassable(x,y,moverModes) that defaults to today's isWalkable (walk) when a cell declares no mode data. Builds on x9q's MovementTags/Locomotion/Collision.
acceptance_criteria: Zone exposes per-mode passability keyed on MovementTags; MovementSystem uses moverModes for terrain too; a flyer crosses a cell that blocks {walk} but not {fly}; existing walk-only zones unchanged (isWalkable == blocks {walk}).
close_reason: Per-mode terrain passability via Tile.blocks + Zone.isPassable(x,y,moverModes), same MovementTags set-relation as entity Collision (ADR-0022). isWalkable == blocks {walk} (walk special-case); walk-only zones unchanged (blocks derives from isWalkable). MovementSystem uses moverModes for terrain; flyer crosses {walk}-blocking water. Tests + ktlint green.

title: Sim zones: cross-zone HuntPlayer targeting policy (opt-in pursuit across transitions)
description: Knob 2 (ADR-0021): a SEPARATE, opt-in AI targeting policy letting a monster in an adjacent (simulated) zone pursue the player across the boundary — pathing toward the Portal that leads to the player's zone and crossing it, instead of freezing at the threshold. Default stays same-zone-only (perception is zone-scoped, ADR-0015), so a far monster is unaware unless a consumer opts in. Sane default targeting = pursue the exit/portal toward the player's zone, NOT omniscient tracking of the player's exact cell (a consumer may supply omniscient if desired — engine is not the limit).
design: ADR-0021 Knob 2. Depends on the adjacency provider (to know the player's zone is a neighbor and pick the connecting portal) and atomic crossing (to follow through). Independent of simulation scope in code (composed at runtime): the monster's zone must be simulated for it to act, which CurrentPlusAdjacent provides.
acceptance_criteria: With the opt-in policy + CurrentPlusAdjacent, a monster in an adjacent zone paths to the connecting portal and crosses to continue the chase; the default (no policy) leaves targeting same-zone-only; headless test: player in zone A, monster in adjacent zone B, tick, assert it advances toward the portal and crosses.
close_reason: CrossZoneHuntPlayerStrategy + HuntPlayer same-zone gate implemented (Opus), reviewed, committed. BehaviorSystemTest 13/13 incl. end-to-end chase-across-transition; full suite green.

title: Sim zones: atomic boundary-crossing movement (any entity, ZoneMember+Position together)
description: Mechanic B (ADR-0021): PortalSystem currently transitions only the player (world.set(player, ZoneMember(targetZoneId))). Generalize crossing so ANY entity that steps onto a Portal (or is moved across a boundary) updates ZoneMember AND Position TOGETHER, atomically — a GameWorld.relocate(entity, zoneId, x, y)-style helper. Required so a chasing monster can actually follow the player through a portal. Independent of the other pieces.
design: ADR-0021 Mechanic B. Generalize PortalSystem beyond the player; ensure no half-updated state (never a ZoneMember change without the matching Position). Pure/headless-testable.
acceptance_criteria: A non-player entity crossing a portal lands in the target zone at the target cell with ZoneMember and Position updated together; no half-updated state; unit-tested.
close_reason: Implemented by Sonnet agents in isolated worktrees, reviewed, cherry-picked to mainline (de04377c ZoneAdjacency, 320f292b relocate/PortalSystem). ZoneAdjacencyTest 5/5, PortalSystemTest 5/5, GameWorldTest 7/7, full suite green. s67.3 also caught+fixed a portal self-relocation bug.

title: Sim zones: simulatedZones as a pluggable policy (CurrentZoneOnly default + CurrentPlusAdjacent)
description: Knob 1 (ADR-0021): generalize GameWorld.simulatedZones from an open fun into a consumer-supplied policy () -> Set<String>, re-evaluated LIVE each tick (systems already call world::simulatedZones). Ship CurrentZoneOnly (default, = today) and CurrentPlusAdjacent (current + neighborsOf(current)); a consumer may return ANY set incl. all zones (no engine cap). The set changes as currentZoneId changes (transitions recompute adjacency); de-simulated zones freeze with state intact and resume when re-simulated (entities persist, ADR-0007).
design: ADR-0021 Knob 1. Depends on the adjacency provider for the CurrentPlusAdjacent built-in. Keep CurrentZoneOnly as the default so existing behavior/tests are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: simulatedZones is a swappable policy; CurrentZoneOnly default preserves current behavior; CurrentPlusAdjacent = current + portal-neighbors and recomputes on zone transition; an arbitrary consumer-supplied set is honored; headless-tested.
close_reason: SimulatedZonePolicy seam + CurrentZoneOnly (default, behavior-preserving) + CurrentPlusAdjacent implemented (Sonnet), reviewed, committed. SimulatedZonePolicyTest 4/4, full suite green.

title: Sim zones: zone-adjacency provider (neighborsOf, portal-derived, overridable)
description: A neighborsOf(zoneId): Set<String> provider giving a zone's adjacent zones (ADR-0021 Mechanic A). Default derived from Portal components: the distinct Portal.targetZoneId among a zone's portal cells. Overridable so a non-portal adjacency (e.g. an overworld grid) supplies its own. N-hop is composable (repeated application) — the engine hardcodes no distance. Foundation for CurrentPlusAdjacent (scope policy) and cross-zone targeting.
design: ADR-0021. Pure/headless. Reads Portal (targetZoneId) across a zone's cells; keep it cheap (it may be evaluated per tick by the live scope policy) — cache per current-zone if needed.
acceptance_criteria: neighborsOf(zone) returns the distinct target zones of that zone's portals; a consumer can override the provider; pure and unit-tested.
close_reason: Implemented by Sonnet agents in isolated worktrees, reviewed, cherry-picked to mainline (de04377c ZoneAdjacency, 320f292b relocate/PortalSystem). ZoneAdjacencyTest 5/5, PortalSystemTest 5/5, GameWorldTest 7/7, full suite green. s67.3 also caught+fixed a portal self-relocation bug.

title: engine/kotile: graphical (pixel-space) UI layer for graphical tile games
description: A reusable UI layer that positions widgets in PIXEL space (not snapped to the tile grid), for GRAPHICAL tile games. Built on the free/overlay render primitive from krogue-tk9 (pixel-space drawSprite + Layer + back-to-front compositing) — a second consumer of that primitive, NOT a parallel render path. Persistent and input-aware, unlike tk9's transient, expiring effects. Enables smooth/free-positioned graphical UI: panels, health bars between rows, tooltips at the exact cursor pixel, sliding/animated elements. Motivated by making the korogue-rogue example optionally graphical (see rogue-jk6 graphical tileset in the korogue-rogue repo). Distinct from — and does NOT replace — the existing grid/text UI toolkit (Menu/Dialog/PagedTextList/TextOverlay/HotkeyMenu), which draws cell-aligned to a tile surface and stays the right choice for ASCII/text UI.
design: From the kotile layer-model discussion. One pixel-space primitive (drawSprite) + Layer interface + painter's-order compositing (krogue-tk9); effects (tk9) and this UI layer are both free-layer consumers, differing in lifetime + input handling, not in how they render. Grid/text UI stays on the tile surface. Needs pixel-space input hit-testing for free-positioned widgets (grid UI uses GridLayout.tileAt; free UI needs its own pixel-space hit-testing). GL-visual — verify with a display (Linux/xvfb), not headless on mac. Do NOT build this until tk9's primitive exists; defer any dedicated UI-layer class until there is a concrete graphical-UI need.
acceptance_criteria: Free-positioned UI widgets render above the grid at arbitrary pixel positions with correct layering and pixel-space input hit-testing; the grid/text UI toolkit is unaffected; implemented as a consumer of tk9's free-layer primitive (no parallel render path).
notes: Design rationale + layer model in docs/adr/0018-layer-model-grid-and-free-layers.md. Second consumer of the free-layer primitive from krogue-tk9 (which must land first).
close_reason: engine/kotile: free (pixel-space) UI layer — UiLayer + Widget + PixelRect on drawSprite; GridLayout.contentPixelAt + KotileInputProcessor pixel-pointer events; second free-layer consumer per ADR-0018. Tests (logic + GL-gated) green; :kotile:demo:uiHarness proves input→hit-test→render.

title: kotile: wrap GridLayout in a libGDX Viewport for HiDPI correctness + hard-clip
description:
Introduce a thin custom libGDX Viewport subclass that CONSUMES the existing pure ScalePolicy/GridLayout (does NOT replace them) to set world size + screen bounds. Motivation is correctness, not perf (projection mechanism does not affect frame cost):

1. HiDPI/retina reconciliation (PRIMARY): KotileCanvas currently mixes Gdx.graphics logical points with the backbuffer pixel size. On retina/mixed-DPI/fractional-scaling displays these differ (e.g. 800x400 window -> 1600x800 backbuffer, per RenderHarness). A Viewport + HdpiUtils.glViewport reconciles logical-vs-backbuffer pixels; today the mismatch is latent and only "works" at clean integer ratios.

2. Hard-clip letterbox: viewport.apply() sets glViewport so overflow/partial-tile bleed is cleanly cut and bars are guaranteed empty. This SUPERSEDES krogue-vuv.

3. Unified unproject (minor; GridLayout.tileAt already covers pixel->tile).

Keep the pure ScalePolicy/GridLayout module (unit-testable without GL) as the brain feeding the Viewport. Keep a y-UP camera with the flip in drawTile; do NOT switch to a y-down world (avoids texture-V orientation risk).

Files: kotile/library/src/main/kotlin/com/sletmoe/kotile/display/KotileCanvas.kt (owns camera/batch/resize/drawTile), rendering/GridLayout.kt + ScalePolicy.kt (pure math, keep as-is). Verify on a real retina display — this is the GL-visual work deferred from krogue-n64.
design: From ADR-0017. This is the deliberate, correctly-framed version of 'adopt libGDX Viewport': a wrapper over GridLayout, justified by HiDPI + hard-clip, NOT a rewrite of the scaling logic. Absorbs the hard-clip scope of krogue-vuv.
acceptance_criteria: On a retina/HiDPI display the grid renders at correct pixel dimensions with no logical-vs-backbuffer mismatch; fixed-grid overflow and letterbox bars are hard-clipped; pure GridLayout tests unchanged; no texture-orientation regression.
notes: VALIDATED on real 2x retina (logical->backbuffer confirmed). Added parameterized fixed-grid snapshot harness: kotile/demo/src/main/kotlin/FixedGridHarness.kt + :kotile:demo:fixedGridHarness gradle task (knobs: winW/winH/cols/rows/policy). Three snapshot cases pass on this box: (1) win850x430 grid40x20 integer -> onscreen 20px (2x), offset 25x15, backbuffer 1700x860: ring centered, equal clean dark-blue letterbox bars all 4 sides, no bleed, crisp; (2) win800x400 grid100x60 integer -> scale1, offset -100x-100: overflow ring/corners cleanly hard-clipped, window shows interior only, no garble; (3) win850x430 grid40x20 fit -> onscreen 21.25px fractional, offset 0x2.5: fills width, clean thin top/bottom letterbox bars with no partial-tile bleed (uneven ring spacing is inherent FitScale, not a clip bug). Corners upright = no texture-orientation regression. Reflow #2 already confirmed 1600x800 crisp earlier. Acceptance met: retina correct pixel dims, overflow+letterbox hard-clipped, GridLayout tests unchanged, no V-flip regression. Remaining: full suite + demos compile green; changes UNCOMMITTED.
close_reason: Implemented GridViewport (libGDX Viewport consuming GridLayout) + HdpiUtils.glViewport hard-clip; validated on real 2x retina via new fixedGridHarness snapshots (scaling, centering, overflow+letterbox hard-clip, no V-flip regression). Full suite + ktlint green.

title: kotile: dirty-region redraw (skip full-grid repaint each frame)
description: Both TileRenderer and AsciiTileWindow repaint the entire grid every frame (top-most cell of every cell, all layers). For a mostly-static roguelike view this is wasted CPU/GPU work each frame. Track dirty cells (writes since last render) and only re-emit changed cells, or cache the composited frame and redraw on change. This is the real rendering-perf ceiling identified during the krogue-n64 codesign; projection mechanism (GridLayout vs libGDX Viewport) does not affect it. Consider interactions with animated tiles (AnimatedAsciiTile / AnimatedSpriteTile), which are dirty every frame their frame advances, and with viewport scrolling (a viewport-origin change dirties everything).
design: From ADR-0017 discussion. Full-repaint is fine functionally; this is an optimization. Design must handle: per-cell dirty tracking vs whole-frame cache; animated cells that self-dirty on a clock; viewport scroll invalidation; and the SpriteBatch begin/end model. Keep the public draw API unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A static frame issues no per-cell draw work after the first paint (or a documented minimal amount); animated and scrolled frames still update correctly; no visual regressions.
close_reason: Implemented as a whole-frame composite cache (GridCompositeCache): TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow recomposite into an offscreen FrameBuffer only when dirty (writes, resize, or any animated tile present), then blit it as one sprite through the existing scaled/sharp-bilinear-aware canvas.drawSprite path. Scoped to the internal-tilemap render()/asLayer() path only; the external-tilemap render(source, viewport) overload (shared/multi-pane tilemaps) is out of scope, documented in ADR-0024. Verified via new GL-gated unit tests plus a live demo pixel-diff (:demo:animationShowcaseHarness) against pre-change output, which caught and fixed two real bugs invisible to isolated single-canvas tests: GL viewport clobbering by FrameBuffer.end(), and FrameBuffer color-texture defaulting to linear (not nearest) filtering. Full design/tradeoffs in docs/adr/0024-dirty-region-redraw-grid-composite-cache.md.

title: kotile: mipmaps + linear min-filter on tile sheets for clean downscaling
description: When native tiles are larger than the on-screen tile size (big tiles -> small window, or FitScale < 1x), nearest-neighbor minification drops pixels and shimmers. Generate mipmaps on TileSheet/font textures and use a mip/linear min-filter so the downscale direction stays clean, regardless of ScalePolicy. Called out as day-one in the krogue-n64 codesign but split out because it is GL-visual and best verified with a context.
design: Implemented: TileSheet uploads a mipmap chain + trilinear (MipMapLinearLinear) min-filter by default; mag stays Nearest so upscaling/1x is unchanged. Threaded useMipMaps (default true) through TileSheet + Font; opt-out available. 1x1 ascii bg texture left default (always magnified). POT padding (macOS NPOT fix) makes mipmaps safe. Verified by eye on Linux (fixedGridHarness downscale before/after) + TileSheetFilterTest (GL-gated) + full suite green. See ADR-0017, docs/STATUS.md.
acceptance_criteria: Downscaled tiles show no aliasing shimmer; upscaling behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Closed

title: kotile: FitScale filtering (sharp-bilinear) for smooth fractional scaling
description: FitScale (from krogue-n64) computes a fractional scale + centering, but tiles are still drawn with the default nearest-neighbor filter, so fractional sizes give uneven/shimmery glyph strokes. Implement sharp-bilinear (integer-upscale then bilinear-downscale, the emulator trick) via a small shader or 2-pass, wired to the FitScale path, so fractional fill looks crisp. Best done where a GL context is available to eyeball the result (the pixel-level integration tests are skipped without DISPLAY).
design: From ADR-0017. IntegerScale ships crisp (integer+nearest). FitScale's placement math and ScalePolicy seam exist; only the smoothing filter is outstanding.
acceptance_criteria: A FitScale grid at a non-integer factor renders glyphs without visible stroke-width shimmer.
notes: INTEGRATION POINT (important): ScalePolicy as shipped is only fun scale(...): Float — the scale-FACTOR knob. Filtering is a SEPARATE, orthogonal knob with NO existing seam. This work does NOT add a ScalePolicy impl; it adds filtering infra (shader or 2-pass FBO) plus a way to know FitScale/fractional is active. Touch: KotileCanvas.kt (SpriteBatch/shader + drawTile), texture filter setup on the font glyph atlas + background texture in AsciiTileWindow.kt and TileSheet.kt. Nearest is fine for IntegerScale; only fractional needs this.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: kyle@sletmoe.com
comments.text:
Implemented sharp-bilinear as a fragment shader (SharpBilinear.kt) bound on KotileCanvas's SpriteBatch, active only when the fixed-grid scale is non-integer (FitScale). Because every drawTile — glyph AND sprite tile — flows through the one batch, the smoothing covers BOTH layers (the requested sprite coverage), not just glyphs. While active the canvas switches the bound texture to a Linear mag filter (per-texture u_textureSize uniform; restored to Nearest in end()); integer/reflow scales are untouched (default shader + nearest, pixel-perfect). Kept distinct from the FBO supersample path (krogue-1zo).

Verified: GL-gated pixel tests in RenderingIntegrationTest — a red/blue checkerboard sprite at 2.75x blends (max min(r,b)=0.50) vs 0.0 crisp at 2x integer (this is the SPRITE-coverage proof), plus a fractional glyph smoke test. Eyeballed :kotile:demo:fixedGridHarness -Ppolicy=fit at 2.25x: glyphs smooth, no shimmer/corruption. Full suite green. Note: original acceptance criterion was glyph-only; sprite coverage now proven by test. docs/STATUS.md updated.

title: Scale policy: supersample-to-FBO then downsample (crisp fractional)
description: An alternative fractional ScalePolicy that renders the tile grid at a large integer tile size into an offscreen framebuffer (FBO), then draws that FBO to the window at the exact fractional scale with linear filtering. Produces the sharpest fractional result and covers BOTH glyph and sprite tile layers (unlike SDF). Tradeoff: FBO plumbing, extra VRAM, an extra full-screen pass. Deferred alternative to FitScale's sharp-bilinear approach chosen in krogue-n64; implement against the ScalePolicy interface n64 introduces.
design: From the krogue-n64 codesign. Day-one FitScale uses the sharp-bilinear (integer-upscale then bilinear-downscale) trick, which is cheaper and shader/2-pass-light. Full supersample+FBO is parked as a higher-quality/higher-cost option if sharp-bilinear proves insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: Fractional scaling looks sharp for both glyph and sprite layers; VRAM and frame-time overhead documented; opt-in policy, not default.
notes: ADR-0036 TIER 2 (resolution-independent PIXEL crispness). Canvas render-target mode in KotileCanvas (NOT a ScalePolicy, NOT a GlyphSource): render the whole grid to an FBO at a large integer tile size, then downsample to the window at exact fractional scale in LINEAR/gamma-correct space (the key cheap lesson from Brogue's downscaleTile). Covers glyphs AND sprite tiles, reuses today's fonts/sheets, keeps the CP437 pixel look. Does NOT reproduce Brogue's smooth-glyph aesthetic (that's tier 3 / krogue-9x7.2) — a bitmap source has no high-res detail to recover. Independent of tier 3; land atop krogue-3eu (HiDPI). Verify on real pixels/retina.

title: Scale policy: pre-rendered multi-size bitmap font asset swap
description: A scaling strategy that bundles several bitmap font sizes (e.g. 10x10, 12x12, 20x20) and picks the nearest at-or-above the target on-screen tile size, then scales minimally (ideally integer) from that source. Minimizes blur because we always scale from a close source size — best quality-per-complexity for bitmap fonts. Glyph-layer only; primarily asset management rather than render logic. Natural home to build on krogue-kotile-font12 (12x12 CP437 font bundling). Deferred alternative to the day-one IntegerScale/FitScale policies from krogue-n64.
design: From the krogue-n64 display-scaling codesign. Complements IntegerScale/FitScale by reducing the source-to-target scale ratio via nearest-size asset selection. Depends conceptually on having multiple bundled font sizes available.
acceptance_criteria: Renderer selects the nearest available font size for the current scale and scales minimally from it; falls back gracefully when only one size is bundled.
notes: INTEGRATION POINT: asset + selection logic, not a ScalePolicy impl. Touch: Fonts.kt (bundle/load multiple CP437 sizes; today it exposes cp437_10x10()), and the font-selection point feeding AsciiTileWindow's canvas (pick nearest size >= on-screen tile size from canvas.layout, then let IntegerScale finish). Builds on krogue-kotile-font12 for the 12x12 asset. Glyph layer only.
close_reason: Superseded per ADR-0036. Multi-size bitmap swap still scales from a bitmap (never arbitrary-scale crisp), adds asset-management + shipped bytes, and is dominated by tier 2 (krogue-1zo, true resolution-independent pixels) and tier 3 (krogue-9x7.2, Brogue-fidelity smooth glyphs). If tier 2 is ever too costly on a device, one extra bundled size + IntegerScale is a trivial fallback needing no dedicated feature.

title: UI toolkit: centered full-window text overlay
description: The new PagedTextList is top-aligned and box-bounded; the toolkit has no primitive for a full-window message screen that clears the field and paints its lines centered (vertically, and ideally optionally horizontally) — the classic game-over / splash / pause / 'you have won' screen. The Rogue example reimplements this privately as PlayScreen.EndOverlay (fills the surface blank, computes a top offset = (height - lines.size)/2, draws each line). Add a generic centered full-window text overlay to com.sletmoe.korogue.ui so any game gets this without re-rolling the centering + clear.
design: Keep the engine generic: the widget owns only layout (clear-to-bg, vertical centering, width/line truncation, optional horizontal centering) and colors — the content (List<String>) is entirely caller-supplied. No Rogue text. Display-only by default (non-interactive); dismissal is the host's concern (Rogue's shell exits on next key), but consider an optional onDismiss key like PagedTextList for reuse. Downstream adoption: korogue-rogue PlayScreen.EndOverlay (showEnd) would be deleted in favor of this.
notes: Surfaced while implementing rogue-sdh.14. Companion to the letter-keyed menu bead (krogue-f8m). Distinct from PagedTextList (top-aligned, bordered, paginated) — this is full-window and centered.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI toolkit: letter-keyed (hotkey) selection menu
description: The engine's Menu widget only supports arrow-key + Enter highlight navigation. It lacks the classic roguelike idiom of a menu whose rows each carry a hotkey letter that selects the row directly ('wield what? a) mace  b) bow ...'). The Rogue example currently reimplements this privately as PlayScreen.Chooser (a List<Pair<Char,String>> drawn one row each, a key in a..z selecting the matching row, unmatched keys ignored). Add a generic hotkey-menu widget to com.sletmoe.korogue.ui so any game can prompt 'pick an item by its letter' without re-rolling it.
design: Keep the engine generic, matching krogue-s3c's pattern: all representation caller-injected. Rows are (key: Char, label: String) pairs (or a small Item type); an onPick(Char) callback fires on a matching keypress; non-matching keys return false (so a host Dialog/modal can swallow or pass them). Caller supplies fg/bg/colors. No Rogue-specific text baked in. Consider whether this is a variant of/extension to the existing Menu or a sibling widget. Downstream adoption: korogue-rogue PlayScreen.Chooser (promptItem) and its Chooser private class would be deleted in favor of this.
notes: Surfaced while implementing rogue-sdh.14 (engine pager adoption). Generic counterpart to the existing arrow-key Menu.kt. Companion to a centered full-window text overlay bead filed alongside this.
close_reason: Closed

title: UI toolkit: paginated text list (--Press space to continue--)
description:
The engine's overlay text widgets (Dialog + TextList, used for Rogue's 'i' inventory and 'D' discoveries) show their rows in a single fixed-height box and silently truncate any rows past the box height (TextList.draw does rows.take(surface.height)). Rogue's original listing (things.c add_line) instead paginates: when a page fills it shows a '--Press space to continue--' prompt and waits for space before the next page.

Add a scrolling/paginated variant of the read-only text list to the UI toolkit (com.sletmoe.korogue.ui) so long listings (a near-fully-identified discoveries screen, a large pack) are fully viewable. Likely a reusable widget (e.g. PagedTextList) that the existing overlay Dialogs can opt into, with space/PageDown to advance and a footer prompt; Escape still closes via the Dialog.

Surfaced while porting Rogue's 'D' discoveries screen (korogue-rogue rogue-sdh.8): the listing is correct but can overflow the box. This is a toolkit-wide concern shared with the inventory overlay, not specific to discoveries.
notes: Redesigned per review (keep engine generic): engine ships a headless generic Paginator<T> (Paginator.kt) — pure page math, no libGDX/rendering/input. PagedTextList.kt is now a thin default renderer over it with ALL representation caller-injected: footer text via a (Paginator)->String? lambda, fg/bg colors, advance/back key sets. No Rogue-specific prompt string baked into the engine. Consumers wanting full control drive Paginator directly. Tests: PaginatorTest, PagedTextListTest. Rogue's '--Press space to continue--' look is supplied by the downstream consumer (korogue-rogue rogue-sdh.14).
close_reason: Added PagedTextList widget to com.sletmoe.korogue.ui (PagedTextList.kt + test). Paginates long read-only listings: fills each page, draws a '--Press space to continue--' footer when rows overflow the box, Space/PageDown advance, PageUp steps back, advancing past the last page invokes onDismiss; single page with no prompt when rows fit. Faithful to rogue5.4.4 things.c add_line. Downstream adoption is korogue-rogue rogue-sdh.14.

title: UI: TextInput single-line text-entry widget (get_str)
description: Add a single-line text-entry Widget to the UI toolkit (ADR-0011) — the toolkit's counterpart to a curses get_str prompt. Accumulates typed characters, draws them with a trailing caret, Enter submits, Backspace deletes; unmapped keys fall through so an enclosing modal swallows them. Maps libGDX key codes to characters directly (lowercase letters, digits, space, hyphen, apostrophe) so it is headlessly testable with no live Gdx.input dependency. Consumed by the Rogue example's 'c' (call) command to nickname an unidentified item kind.
close_reason: Implemented TextInput widget + tests; consumed by korogue-rogue 'c' call command.

title: kotile: dynamic window resize + display scaling (fullscreen centering, tile sizing)
description: Handle dynamic window sizes and resizing. On resize/fullscreen the tile display should stay centered (letterboxed) instead of stretching or anchoring to a corner. Explore tile-size strategies: support larger tiles for big/fullscreen windows; possibly render at a large tile size and downsample for smaller windows, or choose an integer/scale factor from the window dimensions. Needs a resize handler + viewport/centering logic in kotile, decoupled from the fixed-grid assumptions in the current renderer.
design:
CODESIGN (in progress).

RESIZE MODEL — support BOTH, engine stays generic. Keep the existing fitToWindow switch:
- fitToWindow=true  => reflow: tile pixel size constant, visible tile count changes (see more map). ~ libGDX ScreenViewport.
- fitToWindow=false => fixed logical grid (e.g. 80x24), scaled to fill preserving aspect, centered/letterboxed. ~ libGDX FitViewport. This is the path that needs the new centering+scaling; today its docstrings claim letterboxing that isn't implemented (grid just anchors top-left).

SCALING — expose a pluggable ScalePolicy interface. Ship TWO impls day one:
1. IntegerScale (DEFAULT): integer factor floor(min(winW/gridW, winH/gridH)) + nearest-neighbor. Crisp/pixel-perfect; ideal for CP437 + the Rogue example.
2. FitScale: fractional factor (preserve aspect) + sharp-bilinear (integer-upscale then bilinear-downscale, the emulator trick) for crisp fractional fill.
Enable mipmaps on tile sheets day one so the DOWNSCALE direction (big native tiles -> small window) stays clean regardless of policy.

Two orthogonal knobs behind the policies: scale-factor policy (integer vs fractional) and filtering (nearest / bilinear / sharp-bilinear / mip). Best strategy differs by direction: upscale favors integer+nearest; downscale favors mip/linear.

DEFERRED alternatives filed as follow-ups (depend on the ScalePolicy interface this issue introduces): krogue-19k (SDF/MSDF fonts), krogue-yfs (multi-size font asset swap, ties to krogue-kotile-font12), krogue-1zo (supersample+FBO downsample).

OPEN QUESTION — vehicle: adopt libGDX Viewport (FitViewport/ScreenViewport) in KotileCanvas to get letterboxing + unproject/pixelToTile-under-scale for free (implies renaming the existing TileViewport scroll-origin type to avoid the name clash), vs hand-roll the content-rect (offset + scaled tile size) and update pixelToTile manually. Also: centering/scaling belongs at the KotileCanvas level so BOTH TileRenderer and AsciiTileWindow benefit (they currently duplicate resize logic).
notes: IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-30), decisions recorded in ADR-0017. Vehicle resolved: did NOT adopt libGDX Viewport (built-ins can't do IntegerScale; a custom subclass needs a y-down camera = texture-orientation risk unverifiable without a GL context). Instead: pure GL-free ScalePolicy + GridLayout (forReflow/forFixedGrid), owned by KotileCanvas, offset+scale baked into drawTile; TileViewport NOT renamed (gdx Viewport never entered kotile's API). Input: GridLayout.tileAt + new KotileInputProcessor(layout) ctor, wired in engine Game.kt; old 4-lambda ctor and pixelToTile kept for korogue-rogue compat. Tests: GridLayoutTest (15) + 2 InputProcessor cases, all green; full ./gradlew test green. REMAINING (split out, GL-visual): krogue-m2x FitScale sharp-bilinear filtering, krogue-4ni mipmaps, krogue-vuv hard-clip. IntegerScale (default) is complete and crisp; FitScale is structurally wired but visually rough until krogue-m2x.
close_reason: Core shipped + on mainline (ADR-0017): ScalePolicy + GridLayout resize/centering/letterboxing owned by KotileCanvas, IntegerScale default complete + crisp, layout-aware input. Opus-reviewed, no blockers, full suite green. Remaining polish/alternatives are separately tracked follow-ups (m2x FitScale filtering, 4ni mipmaps, 3eu Viewport/HiDPI, 19k/yfs/1zo scale-policy alts).

title: kotile: effects layer for free-moving overlays (projectiles that don't snap to tiles)
description: Add an effects/overlay layer to kotile that renders above the tile grid and is NOT snapped to tile cells, so projectiles, beams, particles, and animations can fly across the screen at sub-tile/pixel resolution and interpolate smoothly between cells. Needs: a render pass on top of the tile surface using float (pixel) positions, and an API to spawn/update/expire transient effects (position, sprite/glyph, lifetime, velocity/path). Distinct from the grid-locked tile rendering.
design:
LAYER MODEL (from design discussion): kotile is already pixel-space underneath — drawTile(cell) is sugar over a pixel-space draw. So this bead establishes the REUSABLE free-layer primitive, not just an effects feature:
1. A pixel-space draw on KotileCanvas: drawSprite(pxX: Float, pxY: Float, region, tint, w, h) — the one new primitive. drawTile becomes sugar over it.
2. A Layer interface (render(canvas), maybe update(dtMs)) + back-to-front (painter's-order) compositing at the screen level, so grid layers and free layers overlay just by draw order in the shared SpriteBatch — no blend/composite machinery needed.
3. The EFFECTS layer (particles/projectiles/beams: transient items with pos/velocity/lifetime) is the FIRST consumer of the primitive.
The graphical UI layer (krogue-<new>) is the SECOND consumer and depends on this. Keep it simple: one primitive + draw-order, several consumers.
notes: Layer model recorded in docs/adr/0018-layer-model-grid-and-free-layers.md. This bead owns the shared free-layer primitive (drawSprite + Layer interface + painter's-order compositing); effects are its first consumer. Graphical UI layer krogue-tvm is the second consumer and depends on it.
close_reason: Implemented across 3 commits: drawSprite primitive + Layer/LayerStack (134d659c), effects layer (dfc6f7b4). Grid renderers gain asLayer(); EffectsLayer is the first free-layer consumer. Verified with headless-GL pixel tests + effectsHarness snapshot; full suite green.

title: kotile: alpha channel for tiles (foreground glyphs over background tiles)
description:
For non-ASCII (graphical/sprite) tilesets, support an alpha channel so a foreground tile — a character/monster/item sprite — can be drawn over a background terrain tile, with transparent pixels showing the tile beneath.

Scope is the SPRITE path only. The ASCII path already supports this: AsciiTileDescriptor carries foregroundColor + backgroundColor, and AsciiTileWindow.renderGrid draws a background fill (tinted backgroundColor) then the glyph on top (foregroundColor); a Color.CLEAR background already lets a glyph overlay whatever is underneath. The gap is the sprite renderer (SpriteTileRenderer + StaticTile/AnimatedSpriteTile), where a cell renders as a single opaque tile with no foreground-over-background layering or alpha blending.

Need: per-cell layering on the sprite path (background terrain tile + foreground entity sprite) with alpha blending, and an API for stacking layers per cell. Pairs with the graphical tileset renderer work (rogue-jk6, in the korogue-rogue repo).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: kyle@sletmoe.com
comments.text: Mipmap interaction (from krogue-4ni): TileSheet now generates mipmaps + a trilinear min-filter by default, so background/foreground graphical tiles both downscale cleanly through the sprite path (the ascii 1x1 bg quad is the only surface excluded, and it's irrelevant here). WATCH FOR: when alpha-keyed tiles are packed adjacently in a sheet and downscaled hard, coarse mip levels average a tile's edge with its neighbor's color/alpha -> faint halos/bleed around transparent edges. Mitigation: use TileSheet 'spacing'/padding (margin/spacing already supported) on any sheet meant to be shrunk aggressively, or pass useMipMaps=false for that sheet. Verify the alpha-layering result at a downscale by eye when this lands.

comments.author: kyle@sletmoe.com
comments.text: Implemented: sprite TileRenderer now composites a cell's z-layers bottom-up (new LayeredTilemap.layersBottomUp) instead of drawing only topCellAt, so a foreground entity sprite on a higher z alpha-blends over a background terrain tile and its transparent pixels reveal the terrain beneath. TileSheet keyColor/alpha + SpriteBatch's default blend supply the transparency; no new tile type needed — the existing drawTile(x,y,z,...) API is the 'stack layers per cell' surface. ASCII path left winner-takes-all by design (two overprinted glyphs would be messy). Verified: 2 headless GL pixel tests (transparent fg reveals bg / opaque fg occludes bg) + LayeredTilemap ordering test; :demo:spriteHarness bottom row shows red-diamond sprites over green terrain at a downscale (terrain shows through transparent corners). Full suite green. Docs/STATUS.md updated.

title: Magical darkness vs darkvision: distinguish from ordinary unlit (lighting↔perception)
description: Close the one remaining divergence from the engine 5e-default perception bar (ADR-0015): magical darkness should block Sight AND Darkvision while TrueSight pierces it. Today magical darkness is just unlit (lightMap null) and DarkvisionSense ignores lighting (requireLit=false), so darkvision penetrates it — an effect that should hard-counter darkvision does nothing. DESIGN IS DECIDED (ADR-0020): model magical darkness as a REGION (environmental) CONCEALMENT on the perception layer, reusing the existing tag + pierces machinery — NOT a lighting value, and no sense special-cases it.
design:
Per docs/adr/0020-magical-darkness-region-concealment.md (supersedes ADR-0015's illumination-layer approach). Implement:
1. A per-cell concealment layer on Zone, analogous to lightMap: a Grid<Set<String>> of concealment TAGS per cell (empty = none). A magical-darkness region sets {visual} (PerceptionTags.VISUAL). Derived/effect-driven state — produced like LightEmitter+LightingSystem (a darkness emitter component + system) or by generation; the per-cell layer is the engine seam, the source can be minimal.
2. A region-concealment step in StandardPerception: unlike target Concealment (gates ENTITIES only), region concealment gates CELLS (and entities on them). A sense reveals a magically-dark cell only if it pierces the cell's tags — pierces applies here exactly as for target concealment.
Result with tag={visual} and NO sense changes: Sight blocked, Darkvision NOW blocked (closes the gap), TrueSight pierces {visual} -> sees. Non-visual senses (tremorsense/telepathy) unaffected. Third suppress mechanism alongside observer Suppressor (gates senses, not pierceable) and target Concealment (gates entities, pierceable). Fully headless-testable. Known refinement (non-blocking, documented in ADR): TrueSightSense conflates truesight+see-invisible so see-invisible also pierces here — split the sense + use a dedicated tag if a game needs them distinct.
acceptance_criteria: A magical-darkness region blocks Sight AND Darkvision (its cells and entities on them are not perceived) but is pierced by TrueSight; ordinary unlit cells (no region concealment) still let Darkvision through; tremorsense/telepathy still detect creatures in it. Headless perception tests. Zone gains a per-cell concealment-tag layer; StandardPerception gates cells by it honoring pierces.
notes: Surfaced 2026-06-13 reviewing perception (krogue-1my) against D&D 5e as the genre default bar. The truesight/blindness and see-invisible behaviour already match 5e; this is the one remaining behavioural divergence. Telepathy naming was reviewed and kept (Brogue/NetHack call the same detect-monsters-through-walls sense 'telepathy'; only tabletop 5e narrows the term to communication).
close_reason: Implemented per ADR-0020: Zone per-cell concealment layer + StandardPerception region-concealment step. Darkvision now blocked by magical darkness, TrueSight pierces, non-visual senses unaffected. StandardPerceptionTest 14/14 incl. real-sense acceptance; full suite green.

description: `./gradlew ktlintCheck` fails on HEAD (since commit 58ef942, krogue-1my.1/.2), independent of krogue-1my.4.
