title: Room-based visibility model (Rogue lit/dark rooms)
description: Rogue's true visibility is room-based: the room you're in is fully revealed if lit, otherwise only your immediate surroundings; corridors show adjacent cells; you never see through walls into unentered rooms. The engine currently offers SymmetricShadowCaster (LOS) and Omniscient (everything). Neither is Rogue-faithful for a multi-room dungeon (shadowcast over-reveals down corridors/through doors; omniscient sees everything). Build a room-aware visibility model once level generation provides room metadata. Depends on [deleted:krogue-c20]. The Rogue example scaffold approximates with uncapped SymmetricShadowCaster for now.
design:
DECISION (2026-07-02): implement as a ROGUE-SPECIFIC PerceptionModel (a RoomBasedPerception), NOT a generic engine model. Rationale: the reveal rules (lit room whole / dark room immediate surroundings / corridors adjacent-only / never see into unentered rooms) are Rogue-idiosyncratic policy, and the data it needs (RoomInfo: membership, dark/ISDARK flag, r_exit doors) is Rogue-specific and already lives in korogue-rogue. The engine provides the seam; using it is the extensibility ethos (ADR-0014), not a shortcoming. Generalize to an engine model only on a second consumer (rule of three), using the Rogue impl as the reference.

CONFIRMED — no engine change needed: PerceptionModel.perceive(observer: Entity, world: GameWorld) already passes the full GameWorld, so a Rogue model can read the LevelRooms/RoomInfo component and apply room policy. The interface KDoc already names this exact case ('a RoomBasedPerception for Rogue's lit/dark rooms ... without touching the engine'). Register RogueRoomPerception via korogue-rogue's GameModule perception-model registry.

SPLIT: engine owns the mechanisms (FOV/shadowcast, light map, Perceived buffer, the PerceptionModel seam); the Rogue model owns only the room-reveal POLICY, composing those + RoomInfo.

PREREQUISITE MET: the 'once level generation provides room metadata' gate (old [deleted:krogue-c20]) is satisfied — korogue-rogue's LevelGenerator + RoomInfo/LevelRooms already carry room membership, the dark flag, and door cells.

LIGHTING INTERPLAY: korogue-rogue currently runs LightingSystem at ambientLight=FULLBRIGHT (krogue-0vg), which masks dark rooms — everything reads as lit. A faithful model needs dark rooms actually dark; the room model + this lighting change go together, and relate to krogue-dta (magical darkness vs darkvision).

HOME: this is Rogue-example work and belongs in the korogue-rogue tracker (per the repo separation — korogue tracks engine/kotile only). Recommend migrating this bead to korogue-rogue; no residual engine task remains.
close_reason: Migrated to korogue-rogue rogue-phf. Rogue-specific work (a RoomBasedPerception via the game's GameModule) with no residual engine task — the engine PerceptionModel seam already suffices.

title: Inventory side panel
description: Bordered side panel listing inventory items (placeholder model for the demo until a real item/inventory system exists). Uses Frame + the scrollable-list logic from LogPanel.
close_reason: Inventory landed with a minimal real item model: Item(name)+Inventory(items) serializable components (registered), PickupSystem (walk onto a non-blocking item -> despawn + add to inventory + ItemPickedUp event), and InventoryPanel widget. Demo: items scattered per zone, sidebar stacks Log over Inventory, pickups logged, round-trips through save/load (verified in-game). 9 tests (286 total). UI epic 6/6.

title: Compact terrain serialization (save files are ~13MB)
description: The demo's save is ~13MB: zones are 200x200 (40k cells each, x2 = 80k tiles), and SaveCodec serializes each cell's full Tile (name string, two colors, booleans) with no interning/RLE — e.g. 'stone wall' written ~34k times per zone (~168 bytes/tile). Walls count as tiles even though randomWalkCave only carves ~6k floors. Options: (1) intern tile prototypes into a per-zone palette + store per-cell index, and/or RLE the row-major grid; (2) revisit demo zone size. Functionally fine today; this is a size/perf follow-up to the 4f save codec.
close_reason: Closed

title: Persist fog-of-war memory across save/load
description: ZoneFog (krogue-ro8) keeps per-zone 'previously seen' memory in-session only; it is not written to save files, so a loaded game starts unexplored. Persist fog per zone in the save model/codec (SaveModel + SaveCodec, ADR-0009) so explored areas survive save/load. Decide whether fog belongs in Zone state or a separate per-zone player-knowledge section of the envelope.
close_reason: Fog persists across save/load: added SaveData.fog (per-zone SavedFog, additive/default-empty so old payloads still load — no version bump per ADR-0009), carried by SaveCodec as Map<String,Grid<Boolean>> (codec stays decoupled from the renderer); ZoneFog.snapshot()/restore() bridge it. 4 new tests (codec round-trip + additive default; ZoneFog snapshot/restore), 238 total. Capability is wired+tested but the demo doesn't yet trigger save/load.

title: Per-zone fog-of-war memory (renderer rebuilt on zone change)
description: 4e rebuilds KotileZoneRenderer on a zone switch, so previouslyVisible (fog dimming) resets — revisiting a zone re-explores it. Persist per-zone visibility (e.g. keep a renderer/fog grid per zone, or move fog state into the zone/ECS) so explored areas stay remembered across transitions.
close_reason: Per-zone fog memory persists across zone transitions: hoisted the 'previously seen' Grid out of KotileZoneRenderer into a host-owned ZoneFog (one grid per zone, reused on return) and inject it into the renderer, so the rebuild on a zone change no longer wipes exploration. 3 ZoneFog tests (234 total). Save/load persistence of fog filed as krogue-k77.

title: Optional: simulate adjacent zones (chase across transitions)
description: Extend ADR-0008 active-only simulation so cross-zone behaviour (a monster chasing the player across a transition) is possible — kept GENERIC per the driving use case: a consumer picks WHICH zones are simulated; the engine imposes no limit (simulate all 50 if you want to pay for it), and a far-away monster is unaware of the player BY DEFAULT but a consumer can opt into broader awareness. DESIGN DECIDED (ADR-0021): two orthogonal knobs, not one. The simulatedZones seam already exists (GameWorld.simulatedZones(): Set<String>, default {currentZoneId}; systems iterate it live).
design: Decomposed into 4 sub-beads per docs/adr/0021-simulation-scope-and-cross-zone-awareness.md: two orthogonal knobs (simulation scope, cross-zone awareness) + two enabling mechanics (adjacency, atomic crossing). Foundations: adjacency provider + atomic crossing (independent). Then the scope policy (uses adjacency) and the cross-zone targeting policy (uses adjacency + crossing). Rogue stays on CurrentZoneOnly. All headless-testable. Epic acceptance: with CurrentPlusAdjacent + the opt-in cross-zone targeting policy, a monster in an adjacent zone chases the player across a transition; defaults leave far monsters unaware and only the current zone simulated.
acceptance_criteria: simulatedZones is a swappable policy with CurrentZoneOnly (default) + CurrentPlusAdjacent built-ins and accepts any consumer set; adjacency derives from portals and is overridable; a cross-zone HuntPlayer targeting policy (opt-in) makes a monster in an adjacent simulated zone path to the portal and cross it (ZoneMember+Position updated atomically) to continue pursuit, while the default leaves far monsters unaware; a de-simulated zone's entities freeze with state intact and resume when re-simulated. Headless tests (player zone A, monster adjacent zone B, tick, assert advance+cross).
close_reason: All 4 sub-beads done + on mainline (ADR-0021): adjacency provider, atomic crossing, simulatedZones policy (CurrentZoneOnly default + CurrentPlusAdjacent), cross-zone HuntPlayer targeting. Epic acceptance proven by the end-to-end chase test (monster in an adjacent zone paths to the portal and crosses to keep chasing). Defaults leave far monsters unaware + only the current zone simulated; Rogue unaffected.

title: Player death + HP feedback (no game-over yet)
description: Discovered during 4b-s5 testing: the player takes combat damage (Health drops by 20 on a zombie bump) but there is no HP display and no death/game-over handling -- the player is excluded from dead-removal, so reaching 0 HP does nothing. Pre-existing gap, outside the 4b ECS-migration steps. Needs: surface player HP, and decide behavior at 0 HP (game-over / restart). Likely after Phase 4b; relates to krogue-ui-layout for any HUD.
close_reason: Resolved by the UI toolkit: HP is surfaced via a live BarWidget (krogue-bhc) and 0 HP now triggers a modal game-over Dialog (Load last save / Quit) that freezes the world (krogue-wh9). CombatSystem still spares the player from despawn; death is handled at the UI/host layer rather than by removing the entity.

title: kotile: minor demo/adapter polish flagged by CodeRabbit (per-frame alloc, empty no-op blocks)
description: Trivial pre-existing cleanups CodeRabbit surfaced on PR #19 (krogue-4lt), left out of that mechanical ktlint PR: (1) kotile/demo UiHarness button widget allocates a new TextureRegion every render (~line 63) — construct once and reuse in drawSprite; (2) kotile/library KotileInputAdapter no-op overrides (~line 45) trip detekt's EmptyFunctionBlock — use '= Unit' expression bodies or suppress at the adapter level. Note: detekt is not currently wired into the build; this is CodeRabbit's own detekt run. Low priority polish.
close_reason: UiHarness.ButtonWidget now builds its TextureRegion once (field) instead of per render; KotileInputAdapter no-op overrides use '= Unit' expression bodies (silences detekt EmptyFunctionBlock).

title: kotile: ViewportDirtyTracker's per-render poll could cost more than it saves on large/high-churn viewports
description:
ViewportDirtyTracker (krogue-c0q, ADR-0024) polls every visible cell's LayeredTilemap.versionAt each render(source, viewport) call, since a shared/external tilemap can't push dirty notifications to an unbounded number of observers. For a typical roguelike grid (80x24 to ~100x40) this is a few thousand cheap int comparisons -- negligible next to a GPU draw call. But if a consumer uses this overload on a much larger scrolling viewport (tens of thousands of visible cells) that also changes on most frames, the poll cost plus the full redraw cost is strictly worse than the pre-krogue-c0q behavior (which just redrew everything with no bookkeeping at all) -- a real, if narrow, case where this caching could net-lose rather than win.

Not a proven regression -- this is asymptotic reasoning, not a measured benchmark; no profiling has been done on this path at any real scale. Only worth acting on if a consumer actually hits this: a scrolling world large enough and changing fast enough to make the O(visible cells) poll's cost exceed the GPU savings from skipping unchanged cells' draws.

Possible mitigations if it ever bites: a size/change-frequency heuristic that falls back to always-redraw (skipping the poll+cache machinery entirely) above some visible-cell-count or churn-rate threshold; or exposing a way for a consumer to opt out of the cache for this overload when they know their scene will always be fully dirty anyway.

title: kotile: free layers (EffectsLayer/UiLayer) have no dirty-tracking; persistent static content redraws every frame
description:
GridCompositeCache (ADR-0024/krogue-drk, refined in krogue-oxi) only caches TileRenderer/AsciiTileWindow's grid-addressed content: it works by glScissor-ing to a fixed, tile-aligned rectangle per cell, so it fundamentally can't apply to ADR-0018's free (pixel-space) layers -- EffectsLayer and UiLayer content lives at arbitrary float positions with no cell to mark dirty. Confirmed: LayerStack/EffectsLayer/UiLayer have zero dirty/cache concept and unconditionally redraw every active effect / visible widget on every render() call, entirely unaffected by (and untouched by) the composite cache work.

This is a non-issue for genuinely transient content (particles, projectiles, a moving cursor) -- that's usually changing every frame it's on screen anyway, which is also exactly when needsContinuousRedraw() keeps krogue-4ul's outer frame-skip from applying, so there was never much to cache there.

It IS a real gap for persistent, static, off-grid content: krogue-tvm's UiLayer already exists and lets a graphical tile game build panels/health bars/tooltips positioned in pixel space purely for sub-tile placement, not because they change often. Such widgets currently redraw in full every single frame the app renders at all, with no way to skip the ones that haven't changed.

Fixing this would need a different technique than GridCompositeCache -- dirty RECTANGLES with arbitrary bounding boxes (e.g. track each widget/effect's last-drawn bounds, and only recomposite the union of old+new bounds when something moves/changes), not tile-scissored cells. Not worth building speculatively; revisit once a real graphical UI (built on krogue-tvm's UiLayer) has enough static/persistent content that this becomes an actual measured perf cost.

title: kotile: per-cell (not whole-frame) dirty tracking for GridCompositeCache
description: krogue-drk's GridCompositeCache (ADR-0024) is a whole-frame cache: any single write, or the presence of ANY animated tile, forces a full recomposite of the entire grid every render() call. This is a deliberate, coarser first cut chosen for lower implementation risk (see ADR-0024's 'Alternatives considered') -- a renderer that ever hosts one animated tile (e.g. a single flickering torch on an otherwise-static map) permanently pays full-grid recomposite cost every frame that tile animates, even though only its own cell actually changed. A follow-up could track per-cell dirty state (e.g. a version-per-position Grid<Int> on LayeredTilemap, or precise increment/decrement bookkeeping of which cells currently hold animated content) to redraw only the cells that actually changed each frame. Only worth doing if the coarse whole-frame cache proves to be an actual perf bottleneck in a real scene with mostly-static content plus a few animated tiles.
close_reason: Implemented: GridCompositeCache now tracks dirty cells individually (markCellDirty/markAllDirty) instead of one whole-frame flag, with two recomposite paths -- fully-dirty (one clear + batched pass, same cost as before) and partially-dirty (per-cell glScissor + clear + draw + immediate batch flush, so untouched cells keep their existing FBO pixels). The sticky 'any animated tile marks everything forever' flag is replaced by a HashSet<Vector2Int> of animated positions, recomputed from ground truth on every single-cell write (refreshAnimatedTrackingAt) rather than incrementally counted, so it can't drift. clearLayer now scans for cells actually populated on that layer before clearing and only marks those, not the whole grid. render(source, viewport) remains out of scope (krogue-c0q). Verified via a new differential technique: two windows/renderers draw the same final content (one via first-paint-then-partial-update exercising the scissored path, the other built directly in one shot as a trusted whole-grid reference) via temporary demo harnesses, diffed pixel-for-pixel -- both the ASCII (single-layer-wins) and sprite (bottom-up multi-layer) paths came back pixel-identical, including a moved sprite and a cleared cell. Full writeup appended to docs/adr/0024-dirty-region-redraw-grid-composite-cache.md's Update section (kept in one ADR per user direction rather than filing a separate one).

title: iOS target: launcher module for the demo (libGDX RoboVM backend)
description:
libGDX targets iOS via RoboVM, an AOT compiler that turns JVM bytecode -> native ARM. Because it works on bytecode (not Java source), Kotlin/JVM works too — this is NOT Kotlin/Native or KMP; it AOT-compiles the same kotlin(jvm) bytecode the project already produces. So iOS is additive: :engine and :kotile:library stay backend-agnostic (as with the Android target), and iOS is a new launcher module (IOSLauncher extends IOSApplication) binding gdx-backend-robovm.

FIRST STEP — de-risk before committing: RoboVM historically lags on newer bytecode/JDK/reflection metadata, and this repo is on Kotlin 2.3.21 (very recent). Spike RoboVM against Kotlin 2.3 bytecode before building out the module; this compatibility is the most likely blocker.

Scope (after spike passes):
- New iOS application module applying RoboVM Gradle plugin.
- gdx-backend-robovm + gdx-platform iOS natives.
- IOSLauncher initialize()ing the demo's existing ApplicationListener.
- robovm.xml with forceLinkClasses for anything loaded reflectively — watch kotlinx.serialization and Kotlin reflection/coroutines.
- Info.plist, iOS SDK config.

Caveats:
- Requires a Mac + Xcode; device deploy needs an Apple Developer account (signing).
- RoboVM is community-maintained (post-shutdown libGDX fork) — expect some toolchain lag.
- Input: demo is keyboard-driven; iOS needs touch/on-screen input (gameplay-UX work).

Companion to krogue-mvm (Android target). Not urgent — build on concrete demand.
acceptance_criteria: A RoboVM spike confirms Kotlin 2.3.21 bytecode AOT-compiles under the pinned libGDX RoboVM version (or documents the blocker); given that, an iOS module builds an app launching the existing demo ApplicationListener on simulator/device; :engine and :kotile:library remain backend-agnostic; desktop demo still runs.

title: Android target: launcher module for the demo (libGDX android backend)
description:
libGDX supports Android as a first-class backend, and the codebase is already positioned for it: :engine and :kotile:library depend only on gdx core (backend-agnostic) — only :demo and :kotile:demo bind gdx-backend-lwjgl3. Adding Android is additive: a new application module, not an engine/kotile refactor.

Scope:
- New Android application module (e.g. :demo-android) applying the Android Gradle plugin.
- Swap desktop backend for gdx-backend-android + per-ABI gdx-platform natives (armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86, x86_64).
- AndroidLauncher (extends AndroidApplication) that initialize()s the demo's existing ApplicationListener.
- AndroidManifest.xml, android{} SDK config, local Android SDK (ANDROID_HOME).

Open questions / caveats:
- Input: demo is keyboard-driven; Android needs touch / on-screen input (gameplay-UX work, not just build plumbing).
- JDK API level: verify engine uses no desktop-only JDK APIs beyond Android's supported set.
- Decide minSdk/compileSdk targets.

Not urgent — build on concrete demand.
acceptance_criteria: A :demo-android module builds an APK that launches the existing demo ApplicationListener on an Android device/emulator; :engine and :kotile:library remain backend-agnostic (unchanged); existing desktop demo still runs.

title: Perception: concealment channel-vs-identity (distinguish see-invisible from truesight)
description: The tag+pierce perception model (ADR-0015) pierces the MATCHED tag, so it cannot distinguish two concealments that block the same channel. Invisible and magical darkness (ADR-0020) both conceal from {visual}, so any sense piercing {visual} (the single TrueSightSense) sees through BOTH — meaning see-invisible and truesight cannot be told apart, and see-invisible incorrectly pierces magical darkness (a minor 5e divergence). NOTE: splitting TrueSightSense into two senses does NOT fix this — both would still be tags={visual}, pierces={visual} and pierce all {visual} concealment. The real fix is a model refinement: separate a concealment's CHANNEL (which visual senses it blocks, matched against sense.tags) from its IDENTITY (what must be pierced to defeat it), and check pierces against the identity. E.g. Invisible: channel {visual}, identity 'invisibility'; magical darkness: channel {visual}, identity 'magical-darkness'; see-invisible pierces {invisibility}; truesight pierces {invisibility, magical-darkness}. Backward compatible if identity defaults to the channel tag. Only a game modelling BOTH magical darkness AND wanting see-invisible distinct from truesight needs it — a narrow case; build on concrete demand (rule of three). Until then a game can swap the whole PerceptionModel (ADR-0014). May never be needed.
design: Touches the Concealment/Suppressor interfaces (add an identity distinct from concealsFromTags/negatesTags) and StandardPerception's pierce check (Sense.isConcealedBy + the new region-concealment gate). Keep it tag-based/no matrix and backward-compatible (identity defaults to the channel tag). Relates to ADR-0015, ADR-0020, krogue-dta.
acceptance_criteria: A concealment can declare a channel + an identity; see-invisible pierces invisibility but NOT magical darkness while truesight pierces both; all existing perception tests still pass with identity defaulting to the channel tag.

title: kotile: hard-clip fixed-grid overflow (glViewport/scissor letterbox)
description: Display scaling (krogue-n64) letterboxes softly: leftover window space is the clear color and nothing hard-clips the content rect. When a fixed grid is larger than the window at 1x (IntegerScale floor), tiles overflow the intended content rectangle instead of being clipped. Add a hard clip to the GridLayout content rect via glViewport or GL scissor in KotileCanvas.begin()/end() so overflow (and any future partial-tile bleed) is cleanly cut and letterbox bars are guaranteed empty. Was deliberately deferred from n64 to avoid a y-down-camera texture-orientation change that can't be verified without a GL context.
design: From ADR-0017. KotileCanvas keeps a y-up ortho projection + manual flip; a scissor rect (bottom-left origin framebuffer px) computed from canvas.layout can clip without touching the camera/projection, avoiding texture-V risk. Must set/restore GL_SCISSOR_TEST around the batch and play nicely with the headless FBO test path.
acceptance_criteria: A fixed grid larger than the window at 1x does not draw outside its content rect; letterbox bars stay at the clear color; existing render tests unaffected.

title: Scale policy: SDF/MSDF distance-field font rendering
description: A ScalePolicy (or font-pipeline) option that renders glyphs from signed/multi-channel distance fields so text stays crisp at any fractional scale via a shader, instead of relying on integer scaling or sharp-bilinear. libGDX ships DistanceFieldFont support. Tradeoffs: glyph-layer only (does NOT cover arbitrary sprite tiles), requires SDF-generated font assets, and softens the hard-pixel CP437 aesthetic. Deferred alternative to the day-one IntegerScale/FitScale policies from krogue-n64; implement against the ScalePolicy interface that n64 introduces.
design: Considered during the krogue-n64 display-scaling codesign. Day-one policies are IntegerScale (integer+nearest, default) and FitScale (fractional+sharp-bilinear). SDF is a resolution-independent alternative for the glyph layer only; parked because it changes the font asset pipeline and doesn't help sprite tiles.
acceptance_criteria: Glyphs render crisply at arbitrary fractional scale without blur; sprite-tile path unaffected; opt-in, not default.
notes: ADR-0036 TIER 3 ALTERNATIVE glyph source (behind the GlyphSource seam krogue-9x7.1), NOT the primary Brogue route. SDF is glyph-only and softens hard pixels, so its home is smoothly-scaled UI/menu TEXT — not the play-field font. Primary tier-3 route is gdx-freetype TTF-at-size (krogue-9x7.2). libGDX DistanceFieldFont is the reference. Build after the freetype source unless a specific UI-text need arises first.

title: engine: sound effects + music support
description: Add audio to the engine (eventually). Sound effects tied to game events plus background music, likely via libGDX audio. Define an audio seam/API (play one-shot sfx, loop/crossfade music, per-channel volume, mute) so games/examples can wire events to sounds without depending on a concrete backend. Backlog — no current consumer.
